title: Stop R and Python language servers answering requests after they stop
description:
Fixes #16155

### Why this change

The R and Python language server wrappers register Positron providers when their client starts: statement range, input boundary, help topic, and (R only) the `ark:` virtual document provider. Before the change in this PR, these registrations stayed even after the client stopped. They went away only at the next activation, or when the session was disposed.

Positron asks the newest provider first, so as a result, a stopped client would be asked before a live console client. The review of #16153 found this for a Quarto session that was shut down; its statement range and help providers were asked first, and each one failed with a dead connection.

In #16153 I added a liveness check to the statement range and help topic providers, so a stale provider does now decline. However, that check is a patch on each provider, not a fix of the lifecycle, and `RInputBoundaryProvider` cannot use the check (#16152). Quarto reads a nullish answer from it as "these boundaries are malformed" and runs the whole range, so a stale input boundary provider can still answer with a dead client.

This PR fixes the lifecycle, or at least improves it in this area. When a client stops, the providers that it registered and the Quarto cell claim of its session go away with it.

### What changes

`extensions/positron-r/src/lsp.ts` and `extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/lsp.ts` get the same change.

- A new `stopServing()` helper disposes the registrations of the current activation and releases the Quarto cell claim of the session. The two go together. If the providers go but the claim stays, the console declines those cells and nothing answers.
- The client state listener calls `stopServing()` when the client reaches `Stopped`. This is the main fix. The session layer calls `deactivate()` only when the wrapper is `Running`. When a client stops on its own (the Quarto session exits, the kernel exits, or the server crashes), `deactivate()` does not run. A fix only in `deactivate()`, as the issue proposed, does not cover this case.
- `deactivate()` also calls `stopServing()` at its start, so the console answers for the full stop window. It calls it again after the wait for initialization. That second call is for `dispose()` while the client is still starting.
- The client state listener moves out of `activationDisposables` into its own field. It must see a `Stopped` event that arrives after the 2 s timeout in `deactivate()`. The next `activate()` disposes it first. The listener also uses its own client, so a late event from an old client cannot change the next activation.

The liveness checks from #16153 sticks around too, just in case.

### Behavior changes to know about

- A console session in the background now holds no registrations. When it comes to the foreground again, `activate()` registers everything again. The providers of the foreground session already answered first, so users see no change from this.
- (R) The `ark:` content provider now goes away at each deactivation. When no R client runs at all, a reopened `ark:` editor cannot resolve. Before, it showed "Error: This document does not exist". When an R client runs, nothing changes.

### Limitations

This PR improves the lifecycle but there are still some subtle issues/problems/limitations:

- One path is very tricky to test manually and has no automated test: a session that is deleted while its language server is still starting. It is the only path that reaches the second `stopServing()` call in `deactivate()`.
- The Python side has no automated tests. The new tests are for R only, in `lsp.unit.test.ts`. The Python code has the same shape, and I tested it by hand.
- If `dispose()` runs while the client of a Quarto session is still starting, the session claims its cells for a short time and then releases them. The claim makes the console clear its diagnostics for those cells, and they come back at the next edit. `main` makes the same claim on this path, and holds it longer.
- The R tests need some stuff on `ArkLsp` to get exposed to be tested: `activationDisposableCount` and `stopClientForTesting()`. Both are public, and their docs say that they are for tests only. If you prefer, I can remove them and keep only the manual tests.
- Out of scope, found during review (we could open followup issues, if we think these are important):
  - (R and Python) The session `dispose()` runs outside the LSP queue. A queued activation can start a new client on a disposed session. This change makes the leak temporary, but does not remove it.
  - (Python) `PythonSession.dispose()` waits on `_lsp.dispose()` with no timeout. If the language server does not stop, the kernel is not disposed.
  - (R) While a Quarto R session runs, its `ark:` provider answers before the provider of the console.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- When an R or Python language server stops, for example after a Quarto session shuts down, Positron no longer asks it for statement ranges, input boundaries, or help. The console session answers instead (#16155).

### Validation Steps

@:console @:quarto @:sessions @:help @:ark @:pyrefly

Manual tests, in R and in Python:

1. Open a `.qmd` and run a chunk, so the document gets its own session. Stop that session, and keep the document open. In a chunk, press <kbd>Cmd+Enter</kbd> and <kbd>F1</kbd>, then run the chunk. The console session must answer.
2. Restart a console session. Make sure that statement range and help work after the restart.
3. Start two console sessions and switch between them. The foreground session must answer.
4. Open a `.ipynb` and start its kernel. The notebook session must answer for its cells.
5. (R) Run `View(lm)` to open an `ark:` editor. Switch to another session and back. The content must still show.
6. Start a session for an untitled `.qmd`, then save it to a file. Statement range and help must work in the saved file.

title: Show folder creation errors in New Folder from Template and New Folder from Git
description: Addresses the first part of #16252 ### Summary _New Folder from Template..._ and _New Folder from Git..._ fill in a default location for the new folder. When a workspace is open, this default is the parent of the workspace folder. On Workbench and Cloud, this parent is often a folder that the user cannot write to, for example `/cloud`. If the user accepted that default, the template flow failed silently, and the Git flow showed an error only after the dialog closed. With this PR, both dialogs find this problem before the user moves on: - When the user enters or browses to a location, the dialog checks if the user can create a folder there. - If the user cannot, the dialog shows "You don't have permission to create a folder in this location." under the location field. - The button that moves on is disabled until the location changes. This is Next or Create in the template flow, and OK in the Git flow. Enter does not get past a disabled button. This PR does not change the default location, which I think would be a bad call. I'll do another PR for #16252 to add settings for the default (`git.defaultCloneDirectory` and `files.dialog.defaultPath`). On Workbench, the default can still be a folder that the user cannot write to but at least the user sees why and can pick another location. ### Why this approach This change ended up larger than I thought it was going to be. Most of the lines of code and complexity comes from trying to get the renderer to know if the user can create a folder in a location. The notes below explain the decisions, so that you can review the code against them and see if you've got any other thoughts. **The check runs in the extension host.** The renderer cannot answer this question by itself: - A file stat reports only the write bit of the folder owner. A root-owned `/cloud` with mode 755 looks writable to every user. - `IFileService` has no access check. To add one, we must change upstream files. The extension host runs where the files are, as the user who owns the session. So the little mini `positron-file-transfer` extension now registers an internal command that calls `fs.access(folder, W_OK | X_OK)`. Creating an entry in a folder needs the search (execute) bit as well as the write bit. Positron already uses `W_OK` in this way in the unsaved-scripts code of the R and Python extensions. **The command works in remote windows.** In Remote SSH, dev containers, and Workbench, the extension runs in the remote extension host. The server starts that host with `--transformURIs`, so the renderer's `vscode-remote:` URIs arrive as `file:` URIs (see `createURITransformer`). I tested this with a dev build of Positron Server. **A folder that does not exist yet gets its answer from the nearest existing folder above it.** `git clone` creates missing parent folders, so this is the folder that the new folders go into. The template flow reports a missing location first, with its own check. **If the command cannot answer, the check passes.** This can happen if the extension is not active, or if the path goes through a file. Then the real folder creation reports any error. Because of this fallback, a different command ID on one side can turn off the check without an error. A guard test, `extensions/canCreateFolderCommand.vitest.ts`, makes sure that the renderer and the extension use the same ID and that the activation event matches. **Why `positron-file-transfer`.** The extension is about files, is small, starts in every build, and runs only in Node. I also looked at `positron-supervisor`, but that one is about kernels and seemed like a less good fit. **Alternatives that I tried out but decided against:** - Create the folder and then delete it, as a test. This has side effects: a file watcher sees a temporary folder, and the folder stays if the delete fails. Also I did not find this pattern being used anywhere in VS Code or Positron. - Check only when the user presses OK or Next, and keep the button enabled. In testing, a second press showed the same error again, and it looked like the button did nothing. - In the template flow, create the folder at the last step and go back to the location step if creation fails. This jumping back and forth was confusing, and it came after the user made every other choice. ### Known limitations - The check runs only when the location changes. If the user changes permissions outside Positron while the dialog is open, the user must select the location again to clear the error. - On Windows, `W_OK` checks only the read-only attribute, not access control lists. The real folder creation catches an ACL error. - In the Git flow, other clone failures, for example a bad URL or authentication, still come from the Git extension in its own dialog. These errors occur after our dialog closes. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - New Folder from Template and New Folder from Git now show an error (and do not continue) when you cannot create a folder in the location (#16252) ### Validation Steps @:new-folder-flow @:modal @:web @:win New Vitest tests cover the extension command (with real file permissions), the renderer helper, the location step, the Git dialog, and the template accept flow. To test manually: 1. Create a folder that you cannot write to: `mkdir -p ~/tmp/nf-readonly && chmod a-w ~/tmp/nf-readonly`. 2. Open _New Folder from Template..._ and select Python Project. Set the location to `~/tmp/nf-readonly`. 3. Make sure that the permission error shows under the location and that Next is disabled. 4. Change the location to a folder that you can write to. Make sure that the error goes away, Next is enabled, and the flow creates the folder. 5. Do steps 2 to 4 again with Empty Project, and with Create instead of Next. 6. Open _New Folder from Git..._ and set the location to `~/tmp/nf-readonly`. Make sure that the error shows under the location and that OK is disabled for clicks and for Enter. 7. If you have a server build or a remote window, do steps 2 and 6 again. Use a folder that the remote user cannot write to. 8. With no settings changed and a workspace open, make sure that the default location is still the parent of the workspace folder. 9. When you are done, remove the folder: `chmod u+w ~/tmp/nf-readonly && rm -rf ~/tmp/nf-readonly`.

title: Stop bundling `jedi` and `parso` with the Python kernel (and update file-count budgets)
description: Addresses #16025 ### Summary This PR removes `jedi` and `parso` from the ipykernel bundle that ships with positron-python. These two packages are 1,921 files in the 2026.10.0 Workbench build, which is about 40% of the files in positron-python, but it turns out that nothing in Positron uses them these days. IPython does require jedi and jedi requires parso, but only one IPython module imports jedi: the completer in `IPython/core/completer.py`. This completer runs only when the kernel gets a Jupyter `complete_request`, and Positron never sends one of these. The supervisor sends `is_complete_request`, which is a totally different message. Console and notebook completions come from the Positron language server and Pyrefly. Our language server has not used jedi since #10908. When jedi is not installed, IPython catches the `ImportError` and uses its other matchers. As a result, a `complete_request` from some other client still gets an answer. Changes: - `gulpfile.js`: a new `removeJedi()` step runs after the pip install of the pure-Python kernel requirements. It deletes `jedi`, `parso`, and their `dist-info` directories. The pins in `py3-requirements.txt` stay, because IPython declares jedi as a dependency. - `positron_ipkernel.py`: removes a warning filter for jedi. The old in-kernel jedi language server needed it. - `positron-path-budget.ts`: the budget for positron-python goes from 5,950 to 3,850. The budget for all of `extensions/` goes from 17,100 to 15,000. One change in behavior is that the bundle paths come first on `sys.path`. If the environment of the user has its own jedi, the bundled IPython now imports that copy at kernel start. Before this PR, the bundled copy had priority. The completer still never runs, so this change has no effect on completions. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:console @:editor @:notebooks @:positron-notebooks @:debug @:variables The dev build can test out this change, because the extension runs from the source tree. After you switch to this branch, run `npx gulp installPythonLibs` in `extensions/positron-python`. If you switch back to `main`, run it again to restore jedi. 1. Make sure that `python_files/lib/ipykernel/py3` contains no `jedi` or `parso` directory. 2. Start a Python console with an environment that **does not** have jedi, for example a new empty venv. If the environment has its own jedi, the kernel imports that copy. 3. In the console, run this code: ```python import IPython, IPython.core.completer as c IPython.__file__ # under python_files/lib/ipykernel/py3 c.JEDI_INSTALLED # False import jedi # ModuleNotFoundError ``` 4. Make sure that console completions, hover, and signature help operate as on `main`. Examples: `os.pa`, `df["` for column names, `%ti` for magics, and `print(`. 5. Do the same completion checks in a notebook cell, and use the debugger to step over a line of code.

title: drive-positron: fix ui.sh and code every helper shares from the nightly run
description:
### Summary

Nightly self-heal: 1 helper fixed, ready to review.

**To do:** Review and merge this PR.

#### finder-ui-click-convert-to-code: fixed

- **What broke:** `ui.sh click` on a Data Explorer toolbar button such as Convert to Code or Import Data reported success but did nothing; no dialog opened.
- **Why:** It pressed the instant the pointer arrived, while the button was redrawing its label for the hover, so press and release hit different elements.
- **In a real run:** the agent did it by hand: 2026-10-12T01:51:22Z ui.sh -s=positron: FAILED read dialog: no dialog is open / 2026-10-12T01:51:35Z raw -s=positron: click "Convert to Code" button in the Data Explorer toolbar / 2026-10-12T01:51:48Z ui.sh -s=positron: click "button" "Cancel" in dialog -> the dialog closed. Same in run 38163745988:...
- **Fix:** It lets the page react to the pointer arriving before pressing, as a person's resting pointer does.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Helper bug in the shared lib.click (scripts/page-lib.ts). It moved the pointer and pressed right away (page.mouse.move, then page.mouse.down with nothing between), and only waited one task turn between press and release. Positron's ActionBarActionButton sets mouseInside state on mouseenter (actionBarActionButton.tsx onMouseEnter -> setMouseInside), and ActionBarButton declares ActionBarButtonFace as a component inside its render (actionBarButton.tsx line 156), so that re-render remounts the button's face and label. When the pointer came from somewhere else (a closed menu, popup or dialog), the remount ran in the turn between press and release: the press landed on the old label and the release on the new one, so Chrome sent no click and ui.sh reported ok, changed:false. A person's pointer rests on the button before pressing, so the remount is done by then; this is not a product bug a user can hit. This is the same fix as the earlier verdict from run 38201813918, which never reached this tree (page-lib.ts still had move+down back to back). Fix: lib.click now waits one page task turn (the same named condition already used after the press: a setTimeout(0) queued after the input's tasks) after the move and before the press. Evidence on the instance: the finding's steps failed (changed:false, no dialog); with the fix Convert to Code opened its dialog 3/3 after Cancel and once after the Column Actions menu, and Import Data after Apply Filter closed the filter popup. With the new pau...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: click exited 0 with changed:false; read dialog: no dialog is open; the screenshot shows only the tooltip and no dialog
- finder, fail: same: click ok, changed:false, exit 0; read dialog: no dialog is open. Earlier, a raw playwright click on the same button opened the dialog
- fixer, fail: After console-run, %view df and choose Column Actions > Sort Descending, ui.sh click button 'Convert to Code' --in editor exited 0 with changed:false, and read dialog said no dialog is open.

**To reproduce:**

```sh
console-run.sh --session heal-find --language python 'import pandas as pd; df = pd.DataFrame({"a":[3,1,2],"b":list("xyz")})'
console-run.sh --session heal-find --language python '%view df'
ui.sh --session heal-find choose button 'Column Actions' 'Sort Descending' --in editor --nth 1
ui.sh --session heal-find click button 'Convert to Code' --in editor
ui.sh --session heal-find read dialog
```

**Commit:** 42b0e7ed63d49d05984afe95ea20e32dd5dfdb07

</details>

title: e2e: stop running the Postgres tests on Windows
description:
Stops running the two Postgres e2e suites on Windows and removes the WSL2 + Docker setup that existed only to serve them.

Windows e2e shards have been failing roughly once a day while setting up WSL. It looks like a timeout, but it isn't one. The job annotation reads "The hosted runner lost communication with the server": the runner dies inside "Set up WSL2 and Docker (for Postgres)", no step log is uploaded, and GitHub fails the job about 45 minutes later. The job is nowhere near its 150-minute limit, and a step timeout can't fire because the runner process that enforces it is gone. On the merge lane, step data confirms this on Oct 6, Oct 7 and Oct 8 (twice). Nine more runs since Sep 16, five of them on Oct 5, have the same annotation and job length, but GitHub kept no step records for them. Each Windows shard set up its own container, so every shard was exposed. The coverage isn't worth the noise.

title: Add `POSITRON_EXTENSIONS`, `POSITRON_PORTABLE`, and `POSITRON_APPDATA` environment variables
description:
Fixes #13598

### Summary

With this PR, Positron now reads three new environment variables: `POSITRON_EXTENSIONS`, `POSITRON_PORTABLE`, and `POSITRON_APPDATA`. They replace `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS`, `VSCODE_PORTABLE`, and `VSCODE_APPDATA`. With the new names, an administrator can redirect the extensions folder or the data folder for Positron without an effect on VS Code, and the reverse is also true. This completes the separation that started when Positron moved its defaults from `.vscode/` to `.positron/` (see discussion #13594 and #8839).

The old `VSCODE_*` names still work as a fallback, as currently implemented for the next _two_ releases. If both names are set, the `POSITRON_*` name wins. When Positron uses a deprecated name, it writes a warning to the Main log, and the CLI writes the same warning to stderr.

Implementation notes:

- A small helper in `src/vs/base/common/positronEnvironment.ts` holds the precedence rule. All read sites use it. An empty `POSITRON_*` value counts as unset, the same as the existing truthiness checks.
- On desktop and CLI startup, `configurePortable()` now sets `POSITRON_PORTABLE` and always removes `VSCODE_PORTABLE`. All other Positron processes see only the new name. `POSITRON_PORTABLE` is also kept across an in-app restart.
- Each change to an upstream file is small and is inside Positron markers, with the original line kept as a comment.
- Internal `VSCODE_*` variables do not change. This includes shell integration, IPC and bootstrap variables, and dev and build variables. These are internal to Positron or are read by third-party tools.

### Tradeoffs

- **The fallback does not fix the reported problem immediately.** Until we remove the fallback, a machine-wide `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS` for VS Code still redirects Positron. The only exception is when the administrator also sets `POSITRON_EXTENSIONS`. For this reason, the removal date is part of the fix; see the rollout plan. ⤵️
- **Extensions no longer see `VSCODE_PORTABLE` on desktop.** Normalization removes it from every child process. An extension that reads it to detect portable mode stops seeing it. I know of no such extension and couldn't find any on GitHub. A side benefit of making this change is that a portable Positron no longer gives its portable folder to a VS Code that you start from the Positron terminal.
- **No warning for `VSCODE_PORTABLE`.** Normalization removes the variable before the warning code runs. Portable mode almost always comes from the data folder next to the app, not from the variable, so the release notes cover this case.
- **The warning is log-only.** There is no notification or dialog. The warning can also show when `--extensions-dir` already overrides `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS`.
- **`POSITRON_EXTENSIONS` has no effect on Positron Server or Posit Workbench.** The server always sets `--extensions-dir`, and that argument wins over the variable. `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS` has the same limit today.
- **The native Rust CLI does not change.** Positron does not build or ship the tunnel binary, so the Rust files stay the same as upstream.

### Rollout plan

| Release | Behavior of `VSCODE_*` | Communication |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.11 | Fallback. `POSITRON_*` wins. A warning goes to the log when Positron uses the fallback. | Release note: new variables, `VSCODE_*` is deprecated, removal in 2027.01. |
| 2026.12 | Same as 2026.11. | Release note: last release that reads `VSCODE_*`. |
| 2027.01 | Positron ignores `VSCODE_*`. | Release note under breaking changes. |

If for some reason this PR misses the 2026.11 branch cut, each row would move one month later. The removal release is one constant in `positronEnvironment.ts`, so that change is small.

Follow-up work after this PR merges:

- An issue for `posit-dev/positron-website` to document the new variables.
- A tracking issue on the 2027.01 milestone to remove the fallback.
- Replies on #8839 and discussion #13594 with the new names and the removal release.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Positron now reads `POSITRON_EXTENSIONS`, `POSITRON_PORTABLE`, and `POSITRON_APPDATA`. With these, you can set the Positron extensions folder and data folders without an effect on VS Code. The `VSCODE_*` names still work, but they are deprecated, and Positron 2027.01 will ignore them (#13598)

#### Bug Fixes

- A portable Positron no longer gives its portable folder to a VS Code that you start from the Positron terminal (#13598)

### Validation Steps

@:critical @:extensions @:win @:web

Use a Windows release build (I kicked some off; find the link below). Start Positron from the Start menu, not from a terminal, unless a step says to use a terminal. Close all Positron windows before each step, because a second launch goes to the instance that is already open. To set a user variable, use **Edit environment variables for your account** in Windows settings. New Start menu launches get the change.

To find the extensions folder, use _Extensions: Open Extensions Folder_. To find the deprecation warning, use _Developer: Show Logs..._ and select **Main**.

**Extensions folder**

1. Set `POSITRON_EXTENSIONS` to `C:\pos-ext`. Start Positron. Confirm that the extensions folder is `C:\pos-ext`, and that the bootstrap extensions install there on the first launch.
2. Also set `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS` to `C:\vs-ext`. Start Positron. Confirm that Positron still uses `C:\pos-ext` and that the Main log has no warning. If VS Code is installed, confirm that it uses `C:\vs-ext`.
3. Remove `POSITRON_EXTENSIONS` and keep `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS`. Start Positron. Confirm that it uses `C:\vs-ext` and that the Main log shows this warning: `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS is deprecated and will be ignored starting in Positron 2027.01; set POSITRON_EXTENSIONS instead.`
4. In a new PowerShell window, run `positron --list-extensions`. Confirm that the warning shows on stderr. Then run `positron --list-extensions 2>$null` and confirm that the warning does not show.
5. Do the "keep Positron on its default" setup that an administrator uses. Open an elevated terminal and run the command below. Then sign out and sign in again, because `reg add` does not tell open programs about the change. Keep `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS` set as in step 3. Start Positron and confirm that it uses `C:\Users\<you>\.positron\extensions`.

```
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment" /v POSITRON_EXTENSIONS /t REG_EXPAND_SZ /d "%USERPROFILE%\.positron\extensions" /f
```

6. Set `POSITRON_EXTENSIONS` to a folder that your user cannot write to, for example a new folder under `C:\Program Files`. Start Positron. Record what happens to the bootstrap extension install and to extension updates. The documentation needs this result.

**Data folders**

7. In PowerShell, run `$env:POSITRON_APPDATA = 'C:\pos-appdata'; positron`. Confirm that Positron creates its user data under `C:\pos-appdata\Positron`.
8. In PowerShell, run `mkdir C:\pos-portable; $env:POSITRON_PORTABLE = 'C:\pos-portable'; positron`. Confirm that `user-data`, `extensions`, and `argv.json` are created under `C:\pos-portable`. In the Positron terminal, confirm that `$env:POSITRON_PORTABLE` shows the path and that `$env:VSCODE_PORTABLE` is empty.
9. While Positron is portable, do an action that restarts Positron, for example change `window.titleBarStyle` and accept the restart. Confirm that Positron still uses `C:\pos-portable`.
10. In PowerShell, run `$env:VSCODE_PORTABLE = 'C:\does-not-exist'; positron`. Confirm that Positron is not portable: it uses the default user data folder, and the Positron terminal shows neither variable.

When you are done, remove the variables and the test folders.

title: Keep the first quick input after a modal dialog from closing at once
description:
- Fixes #9494
- Fixes #16290

When a Positron modal dialog is open, the quick input moves into the dialog so that it is inside the focus scope of the dialog. A `MutationObserver` then watches the dialog and closes the quick input if the dialog removes it. This observer disconnected only when it fired. When the modal closed, the observer stayed attached to the detached dialog. Then the next quick input moved out of that old dialog, the stale observer fired, and the new quick input closed at once.

We have a couple of problems/symptoms that folks are running into with this:

- **#9494:** In _New Folder from Git_, Browse arms the observer. After you click OK, `git clone` asks for the SSH key passphrase with a quick input. The stale observer closes it, askpass returns an empty passphrase, and the clone fails with `Permission denied (publickey)`.
- **#16290:** After an earlier modal used Browse, the first Browse click in a new modal shows no folder picker. The second click works.

Browse opens the simple file dialog (a quick input) on web and remote windows, or when `files.simpleDialog.enable` is on; our Workbench customers see this problem every time.

This PR keeps the observer in a `MutableDisposable`. The controller arms the observer on each show in a modal. It clears the observer on hide, and before each move of the quick input container. All changes are inside Positron blocks in `quickInputController.ts`.

A gap that this PR does not change is that the observer watches only the direct children of the dialog box. If a modal unmounts while a quick input is visible, the observer does not fire. The modal is `inert` while a quick input is open, so I believe this case is really rare.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- The SSH key passphrase prompt now shows when you clone a repository with _New Folder from Git_ after you select a folder with Browse (#9494)
- The first Browse click in the new folder flow now opens the folder picker (#16290)

### Validation Steps

@:new-folder-flow @:modal @:web

On desktop, set `"files.simpleDialog.enable": true` first. Web does not need this setting. Use the File menu to open each dialog. If you use the Command Palette, it consumes the stale observer and hides the problem.

1. Select **File > New Folder from Git...**.
2. Click **Browse...**, cancel the folder picker, and then click **Cancel** on the dialog.
3. Select **File > New Folder from Git...** again, and click **Browse...** once. The folder picker opens on the first click (#16290).
4. Cancel the folder picker, and then click **Cancel** on the dialog.
5. Push <kbd>Cmd+Shift+P</kbd>. The Command Palette opens on the first try (#9494).

Before this fix, nothing opens at step 3 or step 5 (the second try would work).

title: Run a SQL statement against its data connection in the user's session
description:
Closes #16545. Part of #16547. Related to #15068.
**PR 4 of 4** -- stacked on #16182.

> Review this as the diff against `sclark/sql-3-support`, not against `main`.

### Summary

Makes the SQL runnable. PR 2 gave a `.sql` file statement ranges; this runs the statement under the
cursor against the connection the file is bound to, in the user's own R, Python or SQL session.

Three parts:

**The session half of the core API.** An extension can put a data connection into a running session
-- binding it to a variable through the existing Connect With flow -- and ask the driver for the
code that queries it. This is the counterpart to PR 1, which answered everything that did not need
a session.

**One query code generator shared across the drivers.** Each `positron-data-driver-*` extension was
going to need the same "quote this query, wrap it in the language's read call" logic, with only the
recipe per language and variant differing. That logic now lives once in a new
`positron-data-driver-common` package, and each driver supplies its recipes. The quoting is the part
worth reviewing: the query comes from the user's editor, so R and Python each get their own string
literal escaping.

**Cmd+Enter.** Runs the statement through the session the file's connection is bound to, choosing
the language from what the connection was opened with. If the user is working in a SQL console
(ggsql), the statement goes there instead, which is the route #15068 asked about.

Execution goes through `positron.runtime.*` throughout rather than reaching into a
`LanguageRuntimeSession` directly, so it stays on the right side of #12589.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Cmd+Enter in a SQL file runs the statement against its data connection, in the user's R, Python
  or SQL session (#16545)
- Data connection drivers share one query code generator, so querying works the same across DuckDB,
  PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redshift, Snowflake, Databricks and ODBC (#16545)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections @:sessions @:console

No e2e tests are added. Execution is covered by the `positron-sql` extension host suite and each
driver's own suite (databricks 99, redshift 96, odbc 70, postgresql 41, plus 9 in the new shared
package), which is where the generated code can be asserted exactly.

1. Connect to a PostgreSQL or DuckDB database and start an R session.
2. Open a `.sql` file bound to that connection, put the cursor in a `SELECT`, and press Cmd+Enter.
3. Confirm the R console runs a `DBI::dbGetQuery(...)` against the connection variable and prints
   the result -- and that the query is the statement under the cursor, not the whole file.
4. Repeat with a Python session and confirm it runs `pd.read_sql_query(...)`.
5. Rename the connection variable in the console, then run again, and confirm the generated code
   uses the name the session actually holds rather than the driver's default.
6. Run a query containing a double quote and a backslash (`SELECT 'a\"b\\c'`) and confirm it reaches
   the database as written rather than breaking the generated string literal.
7. Run a multi-line statement and confirm it executes as one statement.
8. With a ggsql SQL console open, press Cmd+Enter and confirm the statement runs there rather than
   in R or Python.
9. Press Cmd+Enter in a `.sql` file with no connection and confirm it reports that rather than
   failing silently.

title: Fix webview menu-shortcut suppression ownership
description:
Closes #16553 

The native menu bindings are normally suppressed by the main window when a webview is focused. However, when switching webviews, the blur and focus handlers of the webviews are racing with each other. It's possible to for the cleanup/blur handler of the old webview to fire after the setup/focus handler of the new webview. When this happens, keybindings from the native menu are incorrectly re-enabled.

To fix this, the main window now tracks the webview that owns suppression for each window, which is the only one allowed to restore native menu bindings.

title: drive-positron: fix ui.sh, tree.sh and code every helper shares from the nightly run
description:
### Summary

Nightly self-heal: 2 helpers fixed, ready to review.

**To do:** Review and merge this PR. "finder-tree-variables-no-rows" came back after being fixed on earlier nights; those fixes were never merged.

#### finder-pick-same-label-rows: fixed

- **What broke:** `ui.sh pick` could not choose between quick pick rows that share a label, such as the Python versions in Create Environment.
- **Why:** It matched only the label, ignored --nth, and rejected the 'label (description)' form that its own error printed for each row.
- **In a real run:** the agent did it by hand: 2026-10-10T14:52:59Z ui.sh -s=off: FAILED pick 'Python (3.12)': no row matches "Python (3.12)" / 2026-10-10T14:53:12Z raw -s=off: click option "Python, 3.12" in the Python version quick pick; and in run 38156963931: 2026-10-11T17:13:26Z raw -s=cold2: press Enter on the highlighted version row "Pytho...
- **Fix:** pick now accepts a row as its error shows it, or --nth N, and its error says which to use.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Helper bug in the shared lib.pick (scripts/page-lib.ts). In exact mode the match was only r.label === exact (the old 'hit', line 269), and several matches got '<n> rows match "X"; be more specific' (line 289). In exact mode no text can be more specific: the row as pick's own 'shown' list writes it, 'label (description)', matched no label. ui.sh pick passed only { exact: text } (dp-ui.ts pickRow line 253, and the 'pick' case at line 366 built no nth), so the --nth that parse() accepts was silently dropped. This is the same fix as the earlier verdict from run 38201813918 (commit 91ad9d55ce), which never reached this tree: the code here still had the old match, so the bug came back. Fix, in lib.pick: when no label equals the text, an exact match also takes a row whose 'label (description)' equals it, so label matches still win as before. Matches are sorted into list order, and a new nth option takes the Nth (more than the count is an error). The row returned carries an occurrence, so lib.clickRow clicks the right one when rows look the same. In exact mode the shared error now ends at '<n> rows match "X"' and the caller says how to narrow it. ui.sh pick reads --nth through count() (0 or junk is a usage error, exit 2) and adds: give the row as "shown" writes it, or pass --nth (or --nth only when the shown rows are identical). Words mode (nb.sh pick-kernel, start-session.sh) keeps 'be more specific', which works there because words match descriptions; dp-console still matches ' row...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: pick 'Python 3.12', 'Python, 3.12', 'Python (3.12)' -> no row matches; pick Python -> 4 rows match; shown ["Python (3.11)","Python (3.12)","Python (3.10)","Python (3.9)"]
- finder, fail: fresh palette run: pick 'Python (3.12)' and pick 'Python 3.12' -> no row matches; screenshot shows the row 'Python 3.12'
- fixer, fail: Fixture instance with conda at /opt/conda: palette-run 'Python: Create Environment...', pick Conda, then pick 'Python (3.12)' and pick 'Python 3.12' -> no row matches, shown ["Python (3.11)","Python (3.12)","Python (3.10)","Python (3.9)"]; pick Python -> 4 rows match; be more specific; pick Python -...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
palette-run.sh --session heal-find 'Python: Create Environment...'
ui.sh --session heal-find pick Conda
ui.sh --session heal-find pick 'Python (3.12)'
ui.sh --session heal-find pick 'Python 3.12'
ui.sh --session heal-find pick Python
```

**Commit:** 456f42f364cc3f64e791ac6a067e3b51dbe7e6ff

</details>

#### finder-tree-variables-no-rows: fixed

- **What broke:** `tree.sh` could not see the Variables pane: it listed no variables and told the agent to scroll when asked to expand one.
- **Why:** It only looked for the row kinds other trees use, and the Variables pane draws its rows differently.
- **In a real run:** the agent did it by hand: 2026-10-10T15:04:54Z tree.sh -s=positron: FAILED --view Variables expand cfg: no visible row labelled "cfg"; expand its parent or scroll / 2026-10-10T15:05:02Z raw -s=positron: click the expand chevron of cfg in the Variables pane / 2026-10-10T15:05:19Z raw -s=positron: click the expand chevron of l...
- **Fix:** It now reads, expands and clicks Variables rows, with or without naming the view, and skips other sessions' hidden Variables.
- **Review:** sent back once, then approved
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.
- **Seen before:** fixed on 1 earlier night too (run 38201813918) and came back, so those fixes never landed.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** dp-tree.ts read() queried only `.positron-tree-row` and `.monaco-list-row[role=treeitem]`. The Variables pane draws its rows as `.variable-item` / `.variable-group` / `.variable-overflow` with `.expand-collapse-area` chevrons, so tree.sh found none of them: `rows` returned [] with ok:true, and expand/click/collapse failed with a misleading 'scroll' hint. The fix adds Variables selectors to selectors.ts (css.tree.var*) and parses those rows in read(): the level comes from the `.name-column-indenter` margin, the state from the chevron icon, and the pieces are name, value and type, so the label is the variable name. Reviewer note acted on: Variables rows are now read with or without --view. tree() always goes through lib.scope(a.view); lib.scope('') is the page body, as before, but it now also runs lib.unstack(), so the data-dp-stacked filter leaves out other sessions' Variables in the no-view case too. While checking that live (R on top of a stacked Python session), I found and fixed a second cause: read() left old `data-dp-row` marks on rows it no longer counted (stacked or in another view). After `rows` without --view while Python was on top, the hidden `cfg` row kept mark 5. Then R's `rl` also got index 5, and `[data-dp-row=5]` matched the hidden row first, so `expand rl` failed with 'something drawn on top of it took the click'. read() now clears every data-dp-row mark in the document before it numbers rows. Checked live: no-view `rows` lists the R Variables rows and not th...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: rows -> {"ok":true,"rows":[]}; expand cfg -> no visible row labelled "cfg"; screenshot shows cfg and l rows in Variables
- finder, fail: after del cfg and recreating cfg: rows -> {"ok":true,"rows":[]}; expand cfg -> no visible row labelled "cfg"; view-read shows ' Values cfg {...} dict [2]'
- fixer, fail: With the first-round change in the tree, after cfg = {...} in Python: `tree.sh rows` without --view listed only Explorer rows, and `expand cfg` failed with 'no visible row labelled "cfg"; expand its parent or scroll', while `--view Variables rows` listed cfg. After the no-view fix, with R on top of ...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
console-run.sh --session heal-find --language python 'cfg = {"db": {"host": "x", "port": 1}, "debug": True}'
tree.sh --session heal-find --view Variables rows
tree.sh --session heal-find --view Variables expand cfg
view-read.sh --session heal-find --view Variables
```

**Commit:** 90df2607f3bc953c1a91d1e3171531d5d658d81b

</details>

title: Keep a remembered R following your default R after interpreter discovery
description:
Fixes #15992

This PR fixes one of two causes that make new windows start an older R version instead of the default R. The work in #16505, which merged today, fixes the other cause. Thank you so much, @dhruvisompura! 🎉 

### Background

Positron remembers the R version that you used in each workspace. Windows with no folder open share one stored R for the profile. For R, the stored record includes a `current` flag. When this flag is `true`, positron-r starts the default R at launch instead of the stored binary. Thus the stored R changes when you change the default R, for example with `rig default`.

### What #16505 fixed

The interpreter discovery cache sometimes dropped interpreters, frequently both R entries. The cache reloaded its own saves as if a different window wrote them. Because of this, a new R 4.6 installation did not show in the session picker. Users then started the older R, and Positron stored it. #16505 stops the cache from reloading its own saves. It also fixes expired cache entries that did not recover.

### What this PR fixes

When an interpreter registers during discovery, `onDidRegisterRuntime` refreshes the stored record with the new metadata. #14813 added this step to remove stored `~/` paths but it turns out the step also replaced `extraRuntimeData`, which belongs to the language extension.

The R runtime ID uses only the binary path and the version, so the older R keeps the same ID after the default R changes. Discovery then reports the older R with `current: false`, and the refresh writes that value into the stored record. After that, all new windows start the older R.

This PR keeps the stored `extraRuntimeData` when it refreshes the record. The other fields refresh as before, so the `~/` path fix continues to work. When a session starts, Positron continues to save the full metadata of that session.

The refresh occurs only when no R console starts at launch, for example when the R startup behavior is `manual`. A launch that starts R does not change the flag. I believe this is why the problem was so difficult to reproduce!

This PR does not repair a record that already has `current: false`. Positron cannot tell this record from a user choice of a non-default R. To reset the record, folks will need to start the R version that they want one time.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- New windows start the default R after you change the default, and also after interpreter discovery runs (#15992)

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:sessions

A new unit test in `runtimeStartup.vitest.ts` covers the fix. To test manually on macOS, you need rig and two R versions:

1. Quit Positron totally. Run `rig default 4.4-arm64` (or a different older R that you have).
2. Open a window with no folder (the "no workspace" state). Start R 4.4.
3. Run `1 + 1` in the console, then quit Positron.
4. Run `rig default 4.6`.
5. In your user `settings.json`, set `"interpreters.startupBehavior": "manual"` in the `[r]` and `[python]` blocks. (Probably ask your favorite AI agent to do this, so you don't have to open Positron.)
6. Open a window with no folder. Do not start a session.
7. Wait until the session picker shows your R versions, then quit Positron.
8. Remove the settings from step 5 (again, probably via your favorite AI agent rather than from within Positron). Open a window with no folder.
9. Make sure that R 4.6 starts. Before this fix, R 4.4 starts.

You can see the stored record after step 7. Quit Positron, then run this command. With the fix, the output shows `current= True`:

```sh
sqlite3 ~/Library/Application\ Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb \
  "select value from ItemTable where key='positron.affiliatedRuntimeMetadata.v2.r'" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; a=json.load(sys.stdin); m=a['metadata']; e=m['extraRuntimeData']; print(m['runtimeName'], 'current=', e.get('current'))"
```

title: Fix duplicate missing packages badge
description:
Fixes #16311

Positron notebooks showed the "missing packages" badge twice in the toolbar. There are two badges registered on the same toolbar menu: one for scripts and one for notebooks. The script badge did not exclude notebooks, and the notebook toolbar renders that same menu, so both appeared. The script badge is now hidden when the active editor is a Positron notebook, so notebooks show only their own badge.

This also adds an e2e test that opens a notebook that imports a missing package, switches to another tab and back, and checks that exactly one badge is shown.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- Fix the missing packages badge appearing twice in the Positron notebook toolbar when a script missing a package was also open (#16311)

### Validation Steps

@:packages-pane @:positron-notebooks

1. Enable Positron notebooks and open a notebook with a Python kernel that imports a package that isn't installed (e.g. `import cowsay`).
2. Check that the toolbar shows one "missing package" badge.
3. Switch to another editor tab and back, and check there is still only one badge.
4. Open a Python script that imports a missing package and check that its badge still shows.

title: Merge 1.138.0 from upstream
description:
This PR merges upstream Code OSS changes from 1.134.0 to 1.138.0.

### Notable changes

- Electron is updated to 42.10.0. Run `npm install` after pulling.
- The web workbench's content security policy now uses a per-request nonce instead of fixed script hashes. Positron's own startup scripts (import map, license, SageMaker) were updated to match.
- Automatic updates now wait when the user is on a metered connection. Positron adopts this for its own update checks and for Windows downloads.
- The gate that turns off Copilot inline suggestions when AI is disabled was moved to a new file, because upstream removed the file it lived in.
- Upstream's new scenario tests depend on test infrastructure that Positron removed, so they were dropped.
- Real Codex agent host tests are skipped, since they can't run in our unprivileged CI container and Positron doesn't ship the agent host.

### Testing

Build, Vitest, core unit tests, and extension host tests pass. The full e2e suite was run in the CI lab; the remaining failures were traced to environment gaps or known flakes, not to the merge.

title: Scope R and Python interpreter settings to the window, not to folders
description:
Fixes #13487

### Summary

This PR changes the scope of the R and Python interpreter settings from `resource` to `window`. The `window` scope matches how Positron actually reads these settings; the old `resource` scope promised a behavior that Positron never gave.

**The old scope was wrong.** A `resource` setting can have a different value for each folder in a multi-root workspace. To get the value for a folder, the code must give a folder URI when it reads the setting. The R and Python extensions never give a URI for these settings. As a result, the Settings editor showed these settings in the Folder tab, but Positron ignored a value that a user set there. The extension host also logged a warning each time the code read one of these settings: "Accessing a resource scoped configuration without providing a resource is not expected."

**The `resource` scope was not a deliberate choice.** Before #6953, these settings had the `machine` scope. On Workbench, a `machine` setting shows only in the Remote tab, so Workbench admins could not set defaults for it (#6909). #6953 changed the scope to `resource` to correct this problem. The `window` scope also corrects it, and #6909 lists `window` as a satisfactory scope. Nothing in #6953 needed per-folder values.

**The `window` scope is correct.** This is the main thing I'm arguing here! Interpreter discovery operates one time for the whole window. It does not relate to one folder. A `window` setting can go in user, remote, and workspace settings, but not in the folder settings of a multi-root workspace. This is the behavior that the code already has.

### Effect for users

- Workbench admins can still set defaults. In a remote session, `window` settings show in the User tab.
- Single-folder workspaces do not change. In a single-folder workspace, the folder settings are the workspace settings.
- In a multi-root workspace, the Folder tab no longer shows these settings. If the `settings.json` file of a folder has one of these settings, the editor now tells the user that the value does not apply. Before this change, Positron ignored the value and gave no message.

### Changed settings

- R: `positron.r.customRootFolders`, `positron.r.customBinaries`, `positron.r.interpreters.exclude`, `positron.r.interpreters.override`, `positron.r.interpreters.default`, `positron.r.interpreters.condaDiscovery`, `positron.r.interpreters.pixiDiscovery`, `positron.r.interpreters.pathDiscoveryMode`
- Python: `python.interpreters.include`, `python.interpreters.exclude`, `python.interpreters.override`

`python.defaultInterpreterPath` keeps the `resource` scope. Upstream code reads it with a folder URI, so per-folder values work for this setting.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- R and Python interpreter settings no longer show in the folder settings of a multi-root workspace (Positron always ignored them there anyway) (#13487)

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:vscode-settings

1. On desktop, open a multi-root workspace. In the Settings editor, select a folder in the Folder tab and search for `@tag:interpreterSettings`.
2. Make sure that the R and Python `interpreters` settings do not show. `python.defaultInterpreterPath` still shows.
3. In the `.vscode/settings.json` file of one folder, add `"positron.r.interpreters.default": "/path/to/R"`. Make sure that the editor shows that this setting does not apply.
4. Open a single-folder workspace. Set `positron.r.interpreters.default` in the Workspace tab, then reload the window. Make sure that R starts with that interpreter.
5. For extra credit, on Positron on Workbench, open the Settings editor and search for `@tag:interpreterSettings`. Make sure that all the settings show in the User tab.

title: Add supervisor attachment boundary logging
description:
## Summary

Adds six boundary events around the two operations used to attach to a prestarted supervisor:

- cached-handshake retrieval starts and completes in the extension host;
- cached-handshake replay starts and completes in the server broker;
- `serverStatus()` verification starts and completes or fails.

The existing log timestamps can be compared to determine whether time was spent reaching the broker, replaying or receiving the cached handshake, reaching the status handler, or waiting for its response. No handshake payloads or bearer tokens are logged.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/server-supervisor-handshake.vitest.ts`
- `npm run build-check -- --pretty false`

title: Fix interpreter cache entries that stay expired or get dropped
description:
Fixes #16443

This fixes two bugs that made Positron run a full interpreter discovery on launches that should have used the cache.

### 1. Expired entries never recovered (#16443)

After Positron went unopened for longer than `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` (30 days), every launch ran a full discovery. Every read hides expired entries, so the wipe before discovery missed them. When discovery found the interpreter again, `upsert()` copied the old `firstSeen` onto it, and it stayed expired.

The cache now drops expired entries when it loads from storage and leaves them out when it saves. The wipe has no hidden entries left to miss, so a re-found interpreter gets a new `firstSeen`. Storage also stops keeping entries for interpreters that are never found again, for example because they were uninstalled.

An entry that expires during a session stays in memory. If a background revalidation updates it just after the cutoff, it keeps its old `firstSeen`, so it doesn't get another 30 days without a full discovery.

### 2. Entries dropped during discovery

The main process sends every application storage change back to the window that made it, 100-200 ms later. During discovery the cache saves faster than that. It reloaded its own older saves as if another window had made them, and lost interpreters, often both R entries. This has been there since #13291.

Each save now records which cache instance wrote it, and the cache doesn't reload its own saves.

### Tests

- `runtimeDiscoveryCache.vitest.ts`:
  - one test for each bug
  - expired entries are left out of storage
  - guard: an entry that expires during a session keeps its `firstSeen`
  - guard: saves from other windows still reload
- `runtimeStartup.vitest.ts`: four launches across a 31-day gap.

All new tests fail on `main` except the two guards.

### Videos

Both videos follow the same steps, one on `main` and one on this branch:

1. Launch 1 fills the cache.
2. Every cache date is moved back 31 days.
3. Two more launches follow.

Zed and reticulate are turned off, and discovery is limited to 2 R and 2 Python interpreters.

| | Launch 2 (main / this PR) | Launch 3 (main / this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Full discovery passes | 2 / 2 | **2 / 0** |
| Entries in the cache | 0 / 4 | **0 / 4** |

**Before (main):**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79b55299-6fb0-4db5-b532-9a6ed7201ed2

**After (this PR):**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0c67aa4-9ece-4c00-8a98-4b20414fa213

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Interpreter discovery no longer runs on every launch after Positron goes unopened for longer than `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` (#16443)
- The interpreter cache no longer drops interpreters found during discovery, which made the next launch run discovery again

### Validation Steps

1. In user `settings.json`, add `"interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays": 0.0035`. This shortens the 30-day limit to about 5 minutes. Ignore the warning that the value is below the minimum.
2. Open Positron and wait for the interpreter list to finish loading.
3. Run **Runtime Startup Diagnostics** from the Command Palette. Under Discovery Cache -> Per-bucket state, `positron-r` and `positron-python` both have entries.
4. Quit Positron and wait at least 5 minutes.
5. Reopen Positron and wait for the interpreter list to finish loading. Run Runtime Startup Diagnostics. A full discovery with reason `cold-start` is expected here. Per-bucket state should list R and Python entries again. On `main` it shows "No cached entries."
6. Quit and reopen Positron right away, within 5 minutes of step 5. Run Runtime Startup Diagnostics. The full discovery table should have no `cold-start` rows for `positron-r` or `positron-python`, and "Foreground cache-hit registrations" should be above 0. On `main`, both languages run `cold-start` again.
7. Remove the `maxAgeDays` setting.

description:
Two changes to the exploratory-test report.

title: drive-positron heal: findings need a cost, fixes sized to the finding, known issues skip the fixer
description:
### Summary

Makes the drive-positron self-heal nightly report fewer, more useful helper findings, and stop re-fixing product bugs that already have an issue.

- A finder lead becomes a finding only if it cost the agent something (gave up, did it by hand, or hit it again), with that evidence in the report
- The fixer and reviewer size each fix to the finding instead of widening it to sibling helpers
- The fixer looks up an existing open issue for a product bug (read-only; it never comments or files)
- Later nights skip the fixer for a product bug with an open issue and report it as "known issue #N, hit again tonight"
- The finder is given last week's known product bugs so it keeps their ids across nights

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

Unit tests and check.ts pass. A backtest on recent runs dropped the leads that cost the agent nothing.

title: Keep an untitled Quarto document's kernel after "Save As"
description:
Fixes #16151

### Summary

This is the second of two PRs for #16151. The first PR (#16506) lets a notebook session's language server follow a change of URI. This PR uses that change to keep the kernel of an untitled Quarto document when you save the document to a file.

An untitled "Save As" fires `IUntitledTextEditorService.onDidSave`. However, it does not fire on a file move, so the Quarto kernel manager did not see it. The untitled editor just closed and its kernel stopped, and then the saved file started a new kernel with no variables. The inline outputs stuck around only because of a content-hash match.

This PR makes these changes:

- **The kernel follows "Save As".** The kernel manager moves a Ready or Busy kernel to the saved URI. It also moves the interpreter that you selected for the document. It points the session and its hidden notebook at the saved document, so the R or Python language server restarts on the saved file.
- **The kernel does not follow in three cases.** These cases are a save under a name that is not Quarto, a saved file that already has its own kernel, and a kernel that is still starting. In these cases, the kernel stops when the untitled editor closes, as before.
- **Close with "Save" stops the kernel.** If you close a dirty untitled tab, select **Save**, and Positron does not open the saved file, the kernel stops.
- **Recovery after a reload is now safer.** The recovery path for untitled documents adopts only a Quarto session that no other document uses and that has the same language. Before this change, one untitled document could take the kernel of a different untitled document.
- **No leaked listeners on start.** When a session was adopted while it was still starting, a second set of listeners stayed attached to it. After "Save As", these listeners sent state for the untitled URI, and the kernel badge became red.
- **Outputs move only on a real "Save As".** Before this change, the output manager moved untitled outputs to any saved `.qmd` that you switched to from an untitled tab.
- **Untitled Quarto documents start a kernel automatically.** The auto-start uses the language of the document, because an untitled URI has no file extension. A blank new document with no code chunk does not start a kernel.

### Known limitations

- If you use "Save As" while a cell runs, the kernel and its variables stay but the saved editor does not show the output that the running cell makes after the save, and queued cells fail. The execution manager stores its work by document URI, so a change to the execution manager is necessary. This is probably worth a followup issue? Opinions? On `main`, this case loses the full kernel.
- This PR does not fix a problem that is already on `main` where after a reload, the first console session that reconnects becomes the foreground session, even when a notebook or Quarto editor is active. As a result, the Variables pane can show the variables of the console until you change tabs. Also pretty edge-case-y.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- An untitled Quarto document now keeps its kernel and variables when you save it to a file (#16151)

### Validation Steps

@:quarto

Turn on Quarto inline output.

1. Run _Quarto: New Document_. Add a Python chunk with `x = 42`, then run the chunk.
2. Save the document as `follow.qmd`.
3. Make sure that the kernel badge stays green and that the output stays on the screen.
4. Add a chunk with `print(x)` and run it. The chunk prints `42`.
5. Do steps 1 to 4 again with an R chunk.
6. Open two untitled Quarto documents and run a chunk in each. Each document gets its own kernel, and switching back and forth behaves correctly.

title: Keep `rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()` from reporting the console
description:
- Fixes #16405
- Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1433

Since #16063, `rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()` returns the console when the console input was the last editor with focus. This is not consistent with what folks are expecting as in RStudio, this function only ever returns source documents. The cause is that Ark uses the same frontend RPC for `getSourceEditorContext()` and `getActiveDocumentContext()`, and #16063 made this RPC console-aware.

This PR adds an optional `allow_console` param to the `last_active_editor_context` RPC. The default value is `true`, so the current behavior does not change. When the value is `false`, the frontend ignores the console and returns the last editor in the editor area. RStudio uses the same name (`allowConsole`) for this concept.

In https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1433, `getSourceEditorContext()` and `documentPath()` send `allow_console: false`, the same as in RStudio. `getActiveDocumentContext()` and `insertText()` continue to use the console.

We should merge this PR _before_ the Ark changes get bumped over here, because the current frontend rejects all params on this RPC so the new Ark will fail with an older Positron.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- `rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()` and `rstudioapi::documentPath()` no longer return the console when the console has focus (#16405)

### Validation Steps

@:console @:ark

Use an Ark build that includes https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1433.

1. Open an R file in the editor.
2. Click in the R console.
3. Run `rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()`. Make sure that the result shows the R file.
4. Run `rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()`. Make sure that the result shows `#console`.
5. Run `rstudioapi::documentPath()`. Make sure that the result is the path of the R file.

title: drive-positron: fix ui.sh, panel.sh, start-session.sh and code every helper shares from the nightly run
description:
### Summary

Nightly self-heal: 3 helpers fixed, 1 product bug, ready to review.

**To do:** Review and merge this PR. Look at the 1 product bug below and file an issue if there is none.

#### finder-notebook-editor-type-picker-no-menu: fixed

- **What broke:** `ui.sh click` and `ui.sh choose` on a notebook's editor-type button opened no menu, so the editor type could not be switched.
- **Why:** Playwright released the click at once. The editor's own focus call, queued on press, then ran after the menu opened and closed it.
- **Fix:** ui.sh's click, choose and check now press, let the page finish handling the press, then release, as a person's click does.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** The finding called this a product bug, but the cause is upstream VS Code, and that interacts with how Playwright clicks. With focus/blur tracing on the kept instance, the menu does open: Menu.focus runs from contextMenuHandler on the click. About 10 ms later EditorGroupView.focus -> PositronNotebookEditor.focus takes focus back, menu.onDidBlur fires and hideContextView closes the menu. That focus call is queued by editorGroupView.ts handleTitleClickOrTouch: on mousedown in the title area it runs setTimeout(() => this.focus()) unless the target is in an action bar or breadcrumb item. The editor-type button is in neither. The handler is upstream code; the only Positron block nearby is the positron-action-bar skip, which does not touch this path. When a person clicks, there is time between press and release, so that queued focus runs before the click handler opens the menu. Playwright's locator.click releases at once, so the click (dp-ui.ts click line 99, choose line 198) opened the menu before the queued focus ran, and the menu lost focus and closed. The fix adds a shared lib.click in page-lib.ts. It does a trial click for Playwright's checks, so a timeout still reads as 'the click on ...' (the filter-popup smoke case checks that text). Then it moves the pointer to the element's center, presses, waits one page task turn (a setTimeout(0) evaluated in the page, which runs after the tasks the press queued), and releases. This waits for a named condition, not a timer. Helpers reach...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: ui.sh click: changed false; read menu: no menu is open; raw click: only the tooltip appears within 1.5 s
- finder, fail: after reopening notebook.ipynb: ui.sh click changed false; .context-view display none, no menu; screenshot shows no menu
- fixer, fail: ui.sh click button 'Positron Notebook' --in editor: {ok:true, changed:false}; read menu: no menu is open; ui.sh choose on the same button: no menu, popup or list opened. Tracing showed the menu rendered with its 4 items and got focus, then lost it about 10 ms later to EditorGroupView.focus (queued b...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
open-file.sh --session heal-find notebook.ipynb
ui.sh --session heal-find click button 'Positron Notebook' --in editor
ui.sh --session heal-find read menu
```

**Commit:** c4070e7a2d05c0e0688a4cdfa5b390520b46d580

</details>

#### finder-panel-tabs-guess-not-named: fixed

- **What broke:** `panel.sh tabs` failed with only a list of commands, so explorers could not tell which command lists the editor or panel tabs.
- **Why:** An unknown command got a fixed list of commands that never named the word typed or answered a common guess.
- **Fix:** Unknown commands in all helpers are refused by name, with the nearest command and the full list.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Helper bug, in a class of sibling helpers. dp-panel.ts panelCommands.panel refused an unknown command word with the fixed text 'command: tab, sessions, ...': it did not name the word, and it gave no answer to the guess 'tabs', which two real runs (37707094533, 37547806430) made. The nearest name, tab, switches tabs instead of listing them, editors lists the editor tabs, and no panel.sh command lists the panel's own tabs. Ten other helpers had the same fixed list. tree.sh, qmd.sh and viewer.sh also checked the word only after a page call or inside the page function: tree.sh FOO LABEL exited 1 with 'command: rows, ...', and qmd.sh and viewer.sh FOO needed a live page before refusing. plots.sh and debug.sh echoed the error themselves, so the failure was never logged. The fix adds commandWord()/notACommand() to dp-lib.ts. They refuse an unknown word (exit 2, before any page call) with '"WORD" is not a command: HINT; the commands: ...'. HINT comes from a per-helper map of guesses that have been seen. Otherwise, when the word is part of a command's name or starts with one, HINT names that command ('the nearest is sessions'). panel.sh maps tabs to 'editors lists the editor tabs, ui.sh read panel shows the panel tabs, and tab NAME shows one panel tab'. editor.sh and ui.sh map tabs to the same pointers. The panel.sh header now says no command lists the panel tabs. Helpers reached: panel, editor, ui, window, settings, clipboard, nb, qmd, tree and viewer (dp.ts), plus plots.sh and debug...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: exit 2, error lists the commands, no pointer to editors or a panel-tab listing
- finder, fail: same error; panel.sh editors then listed the three editor tabs
- fixer, fail: panel.sh --session heal-fix tabs: exit 2, {"ok":false,"error":"command: tab, sessions, console, terminals, delete-session, editors, layout or resize"}, with no pointer to editors or the panel tabs. editor.sh, ui.sh, window.sh, nb.sh, plots.sh, debug.sh, settings.sh and clipboard.sh did not name the ...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
panel.sh --session heal-find tabs
```

**Commit:** b93193ac4ed7877ced7c41c40067e498ff5b7292

</details>

#### finder-start-session-ambiguous-no-flag-hint: fixed

- **What broke:** `start-session.sh` with several R or Python interpreters failed with 'be more specific', never saying to pass --name, and listed only some interpreters.
- **Why:** It passed on the picker's generic error for several matches, which knows nothing of --name and lists only the rows on screen.
- **Fix:** It now says to pass --name with words from a listed row, and lists every matching interpreter of the language, including those below the screen.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Cause: in dp-console.ts start-session's choose(), the `if (!p.ok)` branch rewrote only pick's 'no row matches' error (with --name). When several rows matched it fell through to `return { ...p, listed }`, i.e. lib.pick's generic '<n> rows match "Python"; be more specific', which never names --name. Its `shown` is show(found) in page-lib.ts pick, which holds only rows the virtual list has drawn, capped at 8 with no note. On the fixture, 7 Python interpreters existed but the error said '4 rows match' and listed 4 of them. This is the same mistake the earlier no-match fix (run 37814431547) addressed, on the sibling path. Fix, two parts. (1) start-session: when pick reports several rows matching, walk the picker with the existing lib.allRows() and keep the rows of the language that hold the words. Answer '<n> <Lang> interpreters match[ --name "X"]; pass words from one of the rows in "shown" as --name, in the order the row shows them, such as its version', with every such row in `shown` and `more` when the walk was incomplete. That is the wording the no-match error already uses. (2) Shared, in page-lib.ts: pick's whole-word matcher is now lib.hasWords(), so start-session filters with the same rule and does not keep a copy. pick's show() also adds `more: "N more rows not shown"` when it cuts `shown` at 8. Part 2 reaches every pick caller: palette-run, open-file, ui.sh pick, nb.sh kernel, terminal-run --read and start-session. Their error text, speed and key presses do not change; th...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: exit 1, error '2 rows match "R"; be more specific' and '7 rows match "Python"; be more specific'; no mention of --name
- finder, fail: same two errors; `--language r --name 4.4.2 --new` then started R 4.4.2
- fixer, fail: On a fixture instance, `start-session.sh --language python --new` exited 1 with '4 rows match "Python"; be more specific', listing 4 rows. The picker holds 7 Python interpreters, as the no-match path's walk showed. `--language r --new` gave '2 rows match "R"; be more specific', and `--name 3.10.12` ...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
start-session.sh --session heal-find --language r --new
start-session.sh --session heal-find --language python --new
```

**Commit:** 561b725396e6c57b30553b80acc1eff97884b3e9

</details>

#### finder-palette-first-key-after-dialog-swallowed: product bug

- **What broke:** After Positron's New Folder from Template dialog closes, the next `palette-run.sh` or `open-file.sh` call says the palette did not open; the second call works.
- **Why:** Positron's quick-pick code leaves a stale dialog watcher behind, which closes the palette the moment the next key opens it.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Agrees with the newest verdict (run 37814431547, product); no new evidence points elsewhere. palette-run.sh reports Positron faithfully. The cause is Positron-owned code: the '--- Start Positron ---' block in src/vs/platform/quickinput/browser/quickInputController.ts, handlePositronModal() (lines ~172-189). The quick input widget is reparented into .positron-dynamic-modal-dialog-box while the Folder Template dialog is open, and a MutationObserver on that box ('close the quick pick if the modal closed') watches only its childList. Closing the dialog removes the whole overlay, so the observer never fires, stays connected, and the widget is left detached. On the next Ctrl+Shift+P, handlePositronModal() appends the widget back to the workbench, the stale observer sees !modalContainer.contains(ui.container), calls this.hide() and disconnects. So the palette closes in the same keystroke that opens it, and the second press works. Re-checked tonight: while the dialog was open the widget's parent was positron-dynamic-modal-dialog-box; after Close, no .quick-input-widget was in the document; then the first dry-run failed and the second passed. The block was last touched in e0f38e4f89 / 1c1fd41abd, and it is Positron code, not upstream VS Code. Retrying the key in lib.openQuickInput would hide this product bug (rule 4), so nothing was changed. No regression is claimed.

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: after Close: 'the Command Palette did not open' exit 1; the next identical call exit 0
- finder, fail: same: first call fails, second succeeds; open-file.sh README.md after the same steps at 04:18:00Z: 'Quick Open did not open'
- fixer, fail: Ran the finding's steps on a fresh instance (session heal-fix). New Folder from Template opened the dialog and Close closed it. The first palette-run.sh --dry-run 'Python: Create Environment...' exited 1 with 'the Command Palette did not open'; the identical second call exited 0. A second round show...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
palette-run.sh --session heal-find 'Workspaces: New Folder from Template...'
ui.sh --session heal-find click button Close --in dialog
palette-run.sh --session heal-find --dry-run 'Python: Create Environment...'
palette-run.sh --session heal-find --dry-run 'Python: Create Environment...'
```

</details>

title: e2e: make saveFileAs wait for the saved file's tab before returning
description:
Fixes a flake in `notebook-save-settings.test.ts` on Windows Electron ("Session python-notebook-… did not exit within 15000ms"). The `saveFileAs` fixture returned as soon as the Save As dialog closed, before Positron had finished the save. The test read the file the moment the bytes landed, its `afterEach` deleted the file, and the product's post-write stat then failed with "Failed to save". Save As had already rebound the kernel session to the new file URI, so when the suite closed the still-untitled notebook, nothing shut the session down and the suite's wait for the session to exit timed out. The fixture now waits for the active editor tab to show the saved file name before it returns. That tab change only happens after the save succeeds, so the test body and its cleanup cannot run mid-save. The quarto persistence test already waited for the same tab; its wait stays as is. The product-side follow-up (the session is rebound before the save and not rolled back on failure) is #16543. Evidence is in the triage block below. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:positron-notebooks @:quarto @:win The two suites that call `saveFileAs` should pass. The flake only reproduced on Windows CI timing, so the Windows job is the one that matters. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- The test deletes the saved notebook file before Positron's Save As pipeline has finished, which fails the save and orphans the kernel session, so the suite afterEach's wait for the session to exit times out. - **Test:** [Positron Notebooks: Save Settings > notebook.save.outputs=false removes outputs on save](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Positron%20Notebooks%3A%20Save%20Settings%20%3E%20notebook.save.outputs%3Dfalse%20removes%20outputs%20on%20save%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fnotebooks-positron%2Fnotebook-save-settings.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Pattern B/C: Session python-notebook- did not exit within 15000ms (afterEach in notebooks-positron/_test.setup.ts:55), win/electron - **Signal:** attempt-0 renderer.log (run 37824691953): 19:13:14.757 'Reassigning notebook session URI: untitled:Untitled-1.ipynb -> file:///.../test-save-outputs-t9o5be.ipynb'; 19:13:14.860 doSave(1) before write(); 19:13:14.894 handleSaveError(1) 'Unable to resolve nonexistent file'; 19:13:15.095 'Shutting down notebook untitled:Untitled-1.ipynb. Source: Notebook closed'; 19:13:15.107 'Aborting shutdown request for notebook untitled:Untitled-1.ipynb. No active session found'. Same sequence in the linked run 37789747889 (ENOENT stat at t=3465701, 160ms after the Save As OK click; first afterEach evaluate at t=3465677). - **Frequency:** 1/175 runs (0.6%) on main, win/electron - **Hypothesis:** saveFileAs returns as soon as the Save As dialog is accepted. The test's toPass reads the file the moment the bytes land, and the describe-level afterEach (Playwright runs inner afterEach first) unlinks it immediately. FileService.writeFile stats the file after writing, so the unlink in that window makes the save fail. PositronNotebookEditorInput.saveAs had already rebound the session from the untitled URI to the target URI and does not roll back on failure, so when Close All Editors discards the still-untitled notebook, shutdownNotebookSession(untitled URI) finds no session and the kernel session stays idle. Ruled out: kernel never started (log shows session started and bound), external-server dialog path (electron), timeout too short (session is never asked to exit).

title: e2e: stop the OS keyring modal from blocking Electron runs

`--password-store=basic` was set only inside Docker, so every other host still let Electron reach for a real keyring on launch. Both failure shapes are modal dialogs that intercept all input, hanging the run until someone dismisses one by hand.
