title: e2e failure analyzer: easier-to-read report, issue counts in Slack, newest Opus
description:
### Summary

Updates the e2e-failure-analyzer report to be more human readable and get information at a glance. Also update Claude sdk to get the latest Opus models.

**What changes in the report**

- **A one-line count at the top.** A colored box says what kind of issues the run had, e.g. "**1 product issue (suspected)**, 1 test issue. 2 tests passed on retry." It is red when there is a product issue, and a neutral note otherwise.
- **Color-coded categories.** Each row in the Summary table gets a dot (red = product, yellow = test, orange = flaky, blue = infra, white = unclassified), and the Root cause column shows just the category. A small legend sits under the table, along with the model, turns, and cost of the analysis.
- **One heading per failure**, with the same dot, instead of a long nested bullet list.
- **"What happened" first.** Each failure opens with one or two plain sentences anyone can follow: what the test was doing, what went wrong, and whether it is a product, test, or CI problem.
- **Action next, and short.** One next step and who owns it, in about 50 words.
- **Evidence is short, with the details folded away.** A one or two sentence summary, plus a collapsed "Evidence detail" section for the full reasoning.

**What changes in Slack**

The thread message now says what was found, counting each hard failure once (tests that passed on retry are left out):

- Before: `E2E failure analysis complete: View report`
- After: `E2E failure analysis complete. 1 product issue (suspected), 1 test issue. View report`

### Example

Real output from this branch, analyzing [run 37667303282](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/37667303282) ([full report](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/37834212681#summary-113507005999)). The first failure is shown below; the second follows the same layout.

<details><summary>Example report (click to expand)</summary>

> Analyzed [Test: Merge to branch run #37667303282](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/37667303282) on `main` -- commit `a15574a7` "drive-positron: 4 helper fixes from the nightly run (#16501)"

> [!CAUTION]
> **1 product issue (suspected)**, 1 test issue. 2 tests passed on retry.

## Summary

| | Test | Platform | Root cause |
|---|------|----------|------------|
| :red_circle: | Python - queue user input while interpreter is starting | e2e-chromium / ubuntu | suspected product regression |
| :yellow_circle: | R - Flags an installed package with an unscored CRAN advisory | e2e-chromium / ubuntu, e2e-electron / ubuntu | test logic bug |

<sub>:red_circle: product · :yellow_circle: test  |  Analysis run: `claude-opus-5-5`, 13 turns, $0.65</sub>

## Detailed Analysis

### :red_circle: Python - queue user input while interpreter is starting

<sub>e2e-chromium (ubuntu) · suspected product regression (low-medium confidence)</sub>

**What happened:** The test types a short Python command while the interpreter is still starting and expects it to run once the interpreter is ready. The command appeared in the console and a fresh prompt came back, but its output ("done") never showed up in 90 seconds, on both attempts. The output seems to have been lost somewhere in the product, not in the test.

**Action:** Console/runtime owners: in the Python Supervisor debug log, check whether the queued `execute_request` (`7c7e965a`) got back `stream` output and an `execute_reply`. If the output reached the frontend but was not shown, it is a console rendering bug. If no output came back, the queued request was mishandled during startup.

**Evidence:** In the failure-state screenshot of both attempts, the console shows `>>> import time; time.sleep(5); print("done");` with a new `>>>` prompt under it and no `done` line, about 90 seconds into a command that should take 5 seconds.

<details><summary>Evidence detail</summary>

(Full reasoning: test steps, timeline, log sequence, what was ruled out, and how the pass rate fits. See the full report link above.)

</details>

<sub>**Commit:** no related changes (only `.claude/skills/drive-positron` scripts) · **History:** 99% overall, ubuntu/chromium 96% (3 failed, 7 flaky). The pattern was first seen Oct 02, 8 days after the window opened Sep 24, with 15 occurrences since. That points to a real onset around Oct 02, not a long-standing flake.</sub>

</details>

title: Ship one shared copy of DuckDB instead of three
description:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Let's not merge until after we branch for 2026.10.

- Fixes #14265
- Addresses #16025

Before this PR, Positron shipped three copies of DuckDB. `positron-duckdb`, `positron-data-driver-duckdb`, and `positron-data-driver-pins` each had a copy, with a native library of about 110 MB. This PR changes the situation so we ship one shared copy. As a result, each platform build will be about 224 MB smaller.

The change is in packaging only. Each extension still installs its own copy, so `npm install` and dev builds do not change. When the build packages the extensions, it does these steps:

- It leaves `node_modules/@duckdb/**` and `node_modules/detect-libc/**` out of the three extensions.
- It copies one set of these packages (from `positron-duckdb`) to the shared `extensions/node_modules`. Node resolution from `dist/duckdbWorker.js` in each extension finds this copy.
- If the three extensions have different installed versions of `@duckdb/node-api` or `@duckdb/node-bindings`, it stops the build. One copy serves all three extensions, so the versions must be the same.

This PR also pins `@duckdb/node-api` to the exact version `1.5.5-r.3` in each package. It decreases the file-count budgets to match the new layout.

### Build check for the shared copy

If the shared copy is incomplete, the DuckDB worker cannot load DuckDB and would just stop, so the Data Explorer then shows an out-of-memory error for each query. PR E2E tests run from source, so they cannot find this problem.

For this reason, the packaged-tree check at the end of each desktop and server build now examines the shared copy for the build target. The build fails when one of these conditions occurs:

- The native binding for the target is missing.
- A binding for a different platform or architecture ships instead. A cross-build that staged the binding of the host could cause this kind of problem.
- One of the three extensions ships its own copy.
- A runtime dependency of the shared packages does not resolve in the shared `node_modules`. A DuckDB upgrade that adds a dependency would cause this problem.

The DuckDB helpers are in the new `build/lib/positron-duckdb-runtime.ts`, with  tests.

### Why the first attempt failed

This PR is the second attempt after #16480. That PR moved the dependency into `extensions/package.json`, which changed the install layout. This change broke two things:

- The Excel extension check in the postinstall script of `positron-duckdb` did not find `@duckdb/node-api`.
- The macOS x64 cross-build failed. The per-folder `--cpu` rule from #15086 applied to `extensions/`, which also contains `esbuild`.

This PR keeps the install layout of `main`, so these two problems do not occur.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Positron is about 224 MB smaller on each platform as it now ships one copy of the DuckDB library instead of three (#14265).

### Validation Steps

@:data-explorer @:duck-db @:connections

PR CI runs the e2e tests from source, so these tags run the tests that show that the dev layout still works. To test the packaged layout, do a release build:

1. Build the app, for example with `npm run gulp vscode-darwin-arm64`.
2. Make sure that the build log contains `DuckDB runtime ok` for the target.
3. In the built app, open a CSV or Parquet file in the Data Explorer.
4. Preview a DuckDB connection in the Connections pane.
5. Preview a pin in the Data Explorer.
6. Run the release builds on positron-builds for Linux, macOS (arm64 and x64), and Windows.

To run the new unit tests, run `node --test lib/test/positron-duckdb-runtime.test.ts` in the `build` folder.

On a local darwin-arm64 release build, the app has one `libduckdb.dylib`, and the DuckDB workers load it from the shared folder. The new check passes for the darwin-arm64 target. For the darwin-x64 target, it fails and names the missing x64 binding.

title: e2e: scope python.useBundledIpykernel: false to its own console spec
description:
Moves the "Console Pane: Alternate Python" test into its own spec, `console-python-alt-ipykernel.test.ts`, so that `python.useBundledIpykernel: false` applies only to that test. The main `console-python.test.ts` suite now runs with the bundled ipykernel, which is what Positron ships.

### Why

The alternate-Python test was added in #6407 and set `python.useBundledIpykernel` to `false` inside the test. The reorder in #10993 moved that setting ahead of the whole file, and #14282 made it an explicit worker-scoped `beforeApp` override. Since then every test in `console-python.test.ts` has started the primary Python session without the bundled ipykernel.

With the setting off, the CI primary session (Python 3.10.12) loads the image's ipykernel 7.3.0. That release has the shell-socket wedge tracked in #15060. The fix is in ipykernel 7.4.0, which requires Python 3.11. With the setting on, the session uses the bundled ipykernel 6.31.0, which is not affected.

This change restores the main suite to the shipped kernel on every lane without an image rebuild. The `kernelSupervisor.logLevel: 'trace'` override stays in `console-python.test.ts` so the #15060 diagnostics continue.

title: Add Data Explorer context to Assistant
description: Part of #8709. ### Summary Adds a new extension API, `positron.dataExplorer.getContext()`. It describes the Data Explorer in the active editor so Posit Assistant can use it as context: The context includes: - The data's display name, its shape before and after filtering, the active row filters, and the sort keys. - Where the data came from: the runtime session and language for console data, the file URI for file-backed data, or the connection name and driver for data previewed from a data connection. - The cell the cursor is on. Columns are identified by name and rows by label. - The current selection (cells, whole rows, or whole columns) with counts. Column names and row labels are included when there are 50 or fewer of them, and the selected values are included as TSV when the selection has 100 cells or fewer. This keeps large selections from flooding the prompt. To support this, the data grid gets a `getSelection()` method that returns the selection without expanding it into cells. The data connections service can now look up which connection a previewed dataset came from. > [!NOTE] > This PR only adds an API for Assistant; work is also required in Assistant to call the API to get the data and add it to the context. I've done that work in https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2681, but the PRs can be merged in any order. ### Release Notes #### New Features - Posit Assistant now knows about the active Data Explorer, including its data source, filters, sorting, cursor, and selection (#8709) #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:data-explorer Unit tests in `positronDataExplorerInstance.vitest.ts` cover small and large selections.

title: Stop false "did not respond" warnings in the Quarto log for R and Python cells
description:
Fixes #16015

The R and Python language clients in Positron filter diagnostics for Quarto virtual documents (`.vdoc.*` files). The filter came from #11225, and at the time it was to keep vdoc diagnostics out of the Problems pane (quarto-dev/quarto#855). Later, the Quarto extension was updated to use vdocs for cell diagnostics. Quarto waits for a diagnostics change on each vdoc. Because the filter drops the publish, no change would ever arrive and after 10 seconds, Quarto writes this warning to its log:

```log
[EmbeddedDiagnostics] Language server for r did not respond within 10000ms for quarto-diagnostics-check.qmd
```

The warning has no effect on the user, but it confused the triage of other bug reports.

This PR changes the filter in both extensions. The filter now publishes an empty set of diagnostics for the vdoc, and it does not drop the publish. Quarto gets the change event, reads zero diagnostics, and logs no timeout. The Problems pane still shows no vdoc entries. The filter cannot pass the real diagnostics to Quarto instead because Quarto reads diagnostics from the diagnostic collections, and the Problems pane shows everything in those collections. As a result, the vdoc diagnostics would also show in the Problems pane, under the path of a temp file. In #11225 we found that these entries stay after Quarto erases the temp file (quarto-dev/quarto#855).

With the default settings, Quarto does not create vdocs for R or Python cells anymore! 🎉  Positron serves the cell language features from the hidden notebook (#16211). Thus this fix applies only when `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native` is `false`.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Quarto no longer logs a false "did not respond" warning for R and Python cells when `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native` is off (#16015)

### Validation Steps

@:quarto @:problems

1. Set `"quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native": false` in your settings.
2. Open a `.qmd` file that has R and Python code cells.
3. Start an R console and a Python console.
4. Edit a code cell, then wait 10 seconds.
5. Open the Quarto output channel. Make sure that it shows no `did not respond within 10000ms` warning.
6. Make sure that the Problems pane shows no `.vdoc.*` entries.

This PR adds no automated test. The middleware is built inside `activate()` and needs a running language server, so a unit test is not practical.

title: Recheck environment setup after trusting a workspace
description:
Fixes #16136

After you trust a workspace, the Environment Setup card on the Welcome page now checks Python and R again. Before this, it kept saying "The Python extension is not available" until the window reloaded.

### Why it got stuck

The Python extension does not run in an untrusted workspace, so the first check finds no extension. Trusting the workspace turns the extension on without a reload, but nothing told the card to check again. Reopening the Welcome tab did not help either: the service skips the rerun when it sees the same welcome page.

### The fix

`EnvironmentHealthService` now listens for extensions being added and removed:

- When a language's extension is removed, it reruns that language's check right away. The card shows "not available".
- When a language's extension is added, it waits for the extension to activate, then reruns.

The wait matters. The extension service announces an added extension before the extension host has loaded it. Calling the health check command at that point fails with "command not found", and the card shows "The Python check could not be completed". I hit this in the app on my first attempt. The unit tests could not catch it, because they stub the extension service.

The new listeners do nothing until a welcome page has opened. If you never open one, this change never starts the Python or R extension.

The same path should also cover enabling, disabling, or installing the Python or R extension without a reload. I did not test those by hand.

### Screenshots

**BEFORE**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f82f50cc-cb1d-49fe-abd7-93bb149cd086

**AFTER**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12c40438-f197-4f6e-936f-2b52bc0f2e8c

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- The Environment Setup card on the Welcome page now updates after you trust a workspace, instead of saying the Python extension is not available (#16136)

### Validation Steps

@:welcome

1. Open a folder you have not trusted, and choose not to trust it, so the window is in Restricted Mode.
2. Run **Help: Welcome**. Both rows in Environment Setup say the extension is not available.
3. In the Console pane, click **Trust this folder**, then **Trust**.
4. Within a few seconds the card shows results for Python and R.

title: test: dismiss the clear-editor-history confirm on Workbench and Jupyter lanes
description:
Follow-up to #16498. That PR added `workbench.action.clearEditorHistory` to the R Plots `beforeEach` so the Save Plot dialog defaults to the workspace root. The command works on the Electron and Positron Web lanes but breaks the Workbench lane, where it failed the first R plots test on the [positron-builds daily](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/37789747889/job/113353742833). ### Summary `workbench.action.clearEditorHistory` always asks for confirmation. On the Electron and Positron Web lanes the e2e harness starts Positron with `--enable-smoke-test-driver`, and under that flag the dialog service auto-confirms, so the command runs silently. The Workbench and Jupyter lanes attach to a server that Posit Workbench started without the flag. There the confirmation dialog stays open over the workbench and blocks the next `executeCode` call, which waits for the console quick input until the test times out. `openFileQuickAccessAndWait` already handled this case by clicking the dialog's Clear button on served sessions. This PR moves that logic into a new `QuickAccess.clearEditorHistory()` helper and calls it from both places. The helper also: - matches port 8888 (Jupyter) in addition to 8080 and 8787, since the same test is tagged for that lane - waits for the Clear button before clicking it, instead of clicking immediately The no-confirm variant of the command is not an option. Its precondition is the same automation context key that the Workbench lane lacks. Verified against a local Workbench stack (`npm run pwb`): with the fix reverted, `R - Verify basic plot functionality` fails at `console.ts:144` with the quick input hidden, the same error as CI. With the fix it passes, and the trace shows the Clear button being waited for and clicked. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:plots @:workbench @:jupyter The Workbench and Jupyter lanes exercise the dialog dismissal. The plots lane on Electron covers the save test, which still passes `collapseFirst` and depends on the history clear. Not run through the local PETE preview; the PR touches test files only. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- The clear-editor-history command's confirmation dialog is auto-confirmed under the smoke-test driver, which the Electron and Positron Web lanes set, but not on the Workbench and Jupyter lanes, which attach to an externally started server. The dialog blocks the console quick input. Fix: dismiss the dialog on served sessions, as openFileQuickAccessAndWait already did. - **Test:** Plots > R Plots > R - Verify basic plot functionality - **Targeted failure:** `expect(locator('.quick-input-widget .quick-input-box input')).toBeVisible()` at `pages/console.ts:144`, 120s test timeout, Workbench lane - **Signal:** `dialogService.skipDialogs()` returns true only when `enableSmokeTestDriver` is set; the Workbench harness connects to `http://localhost:8787` without starting the server. Local Workbench run: red without the fix with the CI error, green with it, Clear button click present in the trace. - **Frequency:** First seen on the positron-builds daily of 2026-10-08, the first Workbench run after #16498 merged. - **Hypothesis:** Falsified and confirmed locally as above.

title: e2e: add the python test tag and audit ark tag coverage
description:
Adds a `python` e2e test tag so that all Python test cases can run in one CI run, the same way the `ark` tag runs all R test cases. Also audits the `ark` tag, which had drifted since #8331.

### Summary

**New `python` tag.** The tag is added to the feature tags in `test-tags.ts` and applied to every e2e test that starts a Python session, runs Python code, or selects a Python notebook kernel. Placement follows the same rules the `ark` tag uses:

- describe level when every test in the file uses Python
- test level in mixed files
- on the Python entry in parameterized configs (console clipboard, unsaved script, plot attribution, data explorer clipboard, pins and performance, convert-to-code, the startup and execution perf suites, the Python memory scenarios, and the Python assistant eval cases)

The `extensions/positron-python/` path now maps to the new tag in `test-tag-paths-map.json`, so a PR that touches the extension runs the Python set. This mirrors the existing `extensions/positron-r/` mapping to the `ark` tag.

**`ark` tag audit.** 78 R tests added since #8331 had no `ark` tag. They now have it. The gaps were mostly in the Quarto inline output suites, Positron notebooks, data explorer, sessions, variables, packages pane and help. The one test-level `ark` tag in `session-state.test.ts` moved up to the describe, since all three tests there use R.

Counts in the `e2e-electron` project:

| Tag | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ark` | 129 tests in 60 files | 207 tests in 98 files |
| `python` | none | 273 tests in 119 files |

**Scope notes**

- The reticulate suites carry both tags. They start a Python kernel through R.
- Tests that only mention a language without starting it are not tagged. Examples: the help landing page, the folder-template visibility tests, the enforced-settings `.py` save test, and the SQLite data-connections code-variant tests.
- The tags on tests under `workbench/`, `connect/`, `remote-ssh/` and `remote-wsl/` do not run those tests on their own. Those directories are excluded from the default Playwright projects and their lanes are gated on their own lane tags. The tags there are for local runs and nightly jobs. This matches how the `ark` tag already behaves in those directories.
- `histogram-rounding.test.ts` was space-indented, which the precommit hook rejects. It is reformatted. The only non-whitespace change in that file is its new tag.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

Tag metadata only. The CI run proves that both tags select their tests and that every tagged file still loads. Locally:

#### finder-start-session-no-match-shown-omits-language: fixed

- **What broke:** When `start-session.sh --name` matched nothing, the error listed other languages' interpreters and left out some of the requested ones, so --name could not be corrected.
- **Why:** It reported only the first rows drawn in the interpreter picker, whatever their language, and the picker draws only the rows that fit on screen.
- **Fix:** On no match, it reads the whole picker, lists every interpreter of the requested language, and says to pass one of their words as --name.
- **Review:** sent back once and still asks for changes: The same mistake is left in the nb.sh kernel picker. dp-nb.ts:199 (`pick-kernel`) calls `lib.pick` and returns its error unchanged. pick's `shown` (page-lib.ts:256-258) is the first 8 drawn rows of any language, so a `--name` that matches no kernel hides the Python and R kernels below the screen. This is the same virtual-list cut and the same missing guidance that the finding describes. The fixer left it as is. Either apply the same walk there, or move the filter-to-language listing into one shared helper that both callers use. At present the logic sits inline in dp-console.ts:61-68, so any second caller would copy it.; The new `more` output key is not documented. dp-console.ts:67 adds `more: 'the picker lists more rows than were read'` to the failure JSON. The start-session.sh header (line 30) mentions only `shown`. CONTRIBUTING.md says every output fact belongs in the header, and `check.ts` compares header and output. Add `more` to the header text at start-session.sh:27-32.
- **Checked:** failed 2 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Cause: in dp-console.ts start-session's choose(), when --name matched no row the helper returned lib.pick's error unchanged. pick's `shown` is show(all) in page-lib.ts, which is the first 8 rows drawn by the virtual list, of any language. So rows below the screen (Python 3.12.3 (System) or 3.10.12 (Global)) were left out, R and Zed rows were included, and the error did not say how to fix --name. Revised after review: lib.pick is back to exactly what it was, so there is no second 'no row on screen matches' error form. palette-run, open-file, ui.sh pick, nb.sh kernel and terminal-run keep their old failure path: same error text, same speed, no key presses, and dp-palette's 'no row matches' tests and similar-commands read are untouched. That settles all four review notes. A shared marker (note 3) is not needed because only one no-match form exists again. The new walker, lib.allRows() in page-lib.ts, is still a shared helper. It walks the virtual quick-input list with ArrowDown, reading the drawn rows at each step until focus wraps, and puts focus back on a list that does not loop. Only start-session calls it, and only when --name was given and pick said 'no row matches'. start-session then keeps the rows of the requested language and answers: '--name "X" matches no Python interpreter the picker could pick; pass words from one of the rows in "shown" as --name, in the order the row shows them, such as its version', with shown set to every such row (plus `more` if the walk did not ...

#### finder-ui-click-trailing-icon-name: fixed

- **What broke:** `ui.sh click` (and fill, check, choose) could not find a button by the name `ui.sh read` showed when that name ended in an icon, such as a notebook's "Positron Notebook" picker.
- **Why:** Name matching ignored an icon glyph before the name but not after it, while the read output hides both.

#### finder-palette-first-keystroke-lost-after-folder-template: product bug

- **What broke:** After the New Folder from Template dialog is closed, `palette-run.sh` fails once with 'the Command Palette did not open'; the next call works.
- **Why:** Positron's quick input closes itself the first time it reopens after a dialog it was moved into goes away, so the palette flashes shut.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** palette-run.sh reports Positron faithfully. The cause is in Positron-owned code in src/vs/platform/quickinput/browser/quickInputController.ts, inside a '--- Start Positron ---' block (the file is upstream, the block is Positron's): handlePositronModal(). The palette that ran 'New Folder from Template...' was still in the DOM when the dialog opened, so the quick input widget got reparented into .positron-dynamic-modal-dialog-box (seen while the dialog was open: the widget's parent is the dialog box). The code also attached a MutationObserver to the dialog box: 'close the quick pick if the modal closed'. Closing the dialog removes the whole overlay, which leaves the dialog box's childList unchanged, so the observer never fires and stays connected, and the widget is left detached (after Close, no .quick-input-widget is in the document). On the next Ctrl+Shift+P, show() -> getUI() -> handlePositronModal() appends the widget back to the workbench container. That append takes it out of the detached dialog box, the stale observer then sees !modalContainer.contains(ui.container) and calls this.hide(), so the palette closes during the same keystroke that opened it. The observer disconnects after that, which is why the second press works. Evidence: a capture listener sees Control, Shift and p reach the workbench and showCommands consume p (defaultPrevented), and a body MutationObserver sees the widget re-added and then left at display:none. Nothing changed: retrying the press in palett...

The first palette-run --dry-run 'View: Toggle Terminal' failed with 'the Command Palette did not open', and the second one returned ok. While the dialog was open, the .quic...

title: Keep a notebook session's language server on the notebook after "Save As"
description:
Addresses the first part of #16151

When you save an untitled notebook or rename a notebook, Positron moves its session to the new URI with `updateNotebookSessionUri`. Before this PR, only the main thread knew about the new URI. The R and Python language clients run in the extension host. They select the cells that they serve, and claim Quarto cells, from the session metadata that they get when they activate. After a **Save As**, they continued to select the old notebook.

This PR sends the new URI to the extension host and restarts the language client of the session so that it follows the notebook:

- `ILanguageRuntimeSession` and `positron.LanguageRuntimeSession` get an optional `updateNotebookUri` method. A new `$updateNotebookUriLanguageRuntime` RPC carries the change, in the same pattern as `$updateSessionNameLanguageRuntime`.
- `updateNotebookSessionUri` calls the method after it commits the new mapping. The call is not awaited, because the language client restart can take seconds and the **Save As** flow awaits this method before it writes the file. A failure in the extension host is logged and does not roll back the mapping.
- The R and Python sessions restart only the LSP, in one task on the session queue. The LSP stops while the metadata still has the old URIs, so it releases the old Quarto claim. Then the session writes the new URIs and starts the LSP again. The DAP does not change.
- Reticulate sessions forward the call to the Python session that they wrap. (This PR also corrects an old localization lint error in the same reticulate file.)

For Quarto documents, this is the first part of the fix needed for #16151. The Quarto kernel does not follow a Save As yet, and I'll handle that in a later PR.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Notebook language features, such as completions and diagnostics, continue to work after you save an untitled notebook or rename a notebook (#16151)

### Validation Steps

@:console @:sessions @:notebooks @:positron-notebooks @:quarto @:reticulate @:variables

1. Create a new untitled notebook with an R kernel. Run `x <- 1`.
2. Save the notebook to a file.
3. In a new cell, type `x` and trigger completions. Also type a syntax error, something like `y <- c(1, 2`.
4. Make sure that completions and diagnostics work, and that `x` is still in the Variables pane. The kernel output for the session shows `Stopping LSP` and then `Starting LSP` one time.
5. Do steps 1 to 4 again with a Python kernel. The kernel output shows `Stopping Positron LSP server, reason: notebook URI changed`.
6. Rename a saved notebook in the Explorer while its kernel runs. The result is the same as in step 4.
7. Use an R console and a Python console during these steps. Their LSPs should _not_ restart.

Note that I ran into https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16502 while doing manual validation here. Be sure to keep the interpreter that the notebook selects at first.

title: Fall back to Run when a gutter test click asks for an unsupported profile
description:
Fixes #14667

Holding Alt over an editor gutter test icon swapped it to a debug icon, and Alt+click requested a Debug run, even when the test's controller has no Debug profile. R tests only register a Run profile, so the click silently did nothing. A plain click did the same when `testing.defaultGutterClickAction` was set to `debug` or `runWithCoverage`.

The gutter now checks the test's controller capabilities (`ITestProfileService.capabilitiesForTest`), the same check the gutter's right-click menu already uses:

- A plain click whose Debug or Coverage group the controller can't run falls back to Run.
- An Alt+click whose group the controller can't run does the same thing as a plain click, and the icon no longer swaps while Alt is held.
- The hover tooltip describes what the click will actually run.
- Decorations refresh when test profiles change.

Tests whose controller supports Debug and Coverage (e.g. Python) behave exactly as before.

The decision logic lives in a new Positron helper, `common/positronGutterClickAction.ts`, with a Vitest snapshot test. The upstream `testingDecorations.ts` only gets marked call-site edits.

This doesn't change the Debug and Coverage buttons in the Testing view's title bar for R. That's #14592, which has a different cause (positron-python's always-on test controller) and needs a separate fix.

Known limitation (upstream behavior, unchanged): after changing `testing.defaultGutterClickAction`, gutter icons and tooltips update on the next reload.

**Upstream conflict note:**

I am not confident this is the correct approach w.r.t. the size of the upstream changes. I think we could simplify the upstream changes, but there are some tradeoffs. Basically, this PR rewrites the logic. We could refactor it to keep the existing logic but rewrite the effective action. The tradeoff is that changing the logic will cause merge conflicts, but changing the effective action might silently change behavior if the logic changes because there would be no merge conflict. We should likely defer to whomever is handling upstream merges.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Editor gutter test icons no longer switch to a non-working Debug action on Alt/Option for tests that can't be debugged, such as R tests; clicking them runs the test (#14667)

### Validation Steps

@:test-explorer

In an R package that uses testthat (e.g. `qa-example-content/workspaces/r_testing`):

1. Open the Testing view, expand a test file, and open it so the gutter shows run icons.
2. Hold Alt/Option: the icons should not change to the debug icon.
3. Alt+click an icon: the test runs.
4. Set `testing.defaultGutterClickAction` to `debug`, then `runWithCoverage` (reload after each). A plain click runs the test, and the tooltip says "Click to run tests".

In a Python project with pytest (e.g. `qa-example-content/workspaces/python_testing`): holding Alt still swaps to the debug icon, and Alt+click still debugs.

description:
### Summary

Bumps `@playwright/test` to 1.64.0 and pins the e2e setup action to the lockfile, so a new Playwright release can't break CI lanes overnight again.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:critical @:web @:win

1.64 now treats elements inside hidden iframes as hidden, which could affect webview checks; the tags above cover that. Memory metrics dispatched on this branch: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/37764588813

#### finder-glued-flag-read-as-command: fixed

- **What broke:** `debug.sh`, `plots.sh` and the other bash helpers rejected `--timeout=5`-style flags, calling a valid command wrong or the flag unknown.
- **Why:** The bash helpers only understood a flag and its value as two words; only --session accepted the joined form the other helpers take.
- **Fix:** Every bash helper now reads `--flag=value` as the flag and its value, and a static check catches a new flag that does not.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Helper bug in every bash argument loop. Their case statements matched value flags only as two words (debug.sh: `--condition)`, `--log)`, `--timeout)`; plots.sh: `--format)`, `--width)`, `--height)`, `--name)`); a glued --timeout=5 or --format=png fell through to `*) ARGS+=("$1")` and became the command word, so the error was 'command: ...'. The strict loops refused it as 'unknown argument --x=y' instead: stop.sh, listeners.sh, reseed.sh, launch.sh, run-venv.sh and view-read.sh. Only --session (and --max in quickpick-enum.sh) had a glued case. dp.ts parse() accepts --flag=value for every flag and suggests it in its own error. The bash helpers share no parser, so the fix is one uniform first case in each loop, `--a=*|--b=*) set -- "${1%%=*}" "${1#*=}" "${@:2}" ;;`. It splits a glued known value flag into the two-word form the existing case already handles, so the value checks and messages stay the same ('--session=' still says '--session needs a value'). It replaces the per-flag --session=* and --max=* cases. It reaches debug.sh, plots.sh, listeners.sh, monaco-paste.sh, quickpick-enum.sh, view-read.sh, viewer.sh, launch.sh, reseed.sh, run-venv.sh and stop.sh. In debug.sh and plots.sh, an unknown flag in the command position now gets 'unknown flag --x; see --help ...' instead of the command list. To stop the next sibling from regressing, I added a new check, `args`, to test/check.ts. It fails when a bash loop has a case for a value flag (one whose case uses `shift 2`) but no '--...

#### finder-listeners-empty-file-exits-0: fixed

- **What broke:** `listeners.sh` said "no new listener" (exit 0) when its saved list was missing, empty or unwritable, and printed raw shell errors instead of a clear message.
- **Why:** It never checked that the saved list could be written or read, and an empty saved list made every live listener look already seen.
- **Fix:** An empty or bad file path is now refused with one sentence and exit 2, and an empty saved list no longer hides new listeners.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and the smoke views section pass with it (the next nightly runs all of smoke).

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** listeners.sh took any value for --save/--diff/--tree (FILE="${2:-}" and TREE="${2-}" in the argument loop) and never checked the file I/O: --save ran `list > "$FILE"; wc -l < "$FILE" | ... | sed`, so a failed redirect printed bash's raw error twice and the pipeline's last command (sed) gave exit 0 with nothing saved; --diff ran `awk ... "$FILE" -`, whose 'cannot open' error was lost inside $(...), so NEW was empty and the script exited 0, the header's 'no new listener'. Same root cause: the saved list was used without reading it first. title: e2e analyzer: tell stalled from slow, and show the history window
description:
### Summary

The e2e failure analyzer misdiagnosed "R - Flags an installed package with an unscored CRAN advisory" in three main runs on Oct 7 (for example run 37660037141). pak's `apt-get -y update` was stuck against the Ubuntu mirrors. The analyzer called it an "under-budgeted wait" and recommended raising the timeout, which can't fix a step that never returns. The real fix was to take apt out of the test's path (#16509).

This PR makes two changes:

- **Rubric** (`.claude/skills/e2e-failure-analyzer/rubric.md`):
  - A wait is "under-budgeted" only if there is evidence the work was still progressing. If it stalled, stop looking at the budget and name the step it stalled on.
  - A wait spent inside an external network step the feature doesn't need (a package index, a clone, a download) is an external dependency in the test's path. The fix is to remove that step, not wait longer. This applies whether the step stalled or was merely slow.
  - The rule that a log going quiet points at the product gets an exception for the app being blocked on an external process.
  - A first-seen date well after `window_start` (for example "Started today" in a 14-day window) is a real onset, not a censored date.
- **analyze.mjs:** `renderHistoryForTest` read `lookback_days`/`branch` from each test entry, but the history API reports them only at the top level. So every test's history line said `last ? days, branch ?`. The window (now including `window_start`) is carried onto each entry, so the onset sits next to its bounds.

### Validation

I replayed run 37660037141 locally through the **real** `analyze.mjs` using the pinned Agent SDK (0.2.141), `MODEL=opus`, `MAX_TURNS=40`, and a clean environment. Thinking was off unless noted, as in CI. There were 2 runs per cell.

| Cell | Verdict on the widgetframe failure | Recommended fix |
|---|---|---|
| Unchanged, thinking off (matches CI) | under-budgeted wait, 2 of 2 | raise the timeout to 120-180s, 2 of 2 |
| This PR, thinking off | test logic bug: external dependency in the test's path, 2 of 2 | remove the apt step (`PKG_SYSREQS=false`, pre-provision, or a different package), 2 of 2 |
| Unchanged, thinking on | under-budgeted 1, test environment issue 1 | still includes extending the budget |
| Control: this PR, thinking off, run 36640097665 (Python `cowsay` install) | flaky, same as CI, 2 of 2 | no stall or external-dependency claim |

- The unchanged cell reproduces CI's wrong verdict, so the comparison is meaningful.
- This PR flips the verdict and the recommended fix.
- The control is another Packages-pane install that was not stalled. The new rule did not over-correct on it.
- Turning on extended thinking alone did not fix the recommendation. Thinking stays disabled (claude-code#63192 is still open).

The window fix is a smaller gain: it read the onset correctly in 1 of 2 runs with thinking off, versus 0 of 2 without it.

No e2e tests are affected. These files only drive the CI analyzer.

#### finder-editor-timeout-not-a-number-accepted: fixed

- **What broke:** `editor.sh` suggest, hover and definition accepted a nonsense `--timeout` and, without waiting, blamed the language server for not answering.
- **Why:** The timeout was read as a plain number, so a word or negative value made the wait end before it started.
- **Fix:** A timeout that is not a positive number of seconds is now refused as a usage error, in editor, notebook, Quarto, Viewer, window and ui helpers alike.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** dp-editor.ts passed `timeout: Number(p.flags.timeout ?? 5)` to the suggest/hover/definition page function. Number('abc') is NaN (JSON-serialized as null) and '-1' is -1, so the wait loop `Date.now() < end` ended at once and the helper reported 'no hover showed within null s ... no language server answered' (exit 1), or suggest answered ok with no list. The same unchecked Number() on a duration was in dp-nb.ts (--timeout), dp-window.ts (--timeout, so reload ran then reported a false failure), dp-ui.ts (--wait, so the diff was taken at once), dp-qmd.ts (wait N SECS) and dp-viewer.ts (wait-content SECS). Fix in the shared code: dp-lib.ts seconds() now delegates to a new secondsOf(value, name, fallback) that also serves positional durations; editor.sh (suggest/hover/definition --timeout, read before --at moves the cursor), nb.sh --timeout, window.sh --timeout, ui.sh --wait, qmd.sh wait N SECS (checked before the active editor is read) and viewer.sh wait-content SECS all go through it, so a non-positive or non-numeric value is a usage error (exit 2) with nothing done. ui.sh watch --for/--every already range-checked and are unchanged; console-run.sh and start-session.sh already used seconds() and are unchanged. Headers of the six helpers say so. Valid input: positive numbers behave exactly as before (checked hover --timeout 5 and 1.5, qmd wait 1 5 and wait 1, nb wait --timeout 5). Behavior change: a value of 0 (or empty) for editor/nb/window --timeout, ui --wait, qmd wait SECS and ...

- finder, fail: same three results

After the fix: abc, -1, '' and 0 each give...

''`), and unknown flags were only refused when the caller passed the optional `switches` list, which notifications and 15 other commands did not. dp-notifications.ts then read `String(p.flags.click ?? '')`, so bare --click, --click '' and --clera all fell through to the plain listing with exit 0. Fix, in shared code: parse() now always refuses a flag that is in neither withValue nor switches (--help always allowed), and refuses a value flag with no value after it ('--X needs a value', exit 2); every dp.ts command now passes its switches (start-session new, nb replace, notifications clear, palette-run dry-run, plots editor, run-app list, settings user/workspace, shot list, terminal-run read, ui partial/right/enter; console-run/console-read/panel already did). Text flags read as String(p.flags.X ?? '') now go through the existing textFlag() so an explicit empty value (--X '', --X=) is exit 2 too: notifications --click/--match, de-read --title, nb --notebook, qmd --file, run-app --label, shot --view, terminal-run --key, tree --view, ui --in/--watch, viewer --view. Split its number check out of the flag lookup and use that here, instead of copying the logic.; dp-qmd.ts:377: `qmd.sh wait N SECS` uses `Number(a2 ?? 60)` for its timeout, the same mistake. `wait 2 abc` makes `seconds` NaN. title: Let agents list the apps Positron runs, and stop them
description:
Fixes #15940
Fixes #15941

### Summary

An agent could start a Data App but couldn't tell whether it was up or where it was serving, and couldn't stop it. positron-run-app now keeps a record of every app it runs and exposes it through two agent commands. Posit Assistant runs them with its existing `positronCommand` tool.

| Command | What it does | Asks first? |
|---|---|---|
| `positronRunApp.listApps` | Each app's file, framework and status (`starting`, `running`, `exited`, or `unknown` without shell integration). Also its exit code and two URLs: `url` for the user (the proxied address on Posit Workbench) and `localUrl` for requests from inside the session, such as `curl`. | No (read-only) |
| `positronRunApp.stopApp` | Sends Ctrl+C to the app's terminal, or interrupts its console session. If a terminal app is still running 5 seconds later, closes its terminal, which ends the process. Closes the app's Viewer preview once it has stopped. | Yes |

- Covers apps run with the Python framework commands (Dash, FastAPI, Flask, Gradio, marimo, Streamlit) and Shiny for R, whether an agent or the user started them.
- **Not covered: Shiny for Python.** The Shiny extension starts those apps in its own terminal, outside positron-run-app, so they aren't listed. Until that changes, `shiny.stopApp` stops them, and the skill says so. posit-dev/shiny-vscode#114 tracks moving them onto positron-run-app's `runApplication`. The Positron API changes it needed, `cwd` and a `command`/`args` form, landed in #15155. Once a Shiny release with that change ships, these apps show up here with no change to Positron.
- Also not listed: apps started under the debugger, and apps started before the window last reloaded, since the record is kept in memory.

**Waiting for an app's URL now ends when the app exits.** This applies to both the terminal and console paths. An app that fails to start no longer holds the run open, progress notification and all, until URL detection times out. A Shiny for R app that errors on startup no longer shows a "URL detection timed out" warning. This fixes the console half of posit-dev/shiny-vscode#123, and lets an agent stop an app that is still starting and run it again straight away.

**`readOnly` for extension commands.** The `agent` block of `contributes.commands` gains `readOnly`, matching the flag core commands already have, so an extension can mark a command that an agent may run without asking. `listApps` uses it.

**Skill.** The positron-commands skill's `interactive-apps.md` now tells agents:

- to check an app with `listApps` after running it, and what each status means;
- which URL to give the user;
- how to stop an app.

It also corrects the claim that `shiny.stopApp` stops any Shiny app. In Positron it stops only Shiny for Python, because Shiny for R apps run in the console.

Related: #16428 lets Assistant run `shiny.r.runApp`, which Positron reported as disabled for agents. It isn't on this branch.

### Demo


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d899ba23-b0e6-4a97-89b4-5bdfc3916630



### Release Notes

#### New Features

- AI agents such as Posit Assistant can now see which Data Apps are running, with their status and URL, and stop them (#15940, #15941)

#### Bug Fixes

- Running a Data App that fails to start no longer waits out the URL detection timeout before giving up

### Validation Steps

@:apps @:web @:win @:workbench

Use Posit Assistant outside Ask mode. This branch doesn't include #16428, so start Shiny for R apps with the Run App button.

1. Ask Assistant to run a Streamlit or Flask app and tell you whether it's up and at what URL. It should call `positronRunApp.listApps` without asking, and report the app `running` with its URL. On Workbench the URL should be the proxied address, not `localhost`.
2. Ask it to stop the app. It should ask first. Then the terminal shows `^C`, the Viewer clears, and `listApps` reports the app `exited`.
3. Start a Shiny for R app with the Run App button, then ask Assistant to stop it. The console session should be interrupted and the Viewer cleared.
4. Run a Flask app that has an error in it. The run should end at once rather than after the detection timeout, and `listApps` should report `exited` with a non-zero exit code.

Test coverage:

- `appRegistry.vitest.ts` covers:
  - each status;
  - URLs;
  - re-runs under the same name;
  - stopping: interrupt, terminate, an interrupt or terminate that fails, an app that has already exited, and an unknown file.
- `menusExtensionPoint.vitest.ts` covers `readOnly`.
- The extension-host tests in `api.test.ts` use real terminals. They cover:
  - listing a running app and stopping it with Ctrl+C;
  - an app that exits on its own;
  - stopping a console app;
  - ending the run when the app exits before printing its URL.
- **The positron-run-app extension-host suite doesn't run in CI.** `scripts/test-integration.sh` has it commented out as flaky. I ran it locally on Windows, and all the new tests pass. The one failure is a Windows quoting expectation in `commandLine.test.ts`, which this PR doesn't touch.

title: spawn interpreter with metadata via settings
description:
Fixes #12081
Fixes #14767

### Summary

Adds an `interpreters.definitions` setting for defining extra R and Python interpreters. Each entry names an interpreter by `path` and gives it a label, an optional set of environment variables, and an optional startup script. This gives users a supported way to handle custom launch setups, which people have been approximating with workarounds. It is modeled on the per-version extended definitions in Workbench's `r-versions`.

Also adds `interpreters.discovery` (language-overridable). Setting it to `definitionsOnly` turns off all other interpreter discovery for that language, so only the interpreters in `interpreters.definitions` are available.

```json
"interpreters.definitions": [
  {
    "language": "python",
    "path": "/opt/python/3.11.13/bin/python",
    "label": "My new environment",
    "env": { "LOADED_IN_ENV": "yes" },
    "startupScript": "~/code/positron/load-modules.sh"
  }
]
```

How it works:
- Each entry whose `language` and `path` exactly match a registered interpreter becomes a separate interpreter (a variant), with its own stable runtime ID, next to the original. The original stays available.
- If discovery doesn't find the interpreter at `path`, R and Python resolve it directly. The base interpreter is hidden and only the variant is shown.
- Variants update when the setting changes, with a reload. 
- When a session starts or restarts, the supervisor reads the current entry. It sources `startupScript` once in `/bin/sh` (a leading `~` is expanded), starting from the kernel's environment plus the entry's `env`. It captures every variable the script sets or changes and applies them, together with `env`, over the kernel's environment. If the script exits non-zero, the session fails to start and shows the script's error output. Variables the script unsets are not removed. Existing startup commands (conda, environment modules, r-versions) are unchanged and still run as before.
- The same variables are applied to terminals while a variant console is in the foreground. Additions to variables like `PATH` are applied as prepends or appends, so other extensions' changes are kept. MCP's terminal variables, which share the collection, are left alone.
- If a stored or running session belongs to a variant whose entry was removed, it fails to start with a clear error instead of quietly falling back to the original interpreter. With `definitionsOnly`, a stored session for an interpreter not in the definitions also fails to start.
- Startup scripts are not supported on Windows (they need a POSIX shell). There, only `env` is applied, and the skipped script is logged.
- `interpreters.definitions` is machine-scoped, so it can only be set in user or remote settings, not in workspace settings. Changing `interpreters.discovery` requires a restart.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- Added the `interpreters.definitions` setting for defining additional R and Python interpreters with custom environment variables and a startup script (#12081)
- Added the `interpreters.discovery` setting; `definitionsOnly` limits a language's interpreters to the ones in `interpreters.definitions` (#14767)

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:sessions

1. Add an entry to `interpreters.definitions` in user settings, using a `path` copied exactly from the interpreter picker, plus an `env` var and a `startupScript` that exports another variable (e.g. `export FROM_SCRIPT=1`).
2. Open the interpreter picker. Both the original interpreter and the new labeled one should be listed.
3. Start a session with the labeled interpreter and confirm both variables are set (`Sys.getenv()` in R, `os.environ` in Python).
4. Reload the window. The session should reconnect or restart as the labeled interpreter.
5. Change the entry's `label`. The old variant should disappear from the picker and the new one should appear, with no reload.
6. Delete the entry and reload. Restoring the session should fail with "no longer defined in the interpreters.definitions setting" instead of starting the original interpreter.
7. (Windows) Confirm `env` is applied and the startup script is skipped (see the Kernel Supervisor output).


Here's a video of the behavior, where the startup script is just `export STARTUP_RAN=yes`

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a830de4-b96c-418b-a8d9-67a9d816317c

Showing envvars loaded in terminal + `"interpreters.discovery": "definitionsOnly"`

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00dacca3-6107-4212-aeb7-e9548d7746a5


Discovery in non-standard location


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c52ca230-51a3-4800-8c33-df5bbafdca4b

title: test: skip pak sysreqs in the R security-advisory e2e test
description:
### Summary Fixes a flake in "Packages Pane - Security Advisories > R - Flags an installed package with an unscored CRAN advisory" on ubuntu (electron and chromium). It started failing in most main merge runs on Oct 7 (for example run 37660037141). At the failure, the R console shows pak resolving `widgetframe 0.3.1` from cache. It prints `All system requirements are already installed`, then runs `Installing system requirements` / `apt-get -y update` anyway, and that step never returns. R sits at 0-1% CPU, so the install is waiting on the Ubuntu mirrors, not slow. The row never reaches the package list, and `expectPackageInList` times out. pak does this because its `sysreqs_update` option defaults to TRUE when `CI` is set. It refreshes a package's system requirements even when they are already installed. widgetframe has system requirements, so its install depends on the apt mirrors. The sibling R install test uses `cowsay`, which has none, and it has stayed clean over the same window. The test checks advisory rendering, not system requirements. So before installing, it now runs `options(pkg.sysreqs = FALSE)` in the R console. pak forwards `pkg.*` options to its worker process on every call (`remote()` in pak's `R/subprocess.R`). No timeouts change, and the Python test is untouched. ### QA Notes Test-only change. A local run can't exercise this path because Windows has no apt step, so CI on ubuntu is the real check. Because the failure is intermittent, one green run doesn't prove the fix; it's confirmed once failures stop showing up in main's history. ### Validation Steps @:packages-pane ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- pak on CI refreshes already-installed system requirements via apt-get update, which hung on the Ubuntu mirrors; widgetframe never finished installing - **Test:** [Packages Pane - Security Advisories > R - Flags an installed package with an unscored CRAN advisory](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Packages%20Pane%20-%20Security%20Advisories%20%3E%20R%20-%20Flags%20an%20installed%20package%20with%20an%20unscored%20CRAN%20advisory%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fpackages-pane%2Fpackages-pane-vulnerabilities.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed -- .positron-packages-list .packages-list-item-name hasText widgetframe (60000ms) - **Signal:** Console at failure: pak resolved widgetframe 0.3.1 from cache, printed "All system requirements are already installed", then "Installing system requirements" / Executing sh -c apt-get -y update, and printed nothing more for 60s with R at 0-1% CPU. Packages list was rendered throughout; the row never arrived because the install never returned. Sibling R test installing cowsay (no sysreqs) is 584/584 clean over the same window. - **Frequency:** 9/384 runs (2.3%) on main, ubuntu/electron, ubuntu/chromium, rhel/chromium - **Hypothesis:** infra

title: Toggle hidden preferred themes
description:
Fixes #10097

The _Preferences: Toggle between Light/Dark Themes_ command did nothing when the preferred theme was a theme that Positron hides from the theme picker, for example Dark Modern or Dark+. This PR moves the Positron theme filter out of a general service method, so that the filter applies only to the theme pickers.

I got pretty confused about this whole situation, so here's a little bit of background:

### Two kinds of hidden theme

Positron hides 14 upstream color themes from the theme picker. After #16447, these themes are in two groups:

| Group | Themes | Release builds | Dev builds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Installed but hidden | Dark Modern, Dark+, Visual Studio Dark, Light Modern, Light+, Visual Studio Light (from `theme-defaults`) | Installed | Installed |
| Not shipped | Abyss, Kimbie Dark, Monokai, Monokai Dimmed, Quiet Light, Red, Solarized Dark, Solarized Light | Not installed (#16447) | Installed |

This PR fixes the _first_ group. The second group does not ship, so no lookup can find those themes in a release build. For example, the issue's original setup (preferred dark theme = Monokai) still does not toggle in a release build. This is expected, and upstream VS Code also does nothing when the preferred theme is not installed.

### Cause

The filter was inside `IWorkbenchThemeService.getColorThemes()`. Many callers use this method, not only the pickers, so all of these callers lost the hidden themes:

- The toggle command looks up the preferred theme in `getColorThemes()`. When the preferred theme was hidden, the lookup found nothing, and the command did nothing. The filter always kept the active theme, so the toggle could change _from_ a hidden theme but never _to_ one.
- Getting Started, theme preview, and onboarding had the same silent failure.
- The settings schema got its list of themes from two places, one filtered and one not. The list that came last won. As a result, a hidden theme in `settings.json` sometimes showed "Theme is unknown or not installed", although the theme worked.

A theme set in `workbench.colorTheme` always applied correctly, because that path reads the theme registry directly and not `getColorThemes()`.

### What this PR changes

`getColorThemes()` returns all registered themes again, as in upstream. Positron applies the filter only where it shows our specially curated list:

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| _Preferences: Color Theme_ picker | Curated | Curated (no change) |
| Extension _Set Color Theme_ button and quick pick | Curated | Curated (the button is disabled when an extension has only hidden themes) |
| _Set Color Theme_ in the extension context menu | Curated | Curated |
| Toggle, Getting Started, theme preview, onboarding | Cannot find hidden themes | Find hidden themes |
| `settings.json` completions and validation, Settings editor dropdown | Inconsistent | All installed themes, as in upstream |

The settings change is a deliberate choice on my part. A curated settings list would give a false "unknown or not installed" warning for a theme that works, for example Dark Modern from imported VS Code settings. A longer dropdown in the `settngs.json` editing experience is a smaller problem than a false warning.

`workbenchThemeService.ts` now has no Positron changes. The filter is in `positronColorThemeFilter.ts`, and the three upstream call sites use it inside Positron markers.

This PR also adds a new "themes" feature tag for E2E tests. `positronColorThemeFilter.ts` maps to this tag, so a PR that changes the filter runs the new toggle test.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- _Preferences: Toggle between Light/Dark Themes_ now changes to a preferred theme that the theme picker hides, for example Dark Modern or Dark+ (#10097)

### Validation Steps

@:themes

Do these steps in a dev build. Step 4 uses the Abyss extension, which only dev builds include.

1. In `settings.json`, set these values:
   ```json
   "window.autoDetectColorScheme": false,
   "workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme": "Dark Modern",
   "workbench.colorTheme": "Default Positron Light"
   ```
   Run _Preferences: Toggle between Light/Dark Themes_. Make sure that Positron changes to Dark Modern. Run the command again. Make sure that Positron changes back to Positron Light.
2. Run _Preferences: Color Theme_. Make sure that the list does not show Dark Modern, Dark+, Light Modern, Light+, Visual Studio Dark, or Visual Studio Light. Then make Dark Modern the active theme and open the picker again. Make sure that the list shows Dark Modern.
3. In `settings.json`, set `"workbench.colorTheme": "Dark Modern"`. Make sure that the "Theme is unknown or not installed" warning does not show. Type a new value for this setting, and make sure that the completions include Dark Modern and the other hidden themes.
4. In the Extensions view, filter on `@builtin`.
   - Open _Default Themes_ and select _Set Color Theme_. Make sure that the list shows only the themes from step 2.
   - Right-click _Abyss_. Make sure that the menu does not show _Set Color Theme_.

title: Build session start reasons from the session and name the requesting extension
description:
### Summary Stacked on #16309. Merge that first. This PR changes how session start reasons are built, names the extension that asked for a session, and rewords the labels so they say who did what. - **Built from the session.** Callers pass only a start reason ID, plus the requesting extension when an extension asked. The session service writes the saved `startReason` text with the same label code the console info popup uses. `ISessionStartReasonValues` and `createSessionStartReason` are gone. - **Requesting extension.** When an extension starts, selects, restarts, or sends code to a session through a Positron API, the extension is recorded. The extension host supplies its ID, so an extension can't fake it. - **Who ran code.** A console started to run code says whether you ran it, it came from AI chat, or an extension ran it. - **Notebooks in preview tabs.** Positron holds back the kernel for a notebook in a preview or background tab until the tab is active and kept open. The session now keeps the reason it was held back for, such as the kernel being selected. Keeping the tab open only lets it start, so `notebookEditorActivated` is removed. - **Labels.** The #16309 labels are reworded to name the doer in plain words. - **Developer views.** The Runtimes view and the diagnostics report show the requesting extension. The diagnostics report lists each session's details on separate lines. Log lines add the start reason ID. Design notes and the reasoning behind each choice are in review comments on the lines they explain. #### Not in this PR Extensions still can't say *why* they started a session. So the R and Python interpreter pickers record "The R extension selected this interpreter", not "You selected this interpreter". That needs a public API change. ### Label changes
| `startReasonId` | Label in #16309 | New label | |---|---|---| | **Startup** | | | | `affiliatedRuntime` | This workspace's last used interpreter was started when Positron started | Positron started the last interpreter used in this workspace | | `affiliatedRuntimeAtRegistration` | This workspace's last used interpreter was started when found by interpreter discovery | Positron found the last interpreter used in this workspace and started it | | `extensionRecommendedRuntime`, `extensionRequestedImmediateStart` | The {extension} extension recommended (starting) {interpreter} for this workspace (when interpreter discovery finished) | The {extension} extension recommended this interpreter for this workspace | | `extensionRequestedStartAtRegistration` | A new interpreter was found after startup, and the {extension} extension recommended {interpreter} for this workspace | The {extension} extension found this interpreter and recommended it for this workspace | | `languageFileOpened`, `languageFileOpenedAtRegistration` | This interpreter was started after a file written in {language} was opened | A file written in {language} was opened | | **Consoles** | | | | `duplicatedConsoleSession` | A console was duplicated | You duplicated a console | | `duplicatedNotebookSession` | A console was started from the {interpreter} notebook session | You started a new console with a notebook's interpreter | | `userRanCodeWithoutSession` | (new) | You ran code with no {language} console open | | `aiChatCodeExecutedWithoutSession` | (new) | Code from AI chat was run with no {language} console open | | `userStartedAgentSession` | You started an agent console session for this interpreter | (unchanged) | | `codeExecutedWithoutSession` | Code was sent to the console with no {language} session | The {extension} extension ran code with no {language} console open, or Code was run with no {language} console open | | `restartUninitializedSession` | A restart was requested for a session that never started | The {extension} extension requested a restart before this interpreter had started, or A restart was requested before this interpreter had started | | **Extensions** | | | | `extensionApiSelect` | You started this interpreter | The {extension} extension selected this interpreter | | `extensionApiStart` | An extension asked for this session through the Positron API | The {extension} extension started this interpreter | | `extensionStartedAgentSession` | An extension started an agent session for this interpreter | The {extension} extension started an agent session for this interpreter | | **Notebooks** | | | | `newFolderNotebook` | This notebook was created with a new folder from the Jupyter Notebook template | You created a new folder from the Jupyter Notebook template | | `quartoInlineOutput` | The Quarto document {notebook} needed a kernel for inline output | {notebook} needed a kernel for inline output | | `notebookCodeFragmentExecuted` | Selected code in {notebook} was run with no kernel | Selected code in {notebook} was run with no kernel running | | `notebookKernelSelectionDeferred` | The {interpreter} kernel for {notebook} started once its interpreter was found | The {interpreter} kernel was selected for {notebook} and started once Positron found it | | `notebookEditorOpened` | The {notebook} notebook was opened | {notebook} was opened | | `notebookEditorActivated` | {notebook}'s preview tab was kept open, or its background tab was brought to the front | (removed: the session keeps the reason it was held back for) | Labels with an extension fall back to "An extension ..." for sessions saved before the extension was recorded.
### Screenshots ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:console @:sessions @:interpreter @:apps @:notebooks @:quarto Check the start reason in the console info popup (the (i) button in the Console action bar). For the Runtimes view, turn on `interpreters.showSessions` and expand a session in the **Runtimes** tab. Workspaces are under `test/e2e/test-files/workspaces/`. 1. **Extension selects:** run "R: Select Interpreter" and pick an R. Popup: "The R extension selected this interpreter". Runtimes view: `Requesting Extension: positron.positron-r`. 2. **Extension runs code:** set `interpreters.startupBehavior` to `manual` for R, open `shiny-r-example/gen_table.R`, and run "R: Source R File". Popup: "The R extension ran code with no R console open". 3. **You run code:** shut down that console, then press Cmd/Ctrl+Enter on a line in the same file. Popup: "You ran code with no R console open", with no Requesting Extension line. 4. **A kernel relays code:** with no R console, run `rstudioapi::sendToConsole("1 + 1")` in an R notebook (needs `rstudioapi`). Popup: "Code was run with no R console open". It doesn't name Kernel Supervisor. 5. **Extension starts a session:** open `shiny-r-example/app.R` and run "Shiny: Run Shiny App". Popup for the "Shiny" console: "The Positron Run App extension started this interpreter". 6. **Positron's own picker:** run "Start New Console Session" and pick an interpreter. Popup: "You selected this interpreter", with no Requesting Extension line. 7. **Notebook renamed:** open a new untitled notebook and run a cell, then save it as `analysis.ipynb`. The Runtimes view and the diagnostics report both name `analysis.ipynb`. 8. **Startup Behavior link:** use step 7 of #16309's validation steps. Under the start reason, the popup shows "You can change the startup behavior in settings", which opens the Settings editor on the tab where the value is set. 9. **Reload:** after steps 1 and 5, run Developer: Reload Window. The restored sessions keep their labels and Requesting Extension lines. 10. **Notebook in a preview tab:** with no sessions running, single-click a Python `.ipynb` in Explorer so it opens as a preview tab (italic title). Wait a few seconds: no kernel starts. Double-click the tab. Once the kernel starts, the Runtimes view says "The {interpreter} kernel was selected for {notebook}", ID `notebookKernelSelected`. 11. **Code from AI chat:** with no Python console running, ask chat to run some Python and approve the Execute Code tool. Popup: "Code from AI chat was run with no Python console open". Running a chat code block with its Run in Console button says "You ran code with no Python console open" instead.

title: Show session start reason in console info popup
description:
### Summary

Fixes https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16281

This PR shows why a session was started in the Console info popup and the Runtimes view, so it's easier to know what caused a session to start in a number of auto-start cases.

I don't think `startReason` was ever meant to be seen by our users so it was never localized, and the wording for these strings tended to vary quite a bit since this was mostly for developers when debugging. Showing it in the UI means the text has to be translatable and clear to users.

I decided to solve this by adding a `startReasonId`. Each call site now passes an ID from the `SessionStartReasonId` enum, and the UI looks up a translated label from it. The enum also gives us one place that lists every way a session can start. I'm hoping that makes it easier to understand all the different ways a session can be started. And it gives each start a fixed category, so we no longer have to read a string that might be very detailed or very vague.

Each session's start reason has three parts:
- **`startReasonId`**: a fixed key such as `languageFileOpened`. Stored with the session. Missing for sessions saved before this change.
- **Label**: a localized string looked up from the `startReasonId` when the popup is shown. It's filled in with names read from the session: the language, the display name of the extension that provides the interpreter, the interpreter, and the notebook's file name. For example, `This interpreter was started after a file written in R was opened`.
- **`startReason`**: the English label plus any non-translatable values that identify the request, such as `This interpreter was started after a file written in r was opened (language: r)`. Stored with the session. Most values are IDs, such as the language ID and extension ID, so developers can search for them. The interpreter, session, and notebook values are names.

The console popup's "Start Reason" line shows the label. The Runtimes view and diagnostics report show `startReason` and `startReasonId`.

For `startupBehaviorAlways` and `startupBehaviorAlwaysAllLanguages`, the Start Reason line ends with "Change the behavior in settings." The word "settings" is a link. It opens the Settings editor on the tab whose value is in effect: Workspace, Remote, or User. It filters to the session's language when the value is set for that language. In the JSON settings editor, it jumps to the setting instead.

Sessions are still saved in the same format, so older versions of Positron can restore sessions saved by this one. `startReasonId` is a new optional field that older versions ignore.

### Old vs New Start Reasons

In the labels, `{language}`, `{extension}`, `{interpreter}`, and `{notebook}` are filled in from the session when the popup is shown. `{interpreter}` is the interpreter's name, not the session name, so renaming a session doesn't change it. `{notebook}` is the file name of the session's notebook or Quarto document.

<details>

| `startReasonId` | Old `startReason` (on `main`) | New label | Values added to `startReason` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Startup** | | | |
| `affiliatedRuntime` | `Affiliated <language name> runtime for workspace` | This workspace's last used interpreter was started when Positron started | `language` |
| `affiliatedRuntimeAtRegistration` | `Affiliated runtime for workspace registered` | This workspace's last used interpreter was started when found by interpreter discovery | `language` |
| `extensionRecommendedRuntime` | `The <extension> extension recommended the runtime to be started in this workspace.` | The {extension} extension recommended starting {interpreter} for this workspace | `extension`, `interpreter` |
| `extensionRequestedImmediateStart` | `The <extension> extension requested the runtime to be started immediately.` | The {extension} extension recommended {interpreter} for this workspace when interpreter discovery finished | `extension`, `interpreter` |
| `extensionRequestedStartAtRegistration` | `An extension requested that the runtime start immediately after being registered.` | A new interpreter was found after startup, and the {extension} extension recommended {interpreter} for this workspace | `extension`, `interpreter` |
| `startupBehaviorAlways` | `The configuration specifies that a runtime should always start for the '<language ID>' language.` | Startup Behavior is set to "Always" for {language} | `language` |
| `startupBehaviorAlwaysAllLanguages` | `The configuration specifies that a runtime should always start for the '<language ID>' language.` | Startup Behavior is set to "Always" | `language` |
| `languageFileOpenedAtRegistration` | `A file with the language ID <language ID> was open when the runtime was registered.` | This interpreter was started after a file written in {language} was opened | `language` |
| `languageFileOpened` | `A file with the language ID <language ID> was opened.` | This interpreter was started after a file written in {language} was opened | `language` |
| **Consoles** | | | |
| `userSelectedRuntime` | `User selected runtime` | You selected this interpreter | none |
| `userStartedAgentSession` | `User started an agent session` | You started an agent console session for this interpreter | none |
| `newConsoleCommand` | `Runtime id supplied to startNewConsoleSession command` | A command requested a new console for this interpreter | `command` |
| `duplicatedConsoleSession` | `Duplicated session: <session name>` | A console was duplicated | `fromSession` |
| `duplicatedNotebookSession` | `Started console session from notebook session: <session name>` | A console was started from the {interpreter} notebook session | `interpreter`, `fromSession` |
| `codeExecutedWithoutSession` | `User executed code in language <language ID>, and no running runtime session was found for the language.` | Code was sent to the console with no {language} session | `language`, `codeSource` |
| `restartUninitializedSession` | `'Restart Interpreter' command invoked` | A restart was requested for a session that never started | `restartSource` |
| **Extensions** | | | |
| `extensionApiSelect` | `Extension-requested runtime selection via Positron API` | You started this interpreter | `requestingExtension` |
| `extensionApiStart` | `Extension-requested runtime selection via Positron API` | An extension asked for this session through the Positron API | `requestingExtension` |
| `extensionStartedAgentSession` | `Extension-requested runtime selection via Positron API` (with `owner: 'agent'`) | An extension started an agent session for this interpreter | `requestingExtension` |
| **Notebooks** | | | |
| `notebookKernelSelected` | `Runtime kernel <kernel ID> selected for notebook` | The {interpreter} kernel was selected for {notebook} | `interpreter`, `notebook`, `kernel` |

| `newFolderNotebook` | `New Folder Notebook Creation` | This notebook was created with a new folder from the Jupyter Notebook template | none |
