title: e2e: select output lines by keyboard and keep console typing from losing focus
description:
Fixes the two hard failures in the [2026.10.0-208 nightly](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/36993162610). Both were test bugs in e2e page objects. Test-only change. ### Summary - **Output pane** (`Copy Window output log content to editor`, failed on macOS, flaky on ubuntu and windows since it was unskipped in #16348). `scrollToTop` sent the cursor-top key before the output editor had focus, which the view grants asynchronously once the channel model loads. The pane stayed pinned to the streaming Window log, so the top scroll shadow intercepted the click on the first view line and the stream kept detaching it. The page object now waits for editor focus, presses cursor-top, asserts the scroll shadow is gone, and selects lines with Shift+Down. No pointer clicks on view lines. - **Console input** (`Python - Home / End / Ctrl+U act on the console input, not the output scroll`, failed twice on debian web). `clearInput` pressed Ctrl+A on an already-empty input, which Positron turns into "select all console output". The next click on the console landed inside that DOM selection and dropped input focus, so every typed key was lost. It only shows when the test runs first in a worker (after a retry restart), because the previous test normally leaves `x = 42` in the input. `clearInput` now skips select-all when the input is empty, and `typeToConsole` waits for focus to be inside the active console before typing, so dropped keys fail with a focus message instead of an empty-string mismatch. The product side of the focus drop is #16393. Local runs: output copy 3 of 3 on Electron; console-input file 7 of 7 on both web and Electron; the Home/End test alone in a fresh worker (the failing condition) 3 of 3 across web and Electron, where a probe of the old code failed 3 of 4. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:output @:editor @:console @:web @:win Watch the web and windows lanes for `console-input.test.ts` and `output-to-editor-copy.test.ts`. The mac lane only runs nightly. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Output page object clicked a view line in a streaming, not-yet-scrolled-to-top editor; the top scroll shadow intercepted the pointer and re-renders detached the line. - **Test:** [Copy from Output and paste to Editor > Copy Window output log content to editor](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Copy%20from%20Output%20and%20paste%20to%20Editor%20%3E%20Copy%20Window%20output%20log%20content%20to%20editor%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Foutput%2Foutput-to-editor-copy.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded. waiting for locator("div[id=\"workbench.panel.output\"]").locator(".view-line").first() -
intercepts pointer events / element was detached from the DOM, retrying - **Signal:** Every click attempt resolves the first .view-line, then .scroll-decoration (Monaco renders that class only while scrollTop > 0) intercepts the pointer and the line detaches between retries: the pane was still pinned to the Window log tail when selectFirstNLines clicked, so the cursor-top key sent by scrollToTop never reached the editor (the output view focuses its editor asynchronously after the channel model loads). Deterministic on mac (0/11), 5 flaky retries on ubuntu/win since the test was unskipped on 2026-10-01. - **Frequency:** 6/276 runs (2.2%) on main, ubuntu/electron, mac/electron, win/electron - **Hypothesis:** race
### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- clearInput on an already-empty console input makes Ctrl+A select the console output as a DOM selection; the next console click then drops input focus and the typed text is lost. - **Test:** [Console Input > Python - Home / End / Ctrl+U act on the console input, not the output scroll](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Console%20Input%20%3E%20Python%20-%20Home%20%2F%20End%20%2F%20Ctrl%2BU%20act%20on%20the%20console%20input%2C%20not%20the%20output%20scroll%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fconsole%2Fconsole-input.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Error: expect(locator).toContainText(expected) failed - Locator: locator(".console-instance[style*=\"z-index: auto\"] .view-line") Expected substring: "abcDEF" Received string: "" - **Signal:** Trace DOM snapshots: the Python console input editor carries .focused through the Ctrl+K F / Ctrl+A / Backspace presses, loses it in the after-snapshot of the typeToConsole click on .console-instance (t=500582 attempt 0, t=568146 attempt 1), and never regains it; abcDEF never appears in the DOM. Local probe reproduces it 3 of 4 runs (web 2/2, electron 1/2): after clearInput getSelection() is a Range anchored at .console-instance-container, after the click document.activeElement is the view pane body (div.pane.expanded). Product: consoleInput.tsx Ctrl+A on an empty input calls onSelectAll (selectAllRuntimeItems); consoleInstance.tsx mouseDownHandler treats a click inside that selection as copy + focusInput, and the browser default mousedown focus action then moves focus to the pane body. Only happens when the test runs first in a worker (after a retry restart), because the usual leftover x = 42 from the prior test keeps the input non-empty. - **Frequency:** 1/10 runs (10%) on main, debian/chromium - **Hypothesis:** isolation

title: Contribute `"python.analysis.completeFunctionParens": true` for Pyrefly
description:
Addresses #5556.

This PR contributes a `true` default for the Pylance-compatible setting `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens`, which Pyrefly has handling for. When you accept a completion for a function, Positron inserts the parentheses and puts the cursor between them.

This follows the pattern of the default for `pyrefly.commentFoldingRanges` in #11785. Users can still turn the feature off in their own settings.

One note for review is that the two settings reach the language server by different routes. Pyrefly gets `pyrefly.commentFoldingRanges` in the `initialize` request, because the extension sends the whole `pyrefly` section as `initializationOptions`. It gets `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens` later, when the server requests the `python` section with `workspace/configuration`. In full disclosure, I cannot get this behavior to work for me in a dev build at all, although I can get the parentheses added if I put this setting in my user `settings.json` in a release build, once I made a change similar to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/5556#issuecomment-5360312367.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Python function completions now insert parentheses by default (#5556)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:pyrefly

Somebody else really needs to confirm this does actually work, as things seem like a bit of a mess to me:

1. Open a Python file. Do not set `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens` in your own settings.
2. Type `pri` and accept the `print` completion with <kbd>Tab</kbd>. The editor inserts `print()` and puts the cursor between the parentheses.
3. Add `import pandas as pd`. Type `pd.read_c` and accept `read_csv`. The editor inserts `pd.read_csv()`.
4. Add `df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})`. Type `df.sha` and accept `shape`. The editor inserts no parentheses, because `shape` is not callable.
5. Set `"python.analysis.completeFunctionParens": false` in your settings. Run _Developer: Reload Window_. The completions no longer insert parentheses.

This change sets one default value in a manifest, so it adds no tests. The existing autocomplete e2e tests cover Python completions.

title: Respect `completeFunctionParens` in Python runtime completions
description:
Fixes #15657

When `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens` is on, Pyrefly gives function completions the insert text `name($0)`. The `positron-python` language server gave the same names with no insert text. Positron core removes duplicate completions only when their insert text is the same so both items showed, and the item without parentheses was first.

This PR makes the positron-python language server emit the same insert text as Pyrefly. Now the two items are duplicates, and core keeps the positron-python item, which has the runtime details and docs.

- The server reads `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens` with a `workspace/configuration` request after `initialized`. It also registers for `workspace/didChangeConfiguration`, so a change to the setting applies without a reload.
- Only functions and methods (`inspect.isroutine`) get parentheses. Pyrefly does not add parentheses to classes or callable instances, so this server does not add them either.
- The rules match the behavior of Pyrefly 1.3.2, which I examined directly:
  - Bare names in store positions get no parentheses: assignment targets, `for` and `with ... as` targets, `del`, `global`, lambda parameters, and keyword argument names.
  - Attributes always get parentheses, also in store positions such as `obj.method = 1`. Pyrefly does this, so a different rule would show the duplicate again.
  - Parentheses are added also when a `(` follows the cursor.
  - Import lines and `def`/`class` names get no parentheses.
- If the setting is off (the default), the behavior does not change.

One known limitation is that the server reads the setting without a scope URI. In a multi-root workspace where a folder overrides the setting, the server uses the workspace value for all documents.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Python completions for runtime objects no longer show two times when `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens` is on (#15657)

### Validation Steps

@:console @:editor @:pyrefly

1. Set `"python.analysis.completeFunctionParens": true` in your user settings.
2. Start a Python console.
3. Run `import pandas as pd` and `df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})`.
4. Type `df.index.ma` in the console, and then in a Python file. Get completions.
5. Make sure that one `max` item shows. Make sure that it inserts `max()` with the cursor between the parentheses.

title: Bump `brace-expansion` overrides in `positron-python` for security
description:
This PR removes the high npm audit advisories in the runtime dependencies of `positron-python`. This PR is part of the work for posit-dev/positron-builds#1269.

### Summary

`package.json` in `positron-python` pins `brace-expansion` with exact `overrides`, from #15312, so `npm audit fix` cannot move `brace-expansion` to a patched version. This PR changes the three pins to the patched releases:

- `brace-expansion@1`: 1.1.18 to 1.1.21
- `brace-expansion@2`: 2.1.4 to 2.1.7
- `brace-expansion@5`: 5.0.9 to 5.0.12

These versions remove the high advisories for denial of service in `brace-expansion`: uncontrolled recursion and quadratic-time expansion. They also remove the related high advisory for `minimatch`. In the runtime dependencies, `brace-expansion` comes through `glob`, `minimatch`, and `vscode-languageclient`. The extension uses `glob` and `minimatch` for interpreter discovery, file system helpers, and test discovery.

I also ran `npm audit fix --package-lock-only`. This changes the lockfile inside the semver ranges that we already declare:

- `minimatch` 10.2.5 to 10.2.6, under `vscode-languageclient`. The new version requires `brace-expansion ^5.0.8`.
- `browserify-sign` 4.2.5 to 4.2.6. This is a dev dependency only.
- `tslib` is now a runtime dependency in the lockfile, not a dev dependency. `rxjs` requires it at runtime, so the old flag was not correct. The version does not change.

| Scope | Moderate | High | Critical |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime only, before | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| Runtime only, after | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| All dependencies, before | 10 | 13 | 1 |
| All dependencies, after | 10 | 12 | 1 |

The dev advisories that are still open need major version changes, so they are not in this PR. They come through `download` (`decompress`, the one critical), `@typescript-eslint` 5 and 6, `@vscode/vsce` (`markdown-it`), `copy-webpack-plugin` (`serialize-javascript`), and `nyc` (`uuid`).

`npm ci`, `npm ls --all`, and `tsc -p ./ --noEmit` pass for the extension.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Update dependencies of the Python extension to remove known security vulnerabilities

### Validation Steps

To test by hand, open a folder that has a Python virtual environment. Make sure that Positron discovers the environment and that a Python session starts. Then open a folder that has `pytest` tests, and make sure that the tests show in the Test Explorer.

title: e2e: fix two setup races in the settings-import and Posit Assistant suites
description:
Fixes the two hard failures in main run [36904303903](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/36904303903). Both are test-side timing bugs; neither points at a product change.

### Summary

**Settings import: accepted settings are saved** (ubuntu, flaky in 13 of 30 main runs since Sep 30). The test pressed `Home` 18ms after the open-settings chord. The trace frame at that instant shows the status bar still waiting for the chord's second key and no editor open, so the keypress never reached the editor. When settings.json then opened it restored a view state with line 1 scrolled off, and the banner assertion failed. Bare `Home` on Windows and Linux also only moves to the start of the current line, so the helper could not have scrolled to the top even with good timing.

- `scrollToTop` presses Ctrl+Home on Windows and Linux (the Mac path already used Cmd+Up). The only caller is this test file.
- The test now reaches the banner through the file's existing `scrollEditorUntilVisible` helper, whose editor click waits for the editor to open and gives Monaco focus before the scroll keypress. The helper's click and scroll are reordered for the same reason.

**Posit Assistant: open and verify welcome page** (Windows). Both attempts failed in `beforeAll`, in the dev-build update and provider login flow.

- First attempt: after clicking Reload on the update toast, the helper slept 3s and waited for `.monaco-workbench`, then opened the provider modal against a still-starting extension host. The modal took over 15s to render. The reload now goes through a new `hotKeys.reloadWindowWith(trigger)`, which is `reloadWindow` with the trigger factored out, so the toast click gets the same navigation, restored-workbench, and startup-messaging gates the keybinding path already had.
- Retry: the update check found no newer build, so `toasts.waitForAppear` timed out. It had opened the notification center to look for the toast and left it open on the failure path. The center, holding a Python "requirements.txt but no virtual environment" notification, then intercepted every click on the modal's Connect button for 30s. `waitForAppear` now closes the center before rethrowing.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:vscode-settings @:assistant @:win

The settings-import suite should pass on Linux without a retry on the accepted-settings test. The Posit Assistant suites should pass on Windows, including the case where the dev-build update is a no-op.

Local run was not possible on this machine: the shared settings fixture's Cmd+J chord toggled the panel instead of opening settings.json before any changed code ran, so CI is the verification here.

title: Python: run the located uv everywhere and lint against bare uv
description:
Fixes #15835

### Summary

After Positron installs uv, the binary is in `~\.local\bin` (or `~/.local/bin`). The extension host does not have this directory on its PATH until a restart. As a result, a spawn of the bare name `uv` fails with `spawn uv ENOENT`. Code that uses the located binary works, because `UvUtils` also looks in the known install locations.

The original failure in #15835 was in the Python install step: `uv python install` and `uv python find` used the bare name. #16161 corrected those two calls and the uv venv creation with `execLocatedUv`.

This PR corrects the remaining code that spawned the bare name:

- `UVInstaller` (the module installer): `isSupported()` found uv in its install location, but `getExecutionInfo()` returned `execPath: 'uv'`. When uv is available, it is the preferred installer for all non-conda environments. Thus this error affected package installs in many environments.
- `UvPackageManager` (the Packages pane for uv environments): `uv pip freeze`, `uv pip list --outdated`, and the terminal install command all used the bare name.

All four places now use `getLocatedUvCommand()`, which this PR exports from `uv.ts`. The terminal path already quotes the command and adds `& ` for PowerShell, so a path with spaces works.

### Lint rule

To prevent this error in the future, this PR adds two `no-restricted-syntax` selectors for `src/client` in `eslint.config.mjs`:

- A literal `'uv'` as the first argument to a spawn function (`exec`, `execUv`, `execObservable`, `spawn`, `sendCommand`, and more).
- A literal `'uv'` assigned to a variable with the name `execPath`, `command`, or `executable`.

The error message tells the author to use `execLocatedUv()`, `execObservableLocatedUv()`, or `getLocatedUvCommand()`. On the code before #16161 and this PR, the rule finds all six bare spawns. On this branch, the rule finds none, and it gives no false positives in `src/client`.

The rule does not apply to tests, because tests replace the located-uv helpers with fakes that spawn the bare name. In ESLint flat config, a rule in a later block replaces the earlier array. Thus the new Positron block copies the upstream entries (`for..in`, labels, `with`) and adds the two selectors. The only upstream line that changes is `export default [`, which becomes a named `config` array.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Package installs and the Packages pane now work with uv when Positron installed uv in the same session (#15835)

### Validation Steps

@:packages-pane @:interpreter @:win

New unit tests in `uvInstaller.unit.test.ts` and `uvPackageManager.unit.test.ts` make sure that each call site uses the located command. Each test fails if the bare `uv` comes back.

To do a manual test on Windows:

1. Remove uv from the machine.
2. Start a build that includes this PR.
3. Run _Python: Install Python via uv_. Install a Python version and create a uv environment.
4. In the same window, install a package from the Packages pane.
5. Make sure that the install completes without `spawn uv ENOENT` or "uv is not recognized".

title: Let AI agents read and act on data apps in the Viewer
description:
Part of #15099

### Summary

Lets an AI agent see and use what's in the Viewer pane: data apps (Shiny, Streamlit, Dash) and HTML content such as htmlwidgets.

Agents get this through nine Positron commands. Posit Assistant runs them with its existing `positronCommand` tool (posit-dev/assistant#2582). An earlier version of this PR added `positron.ai` extension APIs and two Assistant tools instead. Those are gone, which saves about 1,000 tokens on every Assistant request. The bridge and the service underneath are unchanged.

| Command | What it does | Asks first? |
|---|---|---|
| `positronViewer.read` | A text outline of the page: roles, names and values, with a ref such as `e3` on each control. It waits for the app to settle first. | No |
| `positronViewer.screenshot` | A PNG of the Viewer. It reveals a hidden Viewer first, without taking focus. | No |
| `positronViewer.click`, `.hover`, `.fill`, `.select`, `.press` | Act on a control the way a user would, then return a fresh outline. | Yes |
| `positronViewer.scroll`, `.wait` | Scroll, or wait for the app to settle or for some text to show up. | No |

- Actions check that they took effect. In a Shiny app, that includes checking the server got the value. Once an action has run, later problems are reported in the result rather than as a failure, so an agent doesn't take the action twice.
- Results are text in `<viewer_page>`, `<viewer_action>` and `<viewer_error>` nodes. The page's text is escaped and marked as untrusted. Outlines stay under `positronCommand`'s 32,000-character limit. A screenshot comes back as a base64 image.
- Everything is off when `ai.enabled` is off.

**Asking first.** Agent-command metadata gets a `readOnly` flag, which `positron.ai.getAgentAllowedCommands()` passes on. The Assistant runs read-only commands without asking. Hover asks even though it doesn't change what the user typed, because an app can run server code on hover (a Shiny plot's hover input, a Dash `hoverData` callback).

**Skills.** The `positron-commands` skill's `viewer.md` reference now covers reading and using the page as well as showing it. The showing part came from #16312, and the two share one file. `interactive-apps.md` now tells the agent to check an app it started in the Viewer, rather than ask the user.

**How it works.** A bridge (`viewerBridge.ts`) reads the page and takes the actions.
- On Desktop, the app's frame is cross-origin. The bridge is sent as a script, run in that frame through the main process, and cached on the app's window between calls.
- In web builds, the frames are same-origin. The bridge runs in Positron's page and reaches into the app's frame, so nothing is added to the app.
- Screenshots on Desktop are a native capture. On web, they're rebuilt from the page with [modern-screenshot](https://github.com/qq15725/modern-screenshot) (MIT), a new ESM dependency listed in ThirdPartyNotices.

**Desktop webview fix.** Following a link in the Viewer can give the app's frame a new process and routing ID. The frame ID the webview kept then pointed at a frame that was gone. Frame IDs now also carry Electron's `frameTreeNodeId`, which stays the same across navigations, and the webview and main process find the frame by it. This may also fix `webview-events.js` (copy/paste, context menus) not being re-injected after a link navigation, but I haven't checked that separately.

E2E tests come in a follow-up PR.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- AI agents such as Posit Assistant can now read, take screenshots of, and use data apps and other content in the Viewer pane (#15099)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:viewer @:apps @:assistant @:web @:win

The existing Viewer and app tests cover the webview changes (the frame tracking, and loading URIs). To try the commands, use the Assistant build from posit-dev/assistant#2582 with `assistant.previewFeatures` on, and start a new conversation outside Ask mode (Ask mode doesn't run Positron commands).

1. Run a Shiny, Streamlit or Dash app so it shows in the Viewer.
2. Ask "What's in the Viewer?" The Assistant should read the page without asking, and describe the app and its controls.
3. Ask it to change an input, such as "Set bins to 10". It should ask first, and then the app and its answer should both show the new value.
4. Have it click a link in the app, then ask what's showing. It should describe the new page.
5. Hide the Viewer and ask for a screenshot. The Viewer should come back without taking focus.
6. Set `ai.enabled` to false. Every Viewer command should fail.

The bridge and service were checked by hand on Desktop against Shiny, Streamlit 1.63 and Dash 4.4.1, including a hidden Viewer and following a link, and on a local Workbench instance with Shiny and Streamlit apps. The commands were checked on Desktop, both directly and with the Assistant build from posit-dev/assistant#2582.

Test coverage: unit tests cover:
- the commands: output format, escaping, size limits and which ones ask first;
- the bridge: snapshots and every action, against markup from each framework;
- the service: gating, revealing, layout waits, timeouts and navigation;
- the web and Desktop ways of running the bridge, and frame matching.

The screenshot encoding and the main process's frame lookup need a real canvas and Electron, so the follow-up e2e PR covers them.

title: Support ${workspaceFolder} in R interpreter path settings
description:
Addresses #10389 for R. Python gets the same fix in a follow-up PR, so this doesn't close the issue.

### Summary

R interpreter path settings now support `${workspaceFolder}`. A project can point Positron at an R that lives inside it:

```json
{
  "positron.r.customBinaries": ["${workspaceFolder}/.pixi/envs/default/bin/R"]
}
```

Before this change, that path failed the "is it absolute" check and was dropped with a `not absolute...ignoring` log line.

**Settings covered:** `positron.r.customBinaries`, `customRootFolders`, `interpreters.exclude`, `interpreters.override`, and `interpreters.default`.

**Only `${workspaceFolder}` is supported.** That's what the issue asks for. Environment variables (`${env:NAME}`) are left out on purpose. R users usually set R-related variables in `.Renviron`, which R reads when it starts. The extension runs before any R session, so it never sees those values, and a setting that looks right would fail.

**Multi-root workspaces:** `${workspaceFolder}` is the first folder.

**Paths that can't be resolved are ignored, not guessed.** A path is dropped, with a log line that says why, when:

- it uses `${workspaceFolder}` and no folder is open
- it uses any other `${...}` variable, including a misspelling like `${workspacefolder}`

```
R custom binary path ${env:R_ROOT}/bin/R uses unsupported variable ${env:R_ROOT} (only ${workspaceFolder} is supported)...ignoring
```

In a list setting, only the bad entry is dropped. Matching is an exact string check for `${workspaceFolder}`, not a regex.

**Behavior change for literal `${` in a path.** An absolute path that contains `${`, like `/opt/${x}/bin/R`, used to be accepted as-is. It's now ignored as an unsupported variable. Real R install paths almost never contain `${`, so this is unlikely to affect anyone.

**Discovery cache key.** R's discovery cache is shared by all workspaces, and part of its key was a hash of the raw `interpreters.exclude` and `interpreters.default` text. Two projects with the same `${workspaceFolder}/...` text would have shared a cache entry. The key now hashes the resolved paths.

**Not changed:** workspace trust. Workspace values of these settings are honored in untrusted workspaces, as before.

### Screenshots

- Happy path: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d48cb3c-ae43-4e3b-bb06-b081eac80d74

- Unsupported variables next to a good path: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4adb1c66-4ae6-46b3-89ac-df39e998a17e

- No folder open: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89992104-d986-4122-88ca-9f1279b07d23


### Release Notes

#### New Features

- R interpreter path settings (`positron.r.customBinaries`, `customRootFolders`, `interpreters.exclude`, `interpreters.override`, `interpreters.default`) now support `${workspaceFolder}`, so a project can point at an R installed inside it (#10389)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:ark

Unit tests: `npx vitest run extensions/positron-r/src/setting-variables.vitest.ts`.

Manual check with a project-local R, for example a pixi project (`pixi add r-base=4.4`). Pixi discovery is off by default, so that R is only found through the setting:

1. Open the project folder. In `.vscode/settings.json`, set `"positron.r.customBinaries": ["${workspaceFolder}/.pixi/envs/default/bin/R"]`.
2. Run **R: Print interpreter settings information to Output**. The R Language Pack output shows the full resolved path.
3. Open the interpreter picker. The project's R is listed.
4. Add an entry such as `${env:R_ROOT}/bin/R` next to the good one. The output shows an "unsupported variable" line for it, and the good entry is still listed.
5. Open a window with no folder, with a user-level `${workspaceFolder}/...` entry. The output shows "...but no folder is open...ignoring".

title: Remove provider "Authentication expired" notification
description:

title: Install one pyzmq copy for Python 3.12 and later and update file-count budgets
description:
Addresses #16025

This PR installs pyzmq one time for Python 3.12 and later, instead of one time for each Python version. The result is about 196 fewer files in `positron-python` on macOS and Linux, and about 390 fewer files on Windows.

pyzmq publishes a wheel for each Python version up to 3.11. For Python 3.12 and later, it publishes one `cp312-abi3` wheel. The gulpfile installed this wheel three times, into `cp312`, `cp313`, and `cp314`. The three copies were the same wheel, with only different `__pycache__` files. pyzmq 27.1.0 has no other wheel for 3.13 or 3.14, except free-threaded (`cp313t`, `cp314t`) builds.

**Build.** `bundleIPykernel()` in `gulpfile.js` now uses one list of pyzmq installs for all platforms: `cp39`, `cp310`, `cp311`, and `cp312-abi3`. The `cp312-abi3` install uses `--python-version 3.12 --abi abi3`. The directory name is `cp312-abi3`, not `abi3`, because the `cp3` directories also hold abi3 wheels (psutil, tornado) with a different minimum version.

**Path selection.** `getIpykernelBundle()` in `ipykernel.ts` selects `cp312-abi3` for Python 3.12 and later. For earlier versions, it selects `cp3X` as before.

**Budget.** In `build/lib/positron-path-budget.ts`, the `positron-python` budget goes from 6,350 to 5,950. The expected counts are about 5,020 on darwin-arm64 and about 5,400 on win32-x64. These counts are estimates, and we can look at the counts from a release build before this PR merges.

Notes for reviewers:

- **Python 3.15.** The abi3 wheel also operates with Python 3.15. To add 3.15, change only the version lists in `ipykernel.ts` and `scripts/pip-compile-ipykernel.py`. If pyzmq stops publishing an abi3 wheel, the pip install fails during the build. Fortunatley it will not fail silently.
- **Free-threaded Python.** No change. The old `cp313` and `cp314` directories also held the abi3 wheel, which free-threaded Python cannot load.
- **Local builds.** After you pull this change, remove the old `python_files/lib/ipykernel/universal2/cp312`, `cp313`, and `cp314` directories (or `<arch>/cp31X` on Windows and Linux). Git ignores them, and the build does not remove them. A local release build copies them and will show a file count that is too high.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:console @:sessions @:interpreter @:win

I did these checks:

- For each platform tag that we build (`macosx_10_15_universal2`, `win_amd64`, `win_arm64`, `manylinux_2_28_x86_64`, `manylinux_2_28_aarch64`), pip installs the `cp312-abi3` wheel with `--require-hashes` and the current `cpx-requirements.txt`.
- `npx gulp installPythonLibs` completes on macOS. It makes `universal2/cp39`, `cp310`, `cp311`, and `cp312-abi3`.
- With the bundle paths on `sys.path`, Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 import `zmq` and `ipykernel.kernelapp` from `cp312-abi3`. Python 3.11 imports `zmq` from `cp311`.
- The Ipykernel unit tests pass (`npm run test:unittests -- --grep "Ipykernel"`). The new tests check the selected directory for Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
- The build tests pass: `cd build && node --test lib/test/positron-path-budget.test.ts lib/test/positron-check-path-lengths.test.ts`.

To test by hand in a packaged build (for example, made with `npm run gulp vscode`):

1. Check that `.../positron-python/python_files/lib/ipykernel/universal2` contains only `cp39`, `cp310`, `cp311`, and `cp312-abi3` (on Windows and Linux, check `<arch>/`).
2. Start a Python 3.12, 3.13, or 3.14 console session. The session must start with the bundled ipykernel.
3. Start a Python 3.9, 3.10, or 3.11 console session. This session must also start.
4. Check the positron-python line under File counts: in the build log.

title: e2e: fix Foundry Azure retries and collect the JIT user's Positron logs
description:
Fixes the two failures `posit-assistant-foundry.test.ts` hit in positron-builds nightly run [36844545529](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/36844545529) (azure shard). ### Summary **Retries always failed in the fixture.** The Azure branch of the Workbench fixture called `openWorkspaceFolder` unconditionally after the session launched. On a retry the dashboard relaunches the surviving `test-files` project via "Create new session", which opens Positron directly in that folder (the retry trace shows `?folder=/home/rstudio-ide-test/test-files` and the Explorer already populated), so the Explorer's empty-view "Open Folder" button never exists and the fixture timed out. `dashboard.openSession` now returns whether it created the project, and the copy + Open Folder step runs only on that path, the same way the user1 shards already behave. The copy is idempotent so a stale copy from an earlier suite no longer nests a second `test-files` folder. **First attempt timed out on the model picker.** The overflow menu opened with no "Model" submenu for the full 30s; the assistant hides that submenu until a provider has delivered models. `selectModel` now retries the open -> Model -> pick cycle with short per-step timeouts, mirroring `selectProviderModelMenuMode`, so a late or re-rendered list is retried instead of hanging on one click. The underlying reason Foundry had no models about a second after the chat input appeared is not confirmed yet, because: **The Azure shard's Positron logs were never attached.** The harness copied logs from `/home/user1/...` while the Azure session runs as the JIT user `rstudio-ide-test` (the job log shows the resulting `tar: No such file` error). Logs are now collected and cleaned from both homes, so the next first-attempt occurrence will have the authentication extension's Microsoft Foundry log lines. Candidate for the first-attempt cause, left for a follow-up once a logged occurrence confirms it: the authentication extension reports Foundry managed credentials as absent until `rstudio.rstudio-workbench` is active, and nothing re-fires the ms-foundry sessions when that extension activates later. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:workbench The azure shard of the workbench lane runs both Foundry tests. Both should pass, and the attached `logs-posit-assistant-foundry.test.ts.zip` should now contain a `docker-logs/rstudio-ide-test/` directory with Positron logs. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Two failures in run 36844545529. (1) Retry: Azure fixture calls dashboard.openWorkspaceFolder unconditionally, but relaunching the surviving test-files project opens Positron directly in the folder (URL ?folder=/home/rstudio-ide-test/test-files, title 'Welcome - test-files - Positron'), so the Explorer empty-view 'Open Folder' button never exists. (2) First attempt: chat-form overflow menu opened with no 'Model' submenu for 30s; ModelSelector returns null when the model list is empty, so no provider (Foundry) had delivered models ~1s after the chat input appeared. - **Test:** [Posit Assistant - Microsoft Foundry (Azure managed credentials) > Foundry model responds when authenticated via Azure managed credentials](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Posit%20Assistant%20-%20Microsoft%20Foundry%20%28Azure%20managed%20credentials%29%20%3E%20Foundry%20model%20responds%20when%20authenticated%20via%20Azure%20managed%20credentials%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fworkbench%2Fposit-assistant%2Fposit-assistant-foundry.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** TimeoutError waiting for getByRole('button',{name:'Open Folder'}) in dashboard.page.ts:94 from app-workbench.fixtures.ts:76 on retry; and locator.click timeout on the 'Model' menuitem in positAssistant.ts:413 on attempt 0 - **Signal:** Retry trace after-snapshot at t=180028: frameUrl ...?folder=/home/rstudio-ide-test/test-files, TITLE 'Welcome - test-files - Positron', Explorer Section: test-files, zero 'Open Folder' matches; retry timeline shows 'Create new session' clicked on the existing project row (t=140486) instead of New Session. Attempt-0 aria snapshot: menu [expanded] containing only group '0K tokens · $0.00'; Accounts badge 'Sign in requested'. - **Frequency:** 1/23 runs (4.3%) on main, ubuntu/chromium - **Hypothesis:** (1) Confirmed: openSession's relaunch path (project row survived the async quit) launches into the project folder, as it does for user1 shards where openWorkspaceFolder is only called from createNewProject; the Azure block ignores which path ran. (2) Candidate, unconfirmed: the authentication extension's hasManagedCredentials returns undefined until rstudio.rstudio-workbench isActive and nothing re-fires ms-foundry sessions when that extension activates later (no vscode.extensions.onDidChange listener; forwarder only relays posit-workbench session events), so the assistant's 500ms credential sample records Foundry absent and never re-lists. Cannot confirm: the Azure shard's Positron logs are not collected because reporting.fixtures.ts copies /home/user1/.local/state/positron/logs while the Azure session runs as rstudio-ide-test (tar: No such file in the job log). Ruled out: Workbench sign-in (both attempts reached the dashboard), trust dialog, restored conversation (greeting visible), menu never opening (menu [expanded]).

title: Offer Workbench managed credentials in Snowflake and Databricks connections
description: Fixes #14666 Part of #15436 ### Summary On Posit Workbench, the Snowflake and Databricks data connection drivers now offer a **Workbench Managed Credentials** mechanism when the session was launched with managed credentials. It is listed first, and it asks for nothing except the optional session settings (warehouse/database/schema/role for Snowflake; catalog/schema for Databricks) plus the HTTP path for Databricks. The account or workspace host comes from the credential itself. The Authentication extension handles reading the credentials. It now exports a `managedCredentials` API (`getManagedCredential(authProviderId)`) that returns the access token and its locator (Snowflake account or Databricks host) from a single read of the file Workbench provisions. The drivers call it at connect time and don't parse Workbench's files themselves. This is the first step toward the single auth implementation described in #15436. PAT and OAuth for Databricks still live in the driver. Details: - **Token rotation**: the drivers never cache a token. Snowflake reads a fresh one on every connect and reconnect. Databricks passes a token provider to the SDK as its `external-token` callback, so the SDK fetches a new token when the cached one is about to expire during a session. If Workbench later issues a token for a different account or host, the driver rejects it instead of sending it to the original connection. - **Offering the mechanism**: each driver decides whether to show it at registration time, using the same environment check the Authentication extension uses (`RS_SERVER_URL`, web UI, and `SNOWFLAKE_HOME` / `DATABRICKS_CONFIG_FILE` pointing at a `posit-workbench` path). This way the Authentication extension doesn't have to activate first. - **Generated code contains no credentials**: Python refers to the provisioned `workbench` connection/profile by name, using `connection_name=` for snowflake-connector-python and `Config(profile=...)` for databricks-sql. R uses `odbc::snowflake()` / `odbc::databricks()`, which pick up Workbench credentials on their own. - **Regional Snowflake accounts**: added `readSnowflakeManagedCredentials`, which reads the account and token without the Cortex base-URL validation. That validation rejects regional identifiers such as `xy12345.us-east-2.aws`, which the data driver accepts. `detectSnowflakeCredentials` (used by the Cortex provider) is unchanged. - **Shared helper**: `workbenchCredentials.ts` is copied into both drivers, because extensions can't import each other's sources. `extensions/workbenchCredentials-copies.vitest.ts` fails if the two copies drift apart. Not in this PR: the stretch goal in #14666 of creating the connection automatically at launch, so the user doesn't have to click Connect. The mechanism is pre-selected and needs no input, but the user still starts the connection. ### Release Notes #### New Features - Snowflake and Databricks data connections on Posit Workbench can now use the session's Workbench managed credentials, with no credential input (#14666) #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:connections @:workbench-snowflake @:workbench-databricks Unit/extension-host coverage has been added for the new mechanisms, token rotation, the environment gate, code generation, and regional Snowflake accounts. The existing Workbench managed-credentials e2e tests only check the provisioned environment variables. No e2e test yet runs the Data Connections flow with managed credentials, so check it manually on Workbench: 1. Start a Positron session on Workbench with **Snowflake** managed credentials selected (choose a role, e.g. "Developer"). 2. Open the Connections pane and start a new Snowflake connection. **Workbench Managed Credentials** should be the first mechanism, with no required fields. 3. Connect and check that the schema tree loads. Also check that the generated Python and R code contains no token. 4. Repeat with **Databricks** managed credentials. Only the HTTP path should be required, and the connection should use the workspace host Workbench provisioned. 5. Outside Workbench (desktop, or web without managed credentials), check that the mechanism is not offered. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Log why Posit AI Pass is disabled
description:
Fixes #15672

### Summary

The Workbench default that disables Posit AI Pass was silent. A user saw the provider missing from the picker with nothing in the log explaining why, and had to already know both that `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` exists and that the Workbench default exists at all.

Every branch of `applyPwbPositAIDefault` now says what it did and to which file: applied the default, skipped because the value was already set (info), or skipped because an earlier run already applied it (debug, since it fires on every launch after the first). The failure path now names the file too.

`saveProviderEnabled` returns whether it actually wrote, which is what lets the caller tell "applied the default" apart from "left your choice alone" -- the write itself didn't surface that.

Also adds the issue's nice-to-have: after the catalog loads, one info line lists any providers that resolved to disabled, with the providers.json path. It reports the *resolved* value only; which layer disabled a provider lives in ai-config's internal `resolveEnabled` and isn't exposed, so full provenance needs an upstream change there. Because of that the message names the file without promising that editing it will re-enable anything -- the sealed enforced overlay (`POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED`) outranks the user file, so that advice would be wrong under an admin pin.

Log for provider disabled by admin policy
```
2026-09-29 16:47:29.954 [info] Provider positai is disabled by an admin policy (POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED), which overrides /Users/tmok/.posit/ai/providers.json.
```

Log for provider disabled by user's `providers.json`
```
2026-09-29 16:49:16.499 [info] Provider positai is disabled in /Users/tmok/.posit/ai/providers.json. Set "enabled" to true there to turn it back on.
```

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Posit AI Pass now logs why it is disabled, and where to change it (#15672)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:assistant

Setup. Back up the real config, since production never passes a config path:

```
mv ~/.posit/ai/providers.json ~/.posit/ai/providers.json.bak 2>/dev/null
```

Launch, and open Output -> "Authentication". Clear the filter box: the disabled-providers line is logged during catalog prime, well above the `Registered auth provider` block.

```
RS_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:8787 ./scripts/code-server.sh \
  --connection-token dev --user-data-dir /tmp/pwb-test-1 --log debug
```

`--connection-token` is required only if you have a local `../positron-license/pdol` build; harmless otherwise.

**Resetting between cases.** A fresh `--user-data-dir` does *not* reset the `positAI.pwbDefaultApplied` flag on web -- `globalState` is backed by browser IndexedDB, keyed by origin. Clear site data for `localhost:9888` (or use a private window) before any case that needs a first-run state.

**Case A: first Workbench run, no prior config.** Expect one info line saying the Workbench default was applied, naming the full providers.json path. On disk, `providers.json` gains `providers.positai.enabled: false`. Posit AI is absent from the provider picker.

No disabled-providers line on this run: the catalog primes before the default is written, so at prime time nothing is disabled yet. It appears from the next launch on.

**Case B: relaunch, same browser storage.** No info line about writing the default; at Debug level, one line saying it was applied earlier and is being skipped. The file is unchanged. The disabled-providers line now appears.

**Case C: provider already configured.** With site data cleared, write `{"version":1,"providers":{"positai":{"enabled":true}}}` to `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` and launch. Expect an info line saying positai already has an explicit value at that path, so the default was not applied. The file still reads `enabled: true` and Posit AI appears in the picker.

**Case D: not on Workbench.** Launch the desktop app, or web without `RS_SERVER_URL`. None of the above messages appear and providers.json is not created.

**Case E: write failure.** Make the config path unwritable (e.g. point it at a path under a regular file). Expect a warning naming that path, and the run to continue.

**Case F: admin enforces the setting, overriding the user's file.** The enforced layer is an environment variable, not a file, so providers.json can say `enabled: true` while the provider is off. Set the user file to `{"version":1,"providers":{"positai":{"enabled":true}}}`, then:

```
RS_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:8787 \
POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED='{"version":1,"providers":{"positai":{"enabled":false}}}' \
./scripts/code-server.sh --connection-token dev --user-data-dir /tmp/pwb-test-3
```

Expect the disabled-providers line naming positai; providers.json still reads `enabled: true`, untouched; Posit AI absent from the picker. This is the case the wording is built for -- editing `enabled` here cannot work, because it is already `true`.

Teardown:

```
mv ~/.posit/ai/providers.json.bak ~/.posit/ai/providers.json
rm -rf /tmp/pwb-test-*
```

### QA Notes

The only behavior change is the boolean return from `saveProviderEnabled` and the new log lines. The write path, the `onlyIfUnset` guard, and the globalState flag are unchanged, so cases B, C and F double as regressions for the existing "never clobber a choice" guarantee.

Cases A, B and F were run against a local Workbench-mode server. C, D and E are derived from the code and have not been executed.

title: Don't prepend R to PATH when it's already on PATH
description:
The R extension adds the selected R's folder to the front of the terminal `PATH` so that terminals use the same R as the console. When R lives in a shared system folder like `/usr/bin` (for example, R installed with apt on Debian or WSL), this moved every system tool ahead of everything else on `PATH`, including an activated Python virtual environment. As a result, `pip` in the terminal resolved to the system `pip` instead of the one in the venv.

Now the R extension only adds R's folder to `PATH` when `R` on `PATH` is not already the selected R. If the selected R is already the one on `PATH`, adding it again does nothing useful (and can be harmful), so we skip it. When switching to such an R, any `PATH` entry left over from a previously selected R is removed.

If the selected R is in a shared folder but a different R comes first on `PATH`, we still add R's folder so the terminal gets the right R.

Fixes #15961. 

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Terminals no longer put system tools ahead of an activated Python virtual environment when R is installed in a system folder such as `/usr/bin` (#15961)

### Validation Steps

@:apps @:quarto @:interpreter

1. On Linux or WSL, install R into `/usr/bin` (e.g. `apt install r-base`) and make sure it is the R on `PATH`.
2. Open a folder that contains a Python venv and let it activate.
3. Start an R console, then open a new terminal.
4. Run `which pip`; it should point into the venv.
5. Run "Terminal: Show Environment Contributions"; the R extension should not add `/usr/bin` to `PATH`.
6. Select a different R version in the console, open a new terminal, and check that `which R` points to that version.

title: e2e: unskip output-to-editor copy, outline sessions, and Quarto execution options
description:
Second batch of the e2e skip audit (first batch: #16334). Three skipped tests come back; one stays skipped with an issue attached.

### Summary

- **output-to-editor-copy** (skipped at creation in #11006 because the final assert failed only in CI): the pasted text is now compared line by line. The clipboard carries CRLF on Windows and the editor renders one element per line, so the old whole-string match could never line up.

Pyrefly serves Python symbols before any session starts, and it nests `local_variable` under its function, so the "no session, no outline" check and the fixed row count of 2 were wrong. One `verifyOutline` helper now compares the top-level row labels; an exact match still catches duplicates from multiple sessions.
- **Quarto "execution options are respected when running all cells"** (skipped in #12226 as "flaky on Windows", no issue): the skip is narrowed to Windows and annotated with #16346.
- **notebook-debug** (skipped in #12568): stays skipped, now annotated with #16347. The trace shows the cell drag hover zone covers the left 11px of the glyph margin, so the breakpoint click never reaches Monaco. That is a product bug that also affects users clicking the margin; evidence is on the issue.

title: e2e: scope the Quarto action bar 'date' click to the editor view line
description:
Fixes the `Quarto Document - Verify preview, split editor, open in new window behavior` e2e test, which has failed on roughly 19% of main runs on ubuntu/electron since Sep 28 (for example https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/36760734200). The test clicked `getByText('date')` scoped to the whole editor part. The breadcrumbs bar lives inside that part, and once the Quarto language server returns a document symbol for the YAML front matter the breadcrumb label contains `date:` too. Whether the symbol beats the click is a race, hence the intermittent strict mode violation. The click is now keyed off the `.view-line` whose own text contains `date:`, the same pattern the notebook click-to-cursor test uses. This is locator drift in the test, not a product bug. Verified locally: 3 of 3 serial runs pass on macOS electron. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:editor-action-bar @:quarto The editor action bar suite passes, in particular the Quarto document test on Linux electron. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- getByText("date") scoped to the whole editor part also matches the breadcrumbs label once the Quarto LSP returns a document symbol for the YAML front matter (which contains "date:"); strict mode violation. - **Test:** [Editor Action Bar: Document Files > Quarto Document - Verify `preview`, `split editor`, `open in new window` behavior](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Editor%20Action%20Bar%3A%20Document%20Files%20%3E%20Quarto%20Document%20-%20Verify%20%60preview%60%2C%20%60split%20editor%60%2C%20%60open%20in%20new%20window%60%20behavior%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Feditor-action-bar%2Feditor-action-bar-document-files.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** A - **Signal:** strict mode violation listing a.label-name > span.monaco-highlighted-label with text Y---title: "Diamond sizes"date: 2022-09-12format:... alongside the mtk9 date token; cursor was on line 1 after the Save step typed Y there - **Frequency:** 25/132 runs (18.9%) on main, ubuntu/electron - **Hypothesis:** Breadcrumbs render the outline symbol under the cursor via IconLabel (a.label-name) inside workbench.parts.editor. Document symbols arrive asynchronously from the Quarto LSP, so the label is present only when symbols beat the click, giving the 18.9% rate. Locator drift, not a product bug.

title: Show a dot on console tabs that ran code in the background
description:
Tiny UI improvement related to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14780 and https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/issues/1872 which both let Assistant run code in the background. I based this on #16196 in case there were conflicts, to be merged after.

A console that runs code while you aren't looking at it now shows a small blue dot where the trash icon sits.

"Not looking" means it isn't the selected tab, or the console panel is hidden.

Hovering the tab brings the trash icon back, and the tooltip says how many executions are new; selecting the tab, or showing the panel again, clears the dot. The count comes from the kernel's input echo, so code run by extensions, Posit Assistant, or external agents through the MCP server all counts; silent executions don't.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4eeac072-1041-4d62-afca-bfa5fe516be7

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Console tabs show a dot when code runs in a console you aren't looking at, such as code run by Posit Assistant or an external agent

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:console

1. Start an R console and a Python console, and select the Python tab.
2. Run code in the R session without selecting its tab e.g. using an external agent connected via MCP.
3. The R tab shows a small blue dot where the trash icon normally sits. The Python tab has none.
4. Hover the R tab: the trash icon replaces the dot, and the tooltip reads "1 new execution". Run code in R twice more the same way and it reads "3 new executions". Narrow the pane until the R tab's name is cut short and hover again: the tooltip now reads "R 4.x.x • 3 new executions".
5. Select the R tab: the dot disappears. Select Python again and the R tab stays clear until something else runs there.

title: Tell each Quarto session its hidden notebook URI through session metadata
description:
Fixes #16154

This PR makes core tell each extension the URI of the hidden notebook for a Quarto document. Before, `positron-r` and `positron-python` each worked out that URI from the `notebookUri` of the session. Each extension kept about 85 lines of code for this. The two copies had to match the rules of core exactly. Now core computes the URI once and puts it on the session metadata as `quartoNotebookUri`, and then the extensions read it and delete their copies.

### How it works

- The pure function `quartoNotebookUri` moves from the browser-layer notebook service to `common/quartoVirtualNotebookTypes.ts`. The Quarto kernel manager can then call it before the notebook exists.
- The kernel manager passes the URI to `startNewRuntimeSession` in a new option. The runtime session service copies it to `IRuntimeSessionMetadata.quartoNotebookUri`.
- A shared helper, `reviveRuntimeSessionMetadata`, turns the URIs back into `URI` objects after they cross JSON. It runs when the extension host creates or restores a session, and also runs when stored sessions load.
- The field carries over when an uninitialized session restarts. It follows the document when the new file of an untitled session takes over that session, and it rolls back if that update fails.
- The field is optional. A Quarto session that an older build stored has no value. Nothing crashes, but that session claims no cells and the console client keeps serving them (just the same as before).

### Out of scope

- The extension host does not learn when an untitled document is saved and its session is adopted. The live extension keeps the old value until the session restarts. This was already true for `notebookUri` and in practice, adoption only runs when an untitled session is renumbered after a reload.
- `getRuntimeSessionInterface` in `extHostLanguageRuntime.ts` gives the session metadata of other extensions without reviving URIs (this includes `notebookUri`).
- If we become confident this works on remote SSH, `quartoCellsKey` can stop dropping the remote authority. I left this for a follow-up.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:quarto @:ark @:console

1. Open a saved `.qmd` file with either R chunks and/or Python chunks. Run a chunk so a Quarto session starts. Make sure that completions and hover work in each chunk.
2. In the Python chunk, run a multi-line statement with <kbd>Cmd+Enter</kbd>. Make sure that the whole statement runs.
3. Run _Quarto: New Document_ and add an R chunk. Run it and check completions. Save the file. Run _Developer: Reload Window_, then run the chunk again. Completions must work after the reload.
4. Leave an untitled Quarto document open with a running session. Reload the window so it reopens with a different untitled number. Make sure that the chunk still runs. Make sure that the _Quarto_ output channel shows no errors.
5. Open a real `.ipynb` notebook with an R or Python kernel. Start plain R and Python consoles. Make sure that completions and code execution work as they do on `main`.
6. Open a `.qmd` file without inline output, with only a console running. Make sure that completions in a chunk come from the console client.
7. In a remote SSH window, repeat step 1. This makes sure that the `quarto-cells` URI keeps its authority across RPC and matches the notebook document.

title: Fix/panel layout issues
description:
This PR builds on #16243 by @mburtin. Thank you, Michael, for tracking down these long-standing layout bugs and for the thorough e2e coverage. This branch keeps your commits as they are and adds a follow-up commit that fixes two issues we found while reviewing.

### Summary

From #16243:

- **#2033**: The panel size is shared across workspaces but was saved at its maximized height, so the next workspace opened with a very tall panel. The last non-maximized size is now saved at shutdown, and the panel height is also saved before the editor is hidden at startup.
- **#3328**: The Side-by-Side layout minimizes the panel, but reloading the window or closing the last editor brought it back. A minimized panel now stays minimized, and `paneCompositePart.ts` no longer restores the panel before the layout has finished restoring.
- **#9463**: Moving the last editor to a new window hid the main editor area, leaving nowhere to drag it back. The editor area now stays visible while editors are open in another window.

### Additional fixes

- **Panel stayed un-maximized after another editor window closed.** The #9463 fix counts editors in every window before maximizing the panel, but that check only ran when the main window's editors changed. If you closed the last editor in the main window while another editor window was open, and then closed that other window, the main window kept an empty editor area and the panel never maximized. The maximize check is now a shared helper (`maybeMaximizePanel`) and also runs on `editorService.onDidVisibleEditorsChange`, which covers every window. It is skipped when the auxiliary bar's forced-maximize setting is on.
- **`panel-size.test.ts` couldn't reach its sibling folder.** The test creates `panel-size-other-project` next to the workspace, but the `openFolder` fixture only goes down from the workspace root. Going up with `..` doesn't work either, because the fixture checks that each path segment disappears after it's selected, and the `..` entry appears in every folder. The test now uses a local `openFolderByPath` helper that types an absolute path into the Open Folder picker.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- The bottom panel keeps its size when you switch to a workspace with no open editors and back (#2033)
- The Side-by-Side layout keeps the panel minimized after a reload or after closing the last editor (#3328)
- Moving the last editor to a new window no longer hides the main editor area (#9463)

### QA Notes

@:layouts

Automated: `panel-size.test.ts` passes locally on e2e-electron. `side-by-side-panel.test.ts` and `editor-area-visibility.test.ts` cover #3328 and #9463.

Manual checks (passes):

1. **#2033**: Resize the panel, open a folder with no files, then return to the original folder. The panel size is kept.
2. **#3328**: Apply the Side-by-Side layout and reload the window, with and without an editor open. The panel stays minimized.
3. **#9463**: Pop out a Data Explorer (`View(mtcars)`) into a new window. The main editor area stays visible, and you can drag the editor back into it.
4. **Closing another editor window**: In the Stacked layout with the panel visible, move one of two open files into a new window, then close the file left in the main window. The panel does not maximize yet. Close the other window. The panel in the main window now maximizes. Open a file, and the panel returns to its earlier height.
5. **No regressions**: With the panel hidden (Cmd+J), repeat step 4 and confirm the panel stays hidden. With the auxiliary bar's forced-maximize setting on, close all editors and confirm the auxiliary bar maximizes and the panel does not.

title: Register discovered runtimes with the startup service
description:
Interpreters found during discovery were only saved to the interpreter cache when they were registered for the first time in the window. If an interpreter was already registered (for example, the workspace's affiliated interpreter, or interpreters loaded from the cache on startup), discovery would report it again but it would not be written back to the cache. Because discovery clears the cache for the languages it scans, those interpreters were dropped. This was most visible after running Clear Interpreter Cache followed by Discover All Interpreters: the next launch showed only some of the installed interpreters.

The fix moves the cache write from the "runtime registered" event to the point where a runtime manager reports a discovered interpreter, so every interpreter found during a discovery pass is cached whether or not it was already registered.

Fixes #16244.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- Fix interpreters going missing from the interpreter list after Clear Interpreter Cache and Discover All Interpreters (#16244)

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:sessions

1. Install at least two versions of R (or Python) and open a workspace whose affiliated interpreter is one of them.
2. Wait for discovery to finish, then run Clear Interpreter Cache followed by Discover All Interpreters.
3. Quit and relaunch Positron.
4. Open the interpreter picker and confirm every installed interpreter is listed, including the one that started with the workspace.

title: Add an MCP to Positron for integrating third-party coding agents into Positron workflows
description: Addresses part of posit-dev/assistant#1872. > [!IMPORTANT] > Depends on posit-dev/kallichore#79. That PR must merge and ship in a Kallichore release first. Then this PR bumps `binaryDependencies.kallichore` before it merges. ### Summary External coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, any MCP client) can now work inside the user's **live** Python and R sessions. They run code, read history, look at plots, and drive Positron commands. Everything they do shows up in the Console with the agent's name on it. This works both in extensions (pictured) and for terminal agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Kiro, etc. The guiding principle here was to give these agents a set of tools comparable to those that our own first-party harness (Posit Assistant) has, so that people can bring their own agent to Positron and have it work alongside them in the IDE. The MCP server lives in the kernel supervisor (Kallichore), not in Positron; see posit-dev/kallichore#79 for more detail on why it lives there and what the architecture looks like. This PR is the Positron half: registration, discovery, agent configuration, command brokering, and console attribution. ### What agents get | Tool | Where it runs | What it does | |---|---|---| | `list_sessions` | Kallichore | Sessions in this workspace, foreground flag, connection state | | `execute_code` | Kallichore | Visible run: echoed in the Console, added to history | | `evaluate_code` | Kallichore | Inspection: shown in the Console, kept out of history | | `interrupt_session` | Kallichore | Stop a running cell | | `get_session_history` | Kallichore | Last 100 executions: input, output, errors, who ran them | | `list_positron_commands` | Kallichore (cached catalog) | Search agent-allowed commands; works while Positron is offline | | `run_positron_command` | Positron | Run one command over the frontend channel | | `get_plot` | Positron | The current plot as an image | - Eight tools, not one per command. Search-then-run keeps agent context small (about 1.5K tokens) no matter how many commands exist. - The command catalog is the same one Posit Assistant uses. Extensions add to it through `contributes.commands[].agent`, with no core changes needed. - **New:** notebook agent commands (create, get cells, insert, update, delete, run). The logic is shared with the `positron.notebooks.*` API in a new `notebookAgentOperations.ts`. The main-thread copy is gone. - Tools never start an interpreter (although agents can start one via a command). Output is capped at 32 KB with in-band `truncated` flags. ### How agents connect To the greatest extent possible I've made everything self-configuring by putting the MCP data in places where agents will find it. For manual installation there's a new _Add to Coding Agent_ command: - **Claude Code:** configured automatically, once per workspace, in local scope. It stays out of the repo and needs no approval prompt. - **Codex, Gemini CLI:** one command, _Positron MCP: Add to Coding Agent_. - **VS Code chat / Copilot:** found automatically through an `mcpServerDefinitionProvider`. - **Anything else:** _Copy Connection Details_ gives a URL and token. - **Integrated terminals and the extension host** get `POSITRON_MCP_URL` and `POSITRON_MCP_TOKEN`. ### Console attribution When an agent executes code in the console, a sparkle and the agent's name are shown next to it. Details: - New runtime message `ExecutionRequested`, sent by Kallichore before the code runs. - New `CodeAttributionSource.Agent`. - Agent-run input gets a label in the Console (e.g. "Claude Code"). You can always tell agent code from your own. - The busy indicator follows agent executions. `onDidExecuteCode` fires with agent metadata, so console history and API consumers see it too. ### Visibility The kernel supervisor now shows connected sessions _and_ agents. You can also optionally see connected agents in the status bar: ### Admin controls & configuration - **Off by default.** `ai.mcp.enabled` is `false` and tagged experimental. - **Under the main switch.** The server runs only when `ai.enabled` **and** `ai.mcp.enabled` are both on. Admins can force either off with `POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS`. - **Live.** Toggling takes effect with no reload. Turning it off deregisters the workspace, closes the port once nothing else is registered, clears env vars, and **removes Positron from every agent config it wrote**. - **One polite offer.** If a supported agent is installed, Positron offers to enable the feature once per user. It never offers when AI is off. - **No always-on port.** The listener opens when the first workspace registers and closes when the last one leaves. ### Auditability - Every agent execution is visible in the Console, labeled with the agent's name. - Kallichore forwards agent execution events to Positron. They are emitted with agent attribution to Positron's code execution notification API, for use in Workbench. - Kallichore keeps a per-session execution history that records who ran each execution. - The Kernel Supervisor output channel logs at info level: - registration and deregistration, with the endpoint URL - agent connect and disconnect - every tool call: tool, agent, outcome, duration - every Positron command: command, agent, outcome, duration - Full code is logged at debug only. Tokens are never logged. ### Security - **Loopback only.** The server binds `127.0.0.1`. Non-loopback `Host` or `Origin` gets a 403, which blocks DNS rebinding as the MCP spec requires. - **Separate tokens.** Each workspace gets its own 32-byte bearer token, distinct from the supervisor API token. An MCP token cannot create sessions, pass argv, kill processes, or shut down the supervisor. - **Small blast radius.** A token reaches one workspace's sessions and the agent-allowed commands. Nothing more. - **Constant-time compare.** Kallichore never writes the token to disk. - **Locked-down files.** Connection files are `0600` in a `0700` directory. The folder index holds no tokens. - **Command args checked.** Arguments are type-checked against each command's schema before anything runs. Bad calls are refused with `invalid-args`. - **Kernels as callers.** Kernels get a session-scoped URL, which can only narrow access. A kernel can't run code in its own session, so it can't deadlock itself (`SESSION_IS_CALLER`). - **Trust boundary.** The token is visible to processes launched from this window's terminals. That is the same boundary as the user's shell. - **Consent.** Positron adds no approval dialog. Claude Code and Codex already prompt before tool calls. A second dialog would double-prompt, and it couldn't be shown while Positron is disconnected. Console attribution plus logs are the audit trail. ### Release Notes #### New Features - Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI can connect to Positron's Python and R sessions through a built-in MCP server. They can run code, see plots, and run Positron commands, and agent-run code is labeled in the Console. Turn it on with the experimental `ai.mcp.enabled` setting. #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:mcp @:console @:sessions @:positron-notebooks @:plots The new MCP e2e suite covers Python and R execution with attribution, busy state and interrupt, plots, silent evaluation, command search and run, token rejection, and a stdio agent end to end. The stdio test needs the bumped `kcserver`. Unit coverage: - Extension mocha: agent config writers, frontend, channel, command args and results, server definitions. - Vitest: console attribution, notebook agent commands and operations. Manual: 1. Turn on `ai.mcp.enabled`. Open a workspace with Claude Code installed. 2. Start a Python console. Open a **new** terminal and run `claude`. 3. Ask it to make a plot of some data. - The code appears in the Console with a "Claude Code" label, and the plot appears in the Plots pane. 4. Run _Kernel Supervisor: Show Kernel Supervisor_. - Claude Code is listed under "Coding Agents". 5. Reload the window while the agent works. - The agent keeps going. The attributed activity appears after the reload. 6. Run _Positron MCP: Add to Coding Agent_ and pick Codex. - `~/.codex/config.toml` gets a `positron` stdio entry. 7. Turn off `ai.enabled`. - The Claude Code and Codex entries are removed. - New terminals no longer have `POSITRON_MCP_*` vars. - The Kernel Supervisor log shows the deregistration.

title: Move provider authentication for API-key and Posit AI Pass providers to Posit Assistant
description:
Moves authentication for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, Gemini, DeepSeek, custom providers and Posit AI Pass from Positron's authentication extension to Posit Assistant, and renames every auth provider to its catalog id. Second of three coordinated PRs with posit-dev/ai-lib#114 and posit-dev/assistant#2450; none merges until all three are approved. Builds on George's `prototype/local-assistant-auth` branch. Part of #14190.

- The authentication extension now registers only Bedrock, Google Vertex, Foundry, Snowflake Cortex and Databricks, with Bedrock and Vertex renamed to `bedrock` and `google-vertex`.
- Removes the core provider configuration modal and the `positron.ai` API behind it. The configure-providers entry points open Assistant's provider manager instead.
- Lets extensions open webview panels in the modal editor part, which Assistant uses for its provider manager.
- Extensions granted auth access in `product.json` skip the create-session consent prompt.
- Positron copies every credential the authentication extension stored for a moved provider into Assistant's secret store once per profile at startup: API keys, custom provider entries and the Posit AI Pass token set. The originals stay in place and a key Assistant already holds is not overwritten. If no secret is readable yet, the copy runs again on the next launch.
- Grants Assistant access to the moved providers under their catalog ids in `product.json`.
- Next Edit Suggestions reads the Posit AI Pass session as `positai` and depends on Posit Assistant instead of the authentication extension.
- Pins ai-lib to posit-dev/ai-lib#114 so the headless language model service resolves each provider's auth id as its catalog id.
- Renames the provider ids in the e2e page objects and skips the suites that drove the removed modal until the provider manager has a page object.

## Phase 2

- Decides per-provider ownership from the auth ids Positron's manifest still declares, replacing the hardcoded host-owned list, so a newer Assistant defers automatically once an older Positron drops a provider's registration.
- Deletes Positron's Microsoft Foundry auth provider; Assistant now serves it, including the Workbench-delegated bearer and Entra mode.
- Core's headless service (Git Suggestions, notebook AI) synthesizes the same Entra credential from the catalog that Assistant's own requests use, so Foundry works in both without a stored session.
- Copies a stored Foundry API key into Assistant's credential store alongside the Phase 1 providers, so a user signed in before this change stays signed in.

Smoke-tested by hand: credentials saved on `main` appear in Assistant after one launch of this branch with the matching Assistant build, and the Assistant branch still signs in against a `main` Positron.

title: e2e: unskip four tests whose blocking issues are closed
description:
Unskips four e2e tests whose blocking issues are closed. First PR from an audit of every skip under `test/e2e/`.

### Summary

| Test | Was skipped for | Why it can run now |
|---|---|---|
| `autocomplete.test.ts` R autocomplete in Console and Editor | #15211 Ark LSP hang | Closed 2026-07-31. The fix (posit-dev/ark#1369) is in the Ark submodule since #15226. |
| `code-actions/r.test.ts` R Ctrl+Enter in untitled file | #11533, #15211 | Both closed. The #11533 annotation stays as the test's origin. |
| `new-folder-flow-jupyter.test.ts` suite | #14163 | The issue shows as closed, but the skip PR #14812 closed it by accident: its body said "Skipping until it's resolved: <url>" and GitHub treated "resolved" as a closing keyword. The in-test workarounds and the annotation stay until the suite proves green here. |
| `r-session-hooks.test.ts` window reload fires only session_reconnect | #7593 | Closed 2026-05-28, five days before the skip landed. See below. |

The session hooks reload test passed once and failed twice locally with `--repeat-each 3`. The failing assertion was the last one, which checks that `[.Rprofile] top-level code executed` is absent from the console. Every earlier assertion passed, including the global-variable marker that proves the R process did not restart. The text is replayed console history: output printed outside an execution (the startup output from the restart test) survives Clear Console and is replayed after Reload Window. That is a product bug, filed as #16333. This PR drops the redundant console-text assertion; the marker check already proves `.Rprofile` did not run again.

Local results, electron, three repeats each: 3 of 4 files green on the first run. The session hooks file is green on three repeats after the assertion change.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
