title: 15463 provide better progress ux for connections connecting data explorer etc
description:
Fixes #15463 ### Summary This PR addresses a range of problems with slow-to-load databases in the Data Explorer. Opening a table or view backed by a slow connection used to show a blank window for as long as the backend took to answer, with no indication that anything was happening, and several of the ways that wait could end left the UI stuck in a state it never recovered from. The work here makes the wait legible, makes the failure modes honest, changes how column summaries are fetched so that slow sources deliver what they can instead of nothing at all, and fixes the layout and caching bugs that surfaced along the way. **A progress indicator while the grid has nothing to paint.** `DataGridInstance` gains a `loading` property. While it is true the grid paints a centered indeterminate indicator instead of headers, corners and rows, rather than painting them from information it would have to guess at and then correct. Both the table summary panel and the table data panel use it: the data grid waits until it has the table's shape and its measured column widths, and the summary panel waits until it knows how many columns there are. The summary panel drops its action bar for the duration, since there is nothing yet to sort or filter, which also lines its indicator up with the data grid's rather than sitting 36px below it. The indicator fades in over 150ms on an ease-in curve, so a table that opens promptly is already painted before there is anything to see and only a table that keeps you waiting is announced. **Placeholders for the parts that arrive later, and for the parts that are not coming.** Once the grid can lay itself out, the pieces still in flight are drawn as placeholder marks rather than as blanks: cells whose data has not arrived, and column headers whose schema has not arrived. `TableDataCache.getRowLabel` now distinguishes three states instead of two, so an unlabeled table's row numbers appear immediately, while a table that does have row labels -- which are fetched separately from the shape -- shows a placeholder in that column until they land, rather than briefly showing row numbers that are then replaced by labels. A placeholder pulses because work is under way, so when a fetch comes back with nothing the marks stop moving: the cache reports that its last attempt delivered nothing and the grid paints a steady, dimmed mark in the same place rather than animating indefinitely for a request nobody is waiting on. All the placeholder animations honor `prefers-reduced-motion`. **Column summaries are fetched in two passes.** Every backend answers a batch of profile requests with one aggregate query covering all of its columns and then one further query per column for that column's histogram or frequency table. The null counts come out of the shared aggregate and are close to free; the histograms are the per-column work, and on a slow source they are the whole cost. Asking for both together held the cheap half hostage to the expensive half, so a source that could not draw a window's worth of sparklines inside the timeout also failed to report a single missing-value count, though it had them in hand. The passes are now separate: null counts for the whole visible window go out as a single request, and the histograms, frequency tables and summary statistics follow in chunks. The missing-values bars land for every column almost at once, and the sparklines fill in behind them at whatever rate the source can manage. **Chunks size themselves to the source.** The detail pass used a fixed eight columns per request, which is a bet on what a column costs -- and that figure spans orders of magnitude between a local parquet file and a remote warehouse. A source at two seconds a column failed a batch of eight and would have comfortably managed two. Each pass now probes with a single column, measures it, and sizes the chunks after it to land near three seconds, clamped between one and eight. The measured rate is kept per table, so only the first pass pays for the probe and later scrolling goes straight to the fitted size. Splitting the passes turned out to help here too: by the time the probe runs, the backend state, the schema and the whole null-count aggregate have already been fetched, so the probe measures marginal per-column cost rather than connection setup and cold cache. **Three ways summaries can come up short, and three different things to say.** Previously a failure was silent: the request timed out, the error was logged to the devtools console and swallowed, and every column from the failing batch onward kept a pulsing loading placeholder forever. Now the summary panel reports what happened in a notice row above the column list, and what it says depends on which of these it was. A source that cannot summarize says "Summaries unavailable." with a Retry, or "Some summaries unavailable." where earlier chunks succeeded and their sparklines are on screen. A source that has gone away says so instead, and carries no button, because there is nothing to ask a second time. A source that is answering but slowly says "Summaries paused." with a Continue -- see below. In every case the panel keeps the column names and types it did get, so it remains useful for browsing and filtering, and the columns render with empty summary slots instead of placeholders for work that is over. **A pass that is working but not worth waiting for stops and says so.** A request timeout catches a source that has failed. It has nothing to say about one that is succeeding too slowly to be worth it: a source at two seconds a column never times out -- every chunk of one succeeds -- and would grind through a wide window for minutes while reporting progress the whole time. The detail pass now has a wall-clock budget of thirty seconds, after which it stops, keeps what it computed, and reports. Because results are merged into the cache field by field and a profile already in hand is never requested again, Continue resumes from where the pass stopped with a fresh budget rather than starting over, which is why it is not labelled Retry. **Timeouts that reflect what the user is waiting for.** The `get_column_profiles` timeout was an inline `60000` commented "for now just in case". It is now a documented constant at 10 seconds. With chunks sizing themselves, what this number mostly governs is the probe -- the one column a pass asks about before it knows anything about the source -- and ten seconds is about as long as a single column is worth waiting for, since a source that cannot produce one in that time will not produce the next twenty any faster. It is bounded below by the 10 seconds `GetDataValues` is given, since summaries should not outrank the grid but a batch of histograms is more work than a page of cells, and above by the 30 seconds `updateBackendState` allows for pending tasks to clear. Chunks aim at three seconds rather than at the timeout, so a chunk that comes in three times slower than the one before it still lands inside the budget instead of taking the whole panel down with it. **Correctness fixes found along the way.** - Pending backend requests were never settled when the comm closed, so a runtime that went away left its callers awaiting a result that could not arrive, freed only by their own timeout. `onDidClose` and `dispose` now reject them. - `updateBackendState` cleared its in-flight promise only on success, so one rejection left a rejected promise in the field for the life of the client and every later caller got that same rejection back. This made the retry-on-becoming-visible path unreachable as written. It is now cleared in a `finally`. - Rejecting those pending requests on close exposed an ordering bug: their continuations run as microtasks after `Disconnected` is set, and the last one to drain returned the client to `Idle`, after which requests went out to a closed comm. - A zero-column table (`pd.DataFrame()`) left both panels spinning forever, because the transition out of loading fired no event and there were no rows to fetch. Both panels now announce the transition themselves. - A rejected initial load left a permanent indeterminate spinner instead of an empty grid, recoverable only by hiding and re-showing the editor. The data grid and the summary panel now both recover from this; the summary panel additionally gets its sort and filter bar back rather than losing it along with the rows. - A profile pass could finish having loaded nothing without ever throwing, because a client whose comm has closed answers with an empty array rather than rejecting. That cleared the failure state, took away the notice, and left every column on a placeholder. A pass now checks that it got what it asked for. - Scrolling or resizing the summary panel during a retry cancelled it, because an ordinary update and a retry shared one cancellation token -- so the notice vanished the moment the user touched anything. Ordinary updates now hold off for the length of a retry and catch up afterwards; an invalidating update still cancels it, since the data underneath has changed. - A deferred column-width recalculation could be dropped precisely when it was needed, leaving columns measured with a stale font after an editor-font change during the initial load. Calculator sets are now generation-counted. - The summary action bar spanned from its own row to the data grid, so inserting the notice row between them silently widened that span to cover both. - A column displaying a missing-values percentage could carry a tooltip saying that value could not be calculated, because the panel-wide failure state was consulted before the column's own figures. ### Screenshots This screen recording was rigged for slowness, so the loading indicators and placeholders stay on screen long enough to see. On a real connection most of them never appear at all: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3edb0a07-f8c4-4f15-8100-dd9e31471d42 Under good conditions, a user may briefly see the loading spinners, but will probably not see the column header and row label placeholders. When the user scrolls to a range of cells that takes a moment to load, each cell paints an animated ... after a delay so the wait reads as data on its way rather than as empty cells:

When a source cannot produce column summaries, the panel says so and offers a retry, instead of leaving the loading placeholders pulsing indefinitely:

### Release Notes #### New Features - The Data Explorer now shows a progress indicator while a slow table or view is loading, and placeholders for cells, column headers and row labels that have not arrived yet (#15463) - The Data Explorer now loads column summaries in two passes and sizes its requests to what the data source can deliver, so slow sources show missing-value counts promptly and fill in their sparklines as they can (#15463) #### Bug Fixes - The Data Explorer summary panel now reports when column summaries cannot be calculated, when the data source has disconnected, and when they are taking too long to be worth waiting for, instead of showing loading placeholders indefinitely (#15463) - Fixed the Data Explorer showing a progress indicator forever for a table with no columns, or after a failed initial load (#15463) - Fixed Data Explorer cells and row labels animating as though they were loading after the request for them had failed (#15463) - Fixed scrolling or resizing the Data Explorer summary panel cancelling a column summary retry that was in progress (#15463) ### Validation Steps @:data-explorer @:connections @:duck-db 1. Open a large or slow database table or view in the Data Explorer. Press Retry and confirm the row changes to "Calculating summaries..." while it runs. 7. Press Retry and, while "Calculating summaries..." is showing, scroll the summary panel and drag the splitter. Confirm the notice stays and the retry is not cancelled. 9. title: Pass through console document `id` from rstudioapi editor context
description:
- Fixes #15571
- Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1408

RStudio's `rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()` returns the console's context when the console has focus: path `""`, `id` `"#console"`, the console input, and the selection. Positron's shim returned the last active editor pane instead. A call from the console returned a stale editor context.

This PR makes `ExtHostMethods.lastActiveEditorContext()` and `modifyEditorLocations()` console-aware. When the calling kernel's own console is active and has focus, these methods use the console's context instead of the last editor. If not, they fall back to the editor pane. This matches current behavior.

With that change in the ark PR, the console context now reports `id: "#console"`. The two PRs can merge in either order.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- `rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()`, `getSourceEditorContext()`, `insertText()`, and `documentPath()` now target the console when it has focus, to match behavior from RStudio (#15571).

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

I think it's best to do manual testing using a keyboard shortcut bound to `workbench.action.executeCode.console`. An RStudio addin or keybinding normally runs `rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()`, not the console input. Do something like this:

```json
{
  "key": "cmd+alt+shift+g",
  "command": "workbench.action.executeCode.console",
  "args": {
    "langId": "r",
    "code": "str(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext())",
    "focus": false
  }
}
```

`focus: false` runs the code without a change in keyboard focus. The pane you clicked stays focused, the same as with an RStudio addin shortcut.

- Click into the console input. Then press the shortcut. Confirm that `path` is `""`, `id` is `"#console"`, and the contents and selection match the console input.
- Click into an editor. Then press the shortcut. Confirm that it returns the editor's context instead, the same as current RStudio behavior.
- Run an R session and a Python session together. Make the Python console active. Press an R-bound shortcut. Confirm that it falls back to the editor context. The active console's session does not match the caller's session.
- Make the R console active. Confirm that the R shortcut now returns the R console's context.
- Run the same checks with `rstudioapi::insertText()`. Confirm that it edits the console when the console has focus and a matching session. Confirm that it edits the editor pane in all other cases.

title: e2e: accept single-library install.packages() output in the package helper
description:
Fixes the "R - Renv already installed" New Folder Flow test, which has failed on every Windows main run since #16172 (runs 35773169885, 35798066802, 35857564194). ### Summary `packages.manage('renv', 'install')` waited for `/Installing|Downloading|Fetched/` in the console. For base R the only line that matches is the `Installing package into '...' (as 'lib' is unspecified)` header, and R prints that header only when the session has more than one library path. Since rig 0.10.0 reached winget, `rig add` is a no-op on the Windows e2e lane because the runner image already ships R 4.6.1. The user library that a real `rig add` used to create (`AppData/Local/R/win-library/4.6`) no longer exists, so `rig system add-pak` and `pak::local_install_dev_deps()` install into the system library at `C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.1\library` instead. The R session then has a single library, `install.packages()` skips the header, and the first thing it prints is `trying URL`. The install itself succeeds; the failing snapshot shows `trying URL ... downloaded 2.5 MB ... package 'renv' successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked`. The fix also accepts `trying URL`, which R prints on every platform whenever it downloads a package. The helper already waits for the call to return and confirms `requireNamespace("renv")` is `TRUE` afterwards, so the regex only needs to prove the install started. `remove.packages()` prints its "Removing package from" header unconditionally, which is why the sibling "R - Cancel Renv install" test kept passing. Not changed here: the Windows lane now installs R packages into the system library rather than a user library. That is a side effect of #16172 worth knowing about separately, since it also changes what the R package cache path covers. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A (test infrastructure only) ### Validation Steps @:win @:new-folder-flow The Windows e2e job is the test. Confirm "R - Renv already installed" passes on the Windows lane, and the New Folder Flow suite stays green on the other platforms (which have multiple libraries and still print the header). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Since rig 0.10.0 (+ #16172) the Windows e2e lane has a single R library, so install.packages() no longer prints the Installing package into header the test regex /Installing|Downloading|Fetched/ depends on - **Test:** [New Folder Flow: R Project > R - Renv already installed](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=New%20Folder%20Flow%3A%20R%20Project%20%3E%20R%20-%20Renv%20already%20installed%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fnew-folder-flow%2Fnew-folder-flow-r.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** expect(getByText(/Installing|Downloading|Fetched/)).toBeVisible() 15s timeout in packageManager.ts:41 during packages.manage(renv, install); win/electron only; 3/3 main runs since 458f9d0ac4 - **Signal:** Snapshot shows install.packages output trying URL -> downloaded -> successfully unpacked with no Installing package into line; R source prints that header only when length(.libPaths()) > 1; failing shard log: pak Package library at C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.1\library (rig add was a no-op, rig system add-pak printed no Installing package into); passing shard (rig 0.8.1): pak installed into win-library/4.6 user lib. remove.packages prints Removing unconditionally, which is why the sibling uninstall test still passes. - **Frequency:** 3/63 runs (4.8%) on main, win/electron - **Hypothesis:** infra

title: Fix unusable ODBC data sources and notify on connection failures
description: Fixes #15794 Discovery in Data Connections now checks whether each ODBC data source's driver can actually be resolved. It drops a data source from the pane if the driver's library file is missing, or if no driver by that name is registered. A data source whose driver does resolve, but declares no server or database, shows "No server configured" instead of looking like a working connection. The extension's own messages are clearer now too. Three common unixODBC driver-manager diagnostics are rewritten into plain sentences the user can act on, instead of raw driver-manager text. Separately, any Data Connections driver whose connection fails to open or expand now shows a notification with the error message. Before this change, the only sign of failure was an error icon whose message was a native tooltip, easy to miss, but now you can see them: ### Release Notes #### New Features - Show a notification when a data connection fails to open or expand #### Bug Fixes - Stop listing ODBC data sources whose driver cannot be resolved, and explain why in the output channel (#15794) - Label an ODBC data source that declares no endpoint as unconfigured, instead of looking like a working connection (#15794) - Rewrite raw unixODBC driver-manager errors into messages the user can act on (#15794) ### Validation Steps @:connections @:workbench 1. Register an ODBC driver in `odbcinst.ini` that points at a library file that does not exist, and add a DSN in `odbc.ini` naming that driver. Add a second DSN naming a driver that is not registered anywhere. 2. Open the Data Connections pane. Neither data source should appear. 3. Open the "Data Connections: ODBC" output channel. It should explain why each was dropped, even before you make any connection. 4. Add a DSN whose driver resolves but declares no server or database. It should appear in the pane and read "No server configured". 5. Try to connect to any data source that will fail (wrong password, unreachable server, etc.) and confirm a notification appears with the error message, alongside the usual error icon on the tree row.

title: drive-positron: force in-app dialogs and call playwright-cli directly
description:
### Summary
The drive-positron skill can now dismiss modal message boxes (save-changes prompts and the like), which were native macOS sheets invisible to CDP, keeps working when its window is covered, and stops paying npx's per-call resolve cost.
- Launcher forces `window.dialogStyle: "custom"` into the disposable profile so modals render in the DOM
- Launcher passes `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` and `--disable-renderer-backgrounding` so clicks no longer time out when the window is behind other windows
- SKILL.md examples and helper scripts call `node_modules/.bin/playwright-cli` directly, with an npx fallback
- SKILL.md documents the two kinds of modal, ref-scoped snapshots, strict-mode selector uniqueness, and running `stop.sh` on its own
- `launch-positron` command gains a worktree preflight for a copied or half-installed `node_modules`, a note on stale `build-check` errors, and `--use-inmemory-secretstorage`

### QA Notes
Compared against main with 4 agent-driven UI tasks x 3 runs each (24 runs, macOS only): same 100% task completion, mean run time 192s vs 271s. The dialog-style change is what carries that; without it every old-skill run of the save-prompt task needed an AppleScript or relaunch workaround. The occlusion flags were verified separately by covering the window with a full-screen Finder window: without them the page reports hidden and clicks time out in 5s, with them (2 of 2 runs) frames keep firing and clicks land. Not exercised on Linux or Windows.

title: e2e: move Snowflake tests off the retired legacy service account
description:
Snowflake retired legacy service accounts on 2026-09-22, which disabled `SVC_WORKBENCH_TEST_USER`, the user every password-based Snowflake test authenticated as. Four suites went red on main at once (both Snowflake e2e cases on Linux, the pytest Snowflake connections suite, and the Workbench Session Credentials sign-in), all with `Incorrect username or password was specified`.

### Summary

The replacement credential is the shared IDE service account (`RStudioIDE_Service_Account` in 1Password) with a programmatic access token, which Snowflake accepts wherever a password is expected. The `SNOWFLAKE_USER` / `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD` repo secrets have already been rotated to it. That alone fixed the Python connections e2e test and the pytest suite with no code change (verified in runs 35783524039 and 35783542005). This PR covers what the secrets alone do not:

- **Workbench Session Credentials widget.** `dashboard.page.ts` typed the legacy username and password into Snowflake's native form. The IDE service account signs in through Okta, so the page object now clicks "Sign in using Okta" and reuses `completeOktaSignIn`, mirroring the Databricks widget flow. The Workbench lane's `SNOWFLAKE_USERNAME` / `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD` now come from the token fields on the IDE service account item, for the connections.toml the catalog explorer case writes on that lane.
- **Catalog explorer Snowflake case.** The new account's role sees several dozen databases, listed alphabetically, and the Catalog Explorer section shows only a few rows of a virtualized tree, so `FINANCIAL__ECONOMIC_ESSENTIALS` sat below the fold and was never rendered. The test now scrolls the row into the rendered range before asserting on it.

The token expires 2027-09-22. The expiry is recorded on the 1Password item and in a comment in the Workbench workflow. Sibling ticket for Workbench's own tests: rstudio/rstudio-pro#12901.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:catalog-explorer @:connections @:workbench @:workbench-snowflake

The catalog explorer and connections suites exercise the rotated secrets on the Linux lane. The two Workbench shards exercise the Okta sign-in for the Session Credentials widget and the connections.toml path on Workbench. The Windows and web lanes pick up the catalog explorer case through the nightly full suite.

title: ci: install pak explicitly on the Windows e2e lane
description:
Fixes the Windows e2e lane, which has failed at the "Install R packages" step with `Error in loadNamespace(x) : there is no package called 'pak'` since rig 0.10.0 reached winget.

### Summary

Two things collided:

1. **rig 0.10.0** (released 2026-09-21) added a skip-if-already-installed path to `rig add` (`report_already_installed` in `src/common.rs`). It only fixes up aliases -- it does **not** install pak. rig 0.8.1 reinstalled unconditionally and always printed `Installing pak for R <ver> (if not installed yet)`.
2. The **`windows-2025-vs2026` runner image ships R 4.6.1**, which is exactly what the workflow's r-hub `r-release` lookup resolves.

So `rig add $release` became a 4ms no-op and pak never arrived:

```
[INFO] RIG START [pid:23804] C:\Program Files\rig\rig.exe add 4.6.1
R version 4.6.1 is already installed
[INFO] RIG END [pid:23804] C:\Program Files\rig\rig.exe add 4.6.1
```

It is rig and not the image: the last passing run ([35637890985](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35637890985)) and the first failing one ([35745358762](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35745358762)) ran on the identical image version `20260907.229.1`; the only delta is `Found rig [Posit.rig] Version 0.8.1` -> `0.10.0`. The 09-22 00:28 run still got 0.8.1 from winget and passed R setup.

The fix stops relying on `rig add`'s side effect and calls `rig system add-pak` (still present in 0.10.0, and idempotent) after `rig default`, so the lane works whether or not rig performed a real install.

**Blast radius:** Windows only. macOS and Ubuntu runner images do not preinstall R, so `rig add` there is a real install and still brings pak -- even though `test-e2e-macos-run.yml` and `test-e2e-connect.yml` both track rig *latest* and share the same assumption. `.github/actions/setup-release-screenshot-runtimes/action.yml` is already immune because it guards with `if (!requireNamespace('pak', ...)) install.packages('pak', ...)`.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A (CI only)

### Validation Steps

@:win

The Windows e2e job is itself the test. Confirm in this PR's run that:

1. The "Install default R and resolve versions" step logs `Installing pak for R 4.6.1 (if not installed yet)` after `rig default`, even though `rig add` reports `R version 4.6.1 is already installed`.
2. The "Install R packages (default R version)" step completes instead of failing on `there is no package called 'pak'`.
3. Windows tests run to completion as they did before rig 0.10.0.

title: ci: e2e triage reads workflow steps; report dirs include arch
description:
The e2e failure analyzer diagnosed nightly run
[35712128283](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/35712128283)'s
Windows arm64 R failures as a **product regression**. R had never installed on that
runner.

Two independent blind spots let that happen, and this PR closes both.

### 1. The analyzer never looked at the job's workflow steps

GitHub keeps a job running past a failed step whenever the later steps carry their own
`if:` conditions. On that job, step #23 `Install R 4.4.0` failed:

```
Error: Installation failed: could not find the newly installed R in the registry.
```

`Install R packages for 4.4.0`, `Install R 4.4.2` and `Set up Quarto` were skipped as a
result, and step #34 ran the whole R suite anyway. The Playwright report only knows the
tests failed -- the step conclusions are the sole evidence. `e2e-gather-run-info.js`
asked the jobs API for `{id, name}` and discarded `steps[]`.

Each failed job now carries a `steps` summary: the test-execution step with its
conclusion, plus `failedBeforeTest` (each with a log tail), `skippedAfterFailure`,
`failedAfterTest`, and `failedUnpositioned`. Steps come from the existing jobs call, so
there is **no extra API cost**; a job log is fetched only when there is a pre-test
failure, and its tail is sliced by the step's `started_at`/`completed_at` against the
runner's line timestamps, cut after the step's own error marker, with the `env:` preamble
dropped.

The Action renders this as a `## Job setup step failures` section **before** any test
evidence, repeated as a warning on the affected project's header:

```
- Job: e2e / desktop / electron (windows arm64) (id 106695031392)
  Evidence bundle: e2e-desktop-electron-windows-arm64
  Test step: #34 "Run Tests on Windows (Electron)" -- failure
  FAILED before the tests ran:
    - #23 "Install R 4.4.0"
        ...rig output...
        Process completed with exit code 1.
  Skipped after that failure: #24 "Install R packages for 4.4.0", #25 "Install R 4.4.2",
  #27 "Set up Quarto", ...

Failed jobs whose setup DID complete: e2e / desktop / connect, ... (9 jobs)
```

`rubric.md` -- shared verbatim by the skill and the Action -- gains **"Check the job's
own setup steps before blaming the product"** as its first section. It routes such a
failure to `infrastructure issue` owned by the CI workflow, and names two traps this run
demonstrated:

- **Do not unify a failure across platforms when only one had a broken setup.** The same
  three R tests were reported for arm64 and x64 as one product regression. x64's setup
  was clean, so that finding stands on its own and is now stronger for not being averaged
  with a runner that had no R.
- **Do not read a partial success in the logs as a complete environment.** R 4.4.0
  started fine on arm64 (`Ark (R 4.4.0 language client) ... init successful`) while every
  follow-on install step was skipped. The fixture is `engine: knitr`, and knitr arrives
  transitively through the deps that skipped step installs.

### 2. Report directories collided across architectures

Found while re-running the analysis: the arm64 and x64 evidence bundles were
**byte-identical, down to the log timestamps**. `gen-report-dir` named reports
`{run_id}-{attempt}-{identifier}-{os}` with no arch, so both Windows nightly jobs
resolved to `playwright-report-35712128283-1-electron-windows` and overwrote each other
in S3. The analyzer processed one report twice under two platform labels.

The step timings this PR now surfaces settle whose survived:

| job | tests ran | uploaded |
|---|---|---|
| windows arm64 | 10:27:30 - 10:40:33 (13 min) | 10:40:47 |
| windows x64 | 10:36:56 - 11:57:01 (80 min) | **11:57:16** |

The surviving report's internal events are at 11:37-11:42, inside x64's window. **arm64's
report was destroyed and its results are gone from that run.**

Report dirs are now `...-{identifier}-{os}-{arch}`. The new `arch` input defaults to
`runner.arch`, correct wherever the job that runs the tests also generates the dir.

`test-e2e-macos-run.yml` is the exception: its `merge-reports` job runs on a fixed
`macos-latest`, and `test-full-suite.yml` calls that workflow **twice** with the same
`project: "e2e-macOS-ci"` and only `arch:` differing -- so positron's own full suite has
the same collision, and a bare `runner.arch` would not have fixed it. That job passes
`arch` explicitly.

`rubric.md` also learns the diagnostic, for older runs and any future identifier clash:
byte-identical evidence on two platforms is a collision, not a correlation, and the
overwritten platform's results are unrecoverable rather than shared.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

No product code changes -- this touches CI tooling and the analyzer skill only.

**Caller audit.** All 20 `gen-report-dir` call sites checked against their jobs'
`runs-on`. The sharded pairs that must agree on a name are x64 on both sides and still
resolve identically; macOS was the only mismatch:

| workflow | report-generating job | arch source |
|---|---|---|
| `test-e2e-windows-run.yml` | shard `windows-latest-8x` + merge `windows-latest` | both x64, agree |
| `test-e2e-ubuntu-run.yml` | shard `ubuntu-latest-8x` + merge `ubuntu-latest` | both x64, agree |
| `test-e2e-macos-run.yml` | merge `macos-latest` | **explicit `inputs.arch`** |
| all others | same job as the tests | `runner.arch` default |

**Naming logic** simulated over every real and degenerate case:

```
nightly windows arm64  -> ...-electron-windows-arm64
nightly windows x64    -> ...-electron-windows-x64     (was: both -electron-windows)
full-suite macOS arm64 -> ...-macOS-ci-macos-arm64
full-suite macOS x64   -> ...-macOS-ci-macos-x64       (merge job, explicit arch)
sharded windows shard  -> ...-windows-windows-x64
sharded windows merge  -> ...-windows-windows-x64      (still agree)
explicit empty arch    -> falls back to RUNNER_ARCH
RUNNER_ARCH also empty -> "unknown", not a trailing dash
secret-masked ident    -> masked prefix still stripped
```

**Analyzer verified against real runs**, both data paths:

- positron-builds s3 path (run 35712128283): flags arm64's `Install R 4.4.0` with the rig
  error, attaches it to `e2e-desktop-electron-windows-arm64` only, and lists the other 9
  failed jobs as setup-clean.
- positron blob path (`Test: Merge to branch` runs
  [35667860236](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35667860236),
  [35387261436](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35387261436)):
  surfaced two findings the analyzer had no way to report before -- `Setup Graphviz`
  failing on a Chocolatey 503, and `Install node dependencies` failing, each with the
  Playwright step **skipped**, i.e. a whole shard's tests never ran.

Two false positives showed up during that grounding and are fixed: the setup/test
boundary matched `Run Boostrap extension test` instead of the real Playwright step, and
the `e2e / electron-win` aggregator's `Check test results` gate was being reported as a
broken setup step (jobs with no identifiable test step now go to a separate
`failedUnpositioned` bucket rather than asserting an order).

The analyzer's `awk` extraction still resolves `REPORT_DIR` from job logs with the new
segment and still skips the unexpanded template line. Both YAML files parse, the skill's
11 unit tests pass, and `npm run precommit` is clean.

**What local checks cannot cover:** the first real run on this branch is what proves the
arch suffix end to end -- that each job uploads to its own directory and the analyzer
resolves it. Worth watching one nightly before trusting it.

### Notes for review

- **Existing reports keep the old names.** Nothing reads these paths by pattern in-repo,
  so nothing breaks, but bookmarked URLs and anything reconstructing the path externally
  will need the arch segment going forward.
- **positron-builds picks this up via the submodule** (its nightly calls
  `./positron/.github/actions/gen-report-dir`). Its jobs are single-job per OS/arch, so
  the default is right for them -- but a future merge job there on a fixed runner would
  need the explicit `arch` input the same way macOS does.
- `e2e-gather-run-info.js` has no unit tests, so `summarizeSteps` / `sliceStepLog` are
  covered only by the live runs above. Happy to add some if you'd like the boundary
  heuristics pinned down.

title: Normalize CRLF before splitting Quarto cells into statements
description:
Fixes a Windows-only regression in Quarto inline output: running a multi-statement R cell in a CRLF document failed with `Syntax error: unexpected invalid token` and produced no output. ### Summary `_getCodeInRange` returned the cell text with the document's own EOL, and `_getCodeFragmentsFromBoundaries` then split on `\n` and rejoined on `\n`. On a CRLF document that leaves a trailing carriage return on every line but the last, so each non-final fragment reached the kernel ending in a bare CR -- which R rejects as an invalid token. The first statement errored and the rest of the cell never ran. This was latent until the Ark bump in #16146 (posit-dev/ark#1408). posit-dev/ark#1400 made `strings::lines` strip `\r`, and that function is used only by the `positron/inputBoundaries` handler. Before it, CRLF text failed to parse and came back as a single `invalid` boundary, so Positron sent the whole cell as one request and the CRLF was harmless inside the string. After it, boundaries come back as per-statement `complete` ranges and the statement-splitting path activates. The Ark change is correct -- it stopped masking this one. The fix normalizes where the executed code is read, matching what the Console already does in `enqueueCode` / `submitCode`. The other `getValueInRange` call sites in this file feed `parseCellExecutionOptions`, which normalizes on its own. Caught by CI: the win/electron-only failures in `quarto-inline-output-r.test.ts` ("R - Verify long text output is truncated with open in editor link") and `quarto-inline-output-dataframe.test.ts` (both "R - Verify DataFrame ..." tests), first seen at 2f4a58bc8a and failing on every Windows run since. Windows-only because `.gitattributes` is `* text=auto`, so the `.qmd` fixtures check out CRLF there and LF everywhere else. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Fix running a multi-statement R cell in a Quarto document with Windows line endings failing with a syntax error and producing no inline output ### Validation Steps @:quarto @:win The three e2e tests named above should go green on the Windows lane. Manual check on Windows: 1. Create a `.qmd` with CRLF line endings containing an R cell with two statements: ```r options(max.print = 5000) runif(5000) ``` 2. Run the cell with inline output enabled. 3. Before this change the cell errors with `Syntax error: unexpected invalid token` and `runif` never runs. After it, both statements run and the output renders with its truncation header. Unit coverage runs everywhere: ``` npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronQuarto/test/browser/quartoExecutionManager.vitest.ts ``` The new `strips carriage returns from fragments split out of a CRLF document` case fails without the fix and passes with it. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Windows CRLF cell text is split into statement fragments without line-ending normalization, so every non-final fragment ends in a bare CR that R rejects as an invalid token; the Ark bump (ark#1400 strip CR in strings::lines) stopped input_boundaries returning a single invalid range, which had been masking the bug by sending the whole cell as one request. - **Test:** [Quarto - Inline Output: R > R - Verify long text output is truncated with open in editor link](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Quarto%20-%20Inline%20Output%3A%20R%20%3E%20R%20-%20Verify%20long%20text%20output%20is%20truncated%20with%20open%20in%20editor%20link%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fquarto%2Fquarto-inline-output-r.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** expect(.quarto-inline-output .quarto-output-truncation-header).toHaveCount(1) received 0, win/electron only - **Signal:** Supervisor log: SEND execute_request code="options(max.print = 5000) " then RECV error Syntax error: unexpected invalid token; zero stream messages for the session; runif(5000) never requested; kernel exits cleanly code 0 at teardown. - **Frequency:** 5/68 runs (7.4%) on main, win/electron - **Hypothesis:** Normalizing the code read from the text model to LF makes the first fragment parse, both statements run, output exceeds maxLines (40) and the truncation header renders.

title: Quarto: serve a document's cells from its own session
description:
Fixes #15974

Before this PR, a Quarto document's code cells could be served by the wrong session. Statement range went to the notebook session, which had never synced those cells. That session then answered `Can't find document`, so <kbd>Cmd+Enter</kbd> ran only the first line of a multi-line statement. By contrast, completions went to the console session. That session had synced the cells, but it did not hold the variables the document defined. Not good! 😩 

The fix has three parts.

**Core.** The Quarto forwarder asks each provider registered on a hidden notebook cell and takes the first usable answer. Before, a provider that rejected ended the whole request, so the provider behind it, which did hold the document, was never asked. A rejection now means "no answer", and the loop moves on. Cancellation still ends the request. A provider that rejects on every keystroke is warned about once, not every time.

**positron-r and positron-python.** A Quarto session now names its own hidden notebook in its document selector and its provider registrations. Once its client is running, it claims those cells in a small ownership registry. The console client still syncs every Quarto document's cells. It declines the claimed ones at request time: completion, hover, signature help, definition, statement range, help topic, and diagnostics. Ownership returns to the console when the session's client stops. Real notebook (`.ipynb`) sessions are narrowed the same way, so they no longer answer for another notebook's cells.

An untitled Quarto document carries no file extension in its URI. It is classified by the language id of the open document, the way core's own `isQuartoDocument` does.

This is visible only when `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native` is on. That setting still defaults to `false`. I'm going to do that in a separate PR, after a little bit more cleanup. Speaking of which...

### Follow-ups

I think at least a couple of these are worth doing right away:

- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16151
- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16152
- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16154
- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16155
- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16156

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A still until we flip the switch on the setting

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:quarto @:console @:ark @:editor @:positron-notebooks @:help

Automated coverage:

- 50 Vitest tests for the core forwarder, including one rejection test for each forwarded feature
- 12 Vitest tests for the ownership registry
- 13 extension-host tests for the R providers
- 4 unit tests for the Python providers

The manual checks below cover hover, signature help, and diagnostics. No automated test right now reaches those paths.

**Before you start.** Set both of these in user settings:

```jsonc
"quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native": true,
"quarto.inlineOutput.enabled": true
```

Use something like `test/e2e/test-files/workspaces/quarto_inline_output/simple_r.rmd`, or anything where where you've got a chunk that defines a dataframe such as `df`.

1. **No session.** Open `simple_r.rmd` with no R console running at first. Type `mtc` in a chunk. Completions must appear after a console starts. <kbd>F1</kbd> on `mean` must open R help.
2. **Ownership transfers.** Run the first chunk, which starts the Quarto session for the document. On a new line, type `df$`. Completions must offer `x` and `y` or whatever is appropriate, which only the session knows. With the session still running, check the other hooks: hover on `df` must describe a data frame and typing `mean(` must raise the signature popup.
3. **Diagnostics follow the session.** With the session running, a squiggle about an undefined name from an earlier chunk must be gone. The Problems pane must show one set of diagnostics for the document, not two.
4. **Ownership returns.** Shut the Quarto session down. Type `mtc` again. Completions must still arrive, now from the console client again. The session's squiggles must be gone. The console's squiggles can come back on the next edit.
5. **Real notebooks still work.** Open one `.ipynb` with an R kernel and one with a Python kernel. In a cell, put the cursor on the first line of a multi-line statement and press <kbd>Cmd+Enter</kbd>. The whole statement must run. <kbd>F1</kbd> in a cell must open help.
6. **Untitled documents.** Run _Quarto: New Document_. Add an R chunk that defines a data frame and run it, which is what starts the session. On a new line, type `df$`. Column completions mean the session claimed its own cells. Repeat with a Python chunk.

Also, if you want, you can try out flipping the switch on the setting and running the whole E2E Quarto suite with the new value; this PR gets all of that passing locally for me! 🎉

title: ci: order bootstrap extension bumps by semver, detect pyrefly directly
description:
### Summary

The nightly bootstrap check resolved \"latest\" by **publish date** in two places. Meta published pyrefly `1.2.1` on 2026-09-17, two days after `1.3.1`, so both resolvers picked the backport:

| | version | published_at |
|---|---|---|
| Picked by the old sort | **1.2.1** | 2026-09-17 |
| Highest semver | 1.3.1 | 2026-09-15 |
| Pinned in product.json | 1.3.1 | - |

Two consequences:

1. [`update-extensions.sh`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/scripts/update-extensions.sh) opened #16158, downgrading the pin `1.3.1 -> 1.2.1`. Closed in favor of this PR.
2. [`check-bootstrap-extension-deps.ts`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/scripts/check-bootstrap-extension-deps.ts) has the same sort independently, so it has been auditing **1.2.1's** manifest for blocked dependencies instead of 1.3.1's. That one produced no visible symptom, so it would have gone unnoticed indefinitely.

Both now order by semver and use `published_at` only to break ties. Verified against all 14 bootstrap extensions' live p3m metadata: the selection changes **only** for pyrefly (to 1.3.1) and is identical everywhere else.

`update-extensions.sh` also now refuses to lower a pinned version unless `--allow-downgrade` is passed. The resolver is not the only way in: `--version` and interactive use bypass it entirely, and the existing check was a bare string inequality that treated a downgrade exactly like an upgrade.

### Why pyrefly was uniquely exposed

pyrefly is absent from the detection run. `settingsSkipPyrefly.json` blocks it from installing everywhere except a run with `ALLOW_PYREFLY=true`, because its language server is expensive. The mismatch detector could therefore never see it, and the workflow compensated by bumping it **unconditionally every night** - which is why pyrefly, alone among the 14, was exposed to the resolver daily.

This sets `ALLOW_PYREFLY` on the nightly check and drops that special case, so pyrefly is detected like every other bootstrap extension. The cost is small:

- The check never opens a Python file or a notebook, and pyrefly declares `activationEvents: [\"onLanguage:python\", \"onNotebook:jupyter-notebook\"]`. It installs without its language server ever starting - the expensive part does not happen here.
- The VSIX is already downloaded by this job today (`Downloading multi-platform extension: meta.pyrefly@1.3.1 for linux-x64` in [run 35553600882](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35553600882)); it was only blocked from *installing*. So there is no extra download.

### Two guards that come with making pyrefly required

- `OPTIONAL_MISSING_EXTENSIONS` is keyed off `ALLOW_PYREFLY` rather than deleted, so the safety net stays wherever pyrefly is still blocked.
- Phase 1 of `waitForExtensions` had **no deadline**. With pyrefly now required, an extension that never installs would spin until the Playwright timeout and report only that the test was slow. It is now bounded and fails with the list of what never arrived. The test is also marked `test.slow()`, since installing everything plus both grace periods does not reliably fit the default 2 minute budget.

### Deliberately not included

- **Which pyrefly version to ship.** If Meta intends 1.2.1 as a rollback, that is a deliberate pin, not something the nightly should infer from a publish date. Open VSX and p3m both show 1.3.1 as current, and a clean Positron install lands on 1.3.1, so tracking semver matches what a user gets.
- **`GitHub.vscode-pull-request-github` is pinned at 0.162.0 while p3m serves 0.166.1.** The nightly has never flagged it, which suggests it is not auto-updating in the test environment either - the same blind spot pyrefly had, minus the compensating bump. Worth a follow-up to have the registry check report \"pin is behind latest\" for all extensions.

### QA Notes

@:pyrefly

Verified locally:

- `./scripts/update-extensions.sh meta.pyrefly` -> `Latest version: 1.3.1`, `Already current`, no diff (was resolving 1.2.1 before)
- `--version 1.2.1` -> refused; `--version 1.2.1 --allow-downgrade` -> proceeds
- `node scripts/check-bootstrap-extension-deps.ts` -> clean across all 14, now resolving pyrefly 1.3.1
- `tsc --noEmit -p test/e2e/tsconfig.json` clean; `npm run precommit` clean

The `ALLOW_PYREFLY` half is the part local checks cannot cover - it needs a real run of the nightly job. Validated by dryrun; see CI validation below.

---

### Review follow-ups

Two rounds of automated review each found a real defect in the comparator; both are fixed in follow-up commits.

**`aacc4d49fa` - full SemVer precedence.** The first pass discarded prerelease identifiers and mishandled build metadata, so `2.0.0-beta.2` and `2.0.0-beta.10` compared equal and `1.2.3+linux` parsed as `[1,2,0]` (silently lower). The prerelease half was live rather than theoretical: p3m serves debugpy's `2024.11.0-dev` with `"pre_release": false`, so it survives the stable filter and reaches the comparator. Both implementations now follow SemVer 2.0 precedence, and the jq definition is a single shared `JQ_SEMVER_KEY` so the selector and the downgrade guard cannot drift apart.

**`34537c8d56` - candidates must have a release version string.** The stable filter still trusted p3m's `pre_release` flag alone, which the comments above it had already established is unreliable. Precedence only ranks `2024.11.0-dev` below `2024.11.0`, not below an older genuine release, so a mislabelled prerelease one minor ahead of stable would win selection. A candidate must now clear both the flag and its version string, falling back to all versions only when nothing suffix-free remains. Latent rather than live: debugpy's mislabelled builds are 2024.x against a 2026.6.0 stable.

### On test coverage

`scripts/` has no test collection today (Vitest covers `src/vs`, `test/e2e`, and `extensions`), and adding it would mean restructuring this script's entry point plus changing the shared Vitest config - a decision bigger than this bug fix. Deliberately left as is.

The comparator was instead verified by executing **both** implementations over a shared case table and asserting they agree:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| `1.2.1` vs `1.3.1` (the original backport regression) | lower |
| `2.0.0-beta.2` vs `2.0.0-beta.10` | lower |
| `2.0.0-beta` vs `2.0.0` | lower |
| `1.2.3+linux` vs `1.2.3` | equal |
| `1.2` vs `1.2.0` | equal |
| `1.0.0-alpha.1` vs `1.0.0-beta` | lower |
| `2024.11.0-dev` vs `2024.11.0` | lower |

Plus selector fixtures: stable `1.9.0` beats a mislabelled `2.0.0-dev`; a prerelease-only extension still falls back; the pyrefly `1.3.1`/`1.2.1` pair resolves to 1.3.1. TS and jq agreed on every row.

This is weaker than a committed test - it does not run in CI, so a future edit to either implementation could regress silently. Worth revisiting if `scripts/` ever gains test collection.



---

### CI validation

Validated with `workflow_dispatch` + `dryrun: true` (skips commit/push/PR/Slack) against this branch:

| run | head | result |
|---|---|---|
| [35622331830](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35622331830) | `96f2a585a2` | success |
| [35626750115](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35626750115) | `34537c8d56` (current head) | success |

The run at current head confirms:

- **`meta.pyrefly (1.3.1) found and matches`** - pyrefly installed and was version-compared, rather than skipped as optional. This is the line showing the special case is gone: it is now detected exactly like the other 13.
- `Nothing to bump.` / `No changes to product.json.` - no PR, no Slack. Before this change the same step bumped pyrefly unconditionally and, as of 2026-09-17, produced the downgrade in #16158.
- `check-bootstrap-extension-deps` succeeded with its `Open an issue for each hit` step **skipped**. That step is gated on `hits != '0'`, so the new comparator and the new stable filter resolved all 14 extensions cleanly.

All 14 extensions resolved on the first poll, 33s after launch - unchanged from the 32s measured before pyrefly was added. Installing it costs roughly a second, and neither grace period is reached.

**What this run does not cover:** `update-extensions.sh` never executes, because it only runs when the test reports drift and nothing is drifting today. The dryrun therefore exercises the detection path and the TypeScript resolver; the shell resolver is covered only by the local parity table above.

title: Fix plot origin-file button intermittently not appearing for R plots
description:
This bug was discovered while researching a test flake: `Plot File Attribution > R - Plot origin shows source file after run file command` fails 22% of the time on main, and the trace, kernel logs, and renderer logs traced it to the product race below rather than to the test. This PR fixes the plot origin-file button in the Plots pane intermittently never appearing for a plot. The button reads `metadata.origin`, which for R plots arrives asynchronously: the plots service registers and selects the plot, then fills in `origin` when the backend's `get_metadata` reply lands and fires `onDidUpdatePlotMetadata`. `PlotsContainer` listened for that event in an effect filtered on the selected plot id, but the filter captured `selectedInstanceId` in a stale closure. If the reply landed after React had committed the newly selected plot but before the effect had re-run for it, the event was compared against the previous selection and dropped, and nothing ever recomputed the origin memo. This is why the button was missing for the whole 30s wait while the sibling session-name chip rendered fine. The fix drops the container-local listener and drives the metadata-dependent memos from the `metadataVersion` counter that `usePositronPlotsState` already maintains from a listener subscribed once at mount, which cannot miss an update. A new RTL Vitest forces the reply into the commit-to-effects window with a layout effect and was RED before the fix, GREEN after. Why the run-file test and not the run-line test: when Ark opens the plot comm mid-execution (run line), the frontend's plot RPC queue waits for the kernel to go idle before sending `get_metadata`, so React has time to re-subscribe. With `source()` the comm opens after `execute_reply`, the RPC goes out immediately, and its reply races React's effects. Python plots resolve `origin` synchronously in the frontend, so they were never exposed. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Fixed the plot origin file button sometimes not appearing in the Plots pane for R plots created by sourcing a file. ### Validation Steps @:plots 1. Open an R file containing `plot(1:10)` and run "Source R File" repeatedly (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+S or the command palette). 2. Each time, the plot header should show the session name followed by the file name button; clicking it opens the file. 3. `npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronPlots/test/browser/plotOriginButton.vitest.tsx` passes; reverting the `plotsContainer.tsx` change makes the second test fail. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟡 Medium confidence -- Product race in PlotsContainer: the origin-button memo only recomputes on a locally filtered metadata event whose filter captures selectedInstanceId in a stale closure, so a get_metadata reply arriving between the new plot commit and the effect re-subscription is dropped and the origin button never renders. - **Test:** [Plot File Attribution > R - Plot origin shows source file after run file command](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Plot%20File%20Attribution%20%3E%20R%20-%20Plot%20origin%20shows%20source%20file%20after%20run%20file%20command%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fplots%2Fplot-file-attribution.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed -- Locator: locator(".plot-origin-file"), Timeout: 30000ms, element(s) not found - **Signal:** Trace: .plot-instance img visible at t=1967583, .plot-origin-file wait began 19ms later and burned 30s; plot-origin-file NEVER present in 170 DOM snapshots while the sibling .plot-session-name chip (button R 4.5.2) rendered. R Supervisor log: comm_open 18:44:26.803, get_metadata sent 26.833, GetMetadataReply 26.835 WITH origin.uri=file:///tmp/vscsmoke/test-files/plot-attribution-test.R (range null). renderer.log: no Failed-to-fetch-metadata warning; RenderQueue Runtime-ready gate waited 5ms (plot 2, kernel already idle) vs 11ms (plot 1, comm opened mid-execution). plotsContainer.tsx:96-104 filters onDidUpdatePlotMetadata by a closure-captured selectedInstanceId; originFileName memo deps are [currentPlotInstance, local metadataVersion] only. - **Frequency:** 15/67 runs (22.4%) on main, ubuntu/electron - **Hypothesis:** race

title: Open DuckDB and SQLite files to a data connection page
description:
Fixes #14051 Opening a `.duckdb` or `.sqlite` file from the Explorer landed on "The file is not displayed in the text editor because it is either binary or uses an unsupported text encoding." Those files now open to a page that names the format and offers to create a data connection to the file, or to open the connection you already have to it. ### Screenshots **Before**

**After** If the user does not have a connection for the database file, they see a page that will help them to create a data connection:

If the user does have a connection for the database file, they see a page that will help them to open the data connection:

### What the page does The page is a landing page, not a flow: opening a database file is not on its own a request to connect to it, so nothing is created and no connection is opened until the button is pressed. Its second line and its button answer to four states: | State | Second line | Button | |---|---|---| | Driver loading | Loading the data connection driver... | hidden, but laid out | | No connection yet | Create a data connection to browse and query it. | Create Data Connection | | Connection exists | You already have a data connection to it, named "". | Open Data Connection | | Driver unavailable | The data connection driver is not available. | hidden | **Create Data Connection** opens the existing Configure Data Connection dialog, prefilled: driver and mechanism resolved from the file extension, the database path seeded exactly as the dialog's own Browse picker would format it, and the connection named after the file. **Open Data Connection** is offered when a saved profile already points at this file, so a second connection to the same database isn't created by accident. Either way the Data Connections pane opens with that connection selected and expanded, which is what connects it. Extensions claimed: `.duckdb`, `.ddb` (DuckDB) and `.sqlite`, `.sqlite3`, `.db` (SQLite), for local and remote files only. `.db` is the debatable one: it is the conventional third SQLite extension and the SQLite driver offers it in its own file picker, but nothing guarantees a `.db` file is a SQLite database. One that isn't still gets this page, and the connection fails on connect, which is a clearer outcome than the binary-file page. Happy to drop it if reviewers disagree. The whole editor is gated on `dataConnections.enabled`, read once at startup like the pane itself, so with the feature off these files open exactly as they do today. ### Changes outside the new editor - **Data Connections view takes focus into its tree.** `PositronDataViewPane` had no `focusElement()`, so focusing the view left a focus rectangle around the whole panel and the arrow keys did nothing. Its `onFocused` event also fired from `focus()`, which is too early: `PositronViewPane` defers the real DOM focus by a tick, so anything focusing an inner element would have been undone. Moving the fire into `focusElement()` puts it on the right tick. This affects opening the view by any route, not just from this page. - **`IPositronDataConnectionsService.revealConnection`.** The pane's tree is built as the pane renders, which happens after `openView` resolves, so a plain event would be announced to a tree that doesn't exist yet. The request is recorded and the event is only a nudge; the tree runs the same `takePendingRevealConnection()` on construction and on every nudge, so whichever arrives first honors it, exactly once. - **`IDataConnectionsDriverManager.activateDrivers()`.** Driver extensions activate lazily on the pane's view event. This is the deliberate opt-in for a caller that needs a driver elsewhere; the page calls it so it can show the driver's logo and open its dialog. No package.json activation changes. - **`DataGridInstance.requestFocus()` / `onDidRequestFocus`.** Nothing could hand keyboard focus to a grid. The waffle, which carries the `tabIndex`, answers it. - **Data grid scroll fix.** `scrollToCell` and `scrollToRow` treated a zero-length axis as "everything is past the end" and scrolled the content out of the viewport that arrived a frame later. Nothing corrected it afterwards: the offset is in bounds while the extent is zero, and `setSize` re-clamps only when the size actually changes, so the grid came up scrolled past its content and looked empty. Each axis is now guarded separately, since a collapsed view pane has its full width and no height. ### Release Notes #### New Features - DuckDB and SQLite database files opened from the Explorer now show a page offering to create a data connection to the file, or to open an existing one, instead of the binary-file message (#14051) #### Bug Fixes - Fixed a data grid scroll defect where revealing a row in a view that had not been laid out yet could leave the grid scrolled past its own content and appear empty ### Validation Steps @:connections @:data-explorer With `dataConnections.enabled` turned on and the window reloaded: 1. Open a `.duckdb` file from the Explorer. The page shows the DuckDB logo on a light badge (check both light and dark themes), the file name, and **Create Data Connection**. 2. Press it. The Configure dialog opens prefilled with the file's path and a name taken from the file. Save. The Data Connections pane opens with the new connection selected, expanded, and holding keyboard focus, and the arrow keys move from that row. 3. Return to the file's tab. It now reads "You already have a data connection to it" and offers **Open Data Connection**. Press it and the same connection is selected and opened rather than a duplicate being created. 4. Repeat with a `.sqlite` file. 5. Switch to another view in the sidebar, come back, and press **Open Data Connection** again. The pane must show its rows, not blank space. 6. Reload the window with a database file tab open. The tab comes back. 7. Turn `dataConnections.enabled` off, reload, and open a database file: the binary-file editor appears as before. The data grid change is shared with the Data Explorer, which is why that suite is included above.

title: Use bundled ipykernel for reticulate sessions
description:
Python (reticulate) sessions can fail to start when the project's Python environment lacks `ipykernel`, even when the user's code doesn't depend on it. Users see an error about `positron_ipykernel`, as reported in [this comment](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/6675#issuecomment-5604984461).

This lets reticulate sessions use the `ipykernel` that Positron already ships. It follows the existing `python.useBundledIpykernel` setting and uses the bundle only when it supports the interpreter running inside R.

Ark reports that interpreter's Python version and architecture, and Positron supplies the matching package locations before starting the kernel. The interpreter information is refreshed after R restarts, and the bundle selection is saved for restored sessions.

Updates the Ark submodule to [bc7680f1](https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/commit/bc7680f10e5f50e0e25bf3002f4735e0c02cf94f), including the support merged in [posit-dev/ark#1404](https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1404).

title: Quarto: consolidate cell reconciliation for inline outputs and cell toolbars
description:
Fixes #15792

This PR consolidates Quarto cell-continuity matching (reconstructing which cell is which across a reparse, once cell IDs have changed) into one shared helper, `reconcileCellAssociations` (`common/quartoCellReconciliation.ts`), used by both the inline-output view zones (`quartoOutputManager.ts`) and the cell toolbars (`quartoCellToolbarController.ts`). This replaces two independent inline implementations and fixes a bug in the toolbar one, whose last-writer-wins hash map could remap a toolbar to the wrong cell or dispose it as a false orphan when two cells shared a content hash.

Also shares one cell-ID parser (`parseCellId()`, exported next to `generateCellId()`) in place of two ad hoc `split('-')` call sites, and fixes the `contentHash` doc comment (SHA-1 truncated to 16 chars, not SHA-256).

> [!NOTE]  
> The audit posted on #15792 corrected that issue's original premise: cell identity (IDs, content hashes) was **already centralized** in `quartoDocumentModel.ts`, so there was no cache-drift risk between the virtual notebook and the output cache to fix. Nothing in this PR consolidates anything between the new virtual notebook for Quarto and the `.ipynb` representation for inline output.

The real duplication that I found was just cell-continuity matching, which is what this PR consolidates. Not consolidated here, deliberately:

- The virtual notebook's prefix/suffix splice (text-model handle stability, a different cost model)
- The output cache's on-disk cross-session matching (a problem no in-memory consumer has)
- The two `.ipynb` representations themselves (in-memory vs. always-on persistence)

### How reconciliation works now (the part to review)

A stale cell ID resolving to *some* cell doesn't prove it resolves to the *same* cell, so the helper re-anchors associations in three passes:

1. **Align** the previous and current content-hash sequences with a whole-document LCS diff (`LcsDiff` from `vs/base/common/diff`). An unchanged cell keeps its association no matter what changed elsewhere, including edits or deletions of same-content siblings.
2. **Pair** whatever is left: an unmatched association claims any unclaimed current cell with the same content hash, in previous-position order. The diff reads a reorder as delete-plus-insert, and which of several identical cells it deems deleted is arbitrary, so prefer the outcome that keeps tracked state alive. Identical content makes any survivor an equally good home (the on-disk output cache is keyed by content hash for the same reason).
3. **Fallback** for associations with no previous-parse record at all: same hash matching, in id-index order.

An association is orphaned only when every same-content survivor is claimed by another association, i.e. a cell really did vanish. Within a run of byte-identical cells, which instance was added or removed is fundamentally unknowable; that residual ambiguity is accepted and documented in the function's doc comment.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Fix Quarto inline cell outputs and cell toolbars losing track of their cells (outputs disappearing or attaching to the wrong cell) when cells with identical content are edited, deleted, moved, or reordered (#15792)

### Validation Steps

@:quarto

Unit: `npx vitest --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronQuarto` (427 tests, including 17 reconciliation regression tests covering duplicate-content edits and deletions, adjacent and non-adjacent, reorders, swaps, mixed delete-plus-move parses, and multi-region edits in a single parse).

Manual:

1. Open a `.qmd` and create two cells with identical content.
2. Run the second cell so it shows inline output.
3. Edit or delete the *first* cell. The second cell's output should survive in place.
4. Move a cell with output to elsewhere in the document (cut/paste). The output and cell toolbar should follow it.
5. Insert a new cell above cells with output. Outputs should stay with their cells.

title: Fix integrated browser overlay for Positron modal popup and dialog
description: - Fixes #15547 - Closes #16072 I am opening a new PR here because CI cannot run properly on a pull request from a fork as outlined in #6628. This PR reapplies the commit by @mburtin from #16072 and extends it. ### Summary The browser view's overlay manager did not recognize Positron's modal dialogs and popups. Because of this, those elements could render behind an open browser tab, with no way to interact with them except pressing Esc. This PR registers three Positron overlay classes so the browser view pauses correctly when they are open: - `positron-modal-dialog-container` - `positron-dynamic-modal-dialog-box-container` - `positron-modal-popup-container` The popup entry tracks the popup's full-viewport container, not the small inner popup box, because the container is what determines whether the browser's native WebContentsView needs to pause. The popup's outside-click dismissal listens on the window, so a live WebContentsView under the popup would otherwise swallow those clicks. It also adds Mocha regression tests for all three classes, including a case where the small popup box does not overlap the browser but its full-viewport container does. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Fix Positron modal dialogs and popups rendering behind an open browser view (#15547) ### Validation Steps @:viewer @:modal @:new-folder-flow @:top-action-bar This change has unit test coverage in `overlayManager.test.ts` (11 cases), run with `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/test/electron-browser/overlayManager.test.ts`. This file has no existing E2E coverage, so the tags above run related suites as a regression check rather than adding new E2E tests. Manual steps (desktop app only as that integrated browser view is Electron only): 1. Open an HTML file, or a URL, in the internal browser so it renders in the editor area. Resize it to overlap the center of the window. 2. Static dialog: run *File > New Folder from Template...*. Confirm the wizard renders on top, and the browser shows its paused placeholder. 3. Dynamic dialog: open the Assistant pane, click the gear icon, then *Configure LLM Providers* (or use the Connections pane, the `+` button, then *New Connection*). Confirm the same behavior. 4. Popup: click the folder icon in the top action bar. Confirm the popup renders on top, the browser pauses, and a click inside the browser area dismisses the popup. 5. Resize the browser to the right half of the editor area, then reopen the folder popup from the top-left action bar so it does not geometrically overlap the small popup box. Confirm the browser still pauses. This checks that the fix tracks the popup's container, not just the box. 6. With nothing open, confirm the browser is not paused.

title: e2e: wait for a closed notebook's session to exit before the next test
description:
Mitigates https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16129 (test side only; the product issue stays open).

In the shared `afterEach` for the Positron notebook suites, closing a notebook shuts its kernel session down asynchronously, and the shutdown outlives the hook. When the next test creates an untitled notebook within about a second, it is given the same `Untitled-1.ipynb` URI, binds to the still-exiting session, and selecting a kernel never starts a fresh one. The kernel badge then sits on the exited icon until the 45s kernel start timeout. This hit `notebook-inline-data-explorer.test.ts` in the first positron-builds nightly.

The hook now reads the foreground session id before closing editors and, when it is a notebook session, polls the smoke-test metadata command until that session is gone or reports `exited`. This adds two `Sessions` helpers, `getForegroundSessionId()` and `expectSessionToBeGone()`. Both are no-ops on external servers (Workbench, Jupyter, Positron Server), where the smoke-test command is not registered. The wait is bounded at 15s and is about a second on the happy path. Remove it once #16129 is fixed.

The first CI run of this PR surfaced a second product bug: `notebook-edit-mode.test.ts` ends with the kernel paused at a breakpoint, and a paused kernel acknowledges the shutdown request but never exits (https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16133), so the new wait timed out. That test now stops the debugger before the hook closes the notebook, via a new `Debug.stop()` that runs `workbench.action.debug.stop` through the driver and waits for the paused thread to leave the Call Stack.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:positron-notebooks

All tests in the Positron notebook suites should pass on the first attempt. In the trace, each test's `afterEach` should show an "Expect session to be gone: python-notebook-..." step after "Close all editors".

title: fix: the unit lane failing on cache hits from an e2e-only import

The `test / unit` job fails on any branch whose npm caches hit, with `Failed to resolve import "archiver" from test/e2e/fixtures/test-setup/reporting.fixtures.ts`. Moving the trace-snapshot resolver into its own dependency-free module keeps the Vitest unit lane out of the e2e dependency graph.

title: e2e: let the Workbench dashboard fall back to New Session after Quit
description:
Fixes the first-attempt fixture-start failure of `workbench/posit-assistant/posit-assistant-foundry.test.ts` on the Workbench Azure lane, seen in the 2026-09-18 positron-builds nightly ([report](https://d38p2avprg8il3.cloudfront.net/playwright-report-35330437948-1-workbench-ubuntu-azure-ubuntu/index.html)).

`openSession()` in the dashboard page object assumed the project row survives quitting its session, and asserted on the row's "Create new session" button after `quitSession()`. That holds for user1, but for the Azure JIT user (`rstudio-ide-test`) a project with no session is not listed at all: after Quit the Projects table empties into the "No projects" state and the button never appears. Whenever the preceding managed-credentials file left a session behind (or its quit was still in progress), the foundry test's fixture failed at 0ms and only passed on retry, when the table was already empty and the create-new-project path was taken.

`openSession()` now waits for whichever settled state appears after Quit: it reuses the row's "Create new session" button when the row persists, and falls through to `createNewProject()` when the table is empty. The Azure early-return in `createNewProject()` is unchanged, so the fixture still handles the workspace copy for the JIT user.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:workbench @:workbench-azure

Both Workbench lanes should pass on the first attempt. In the Azure lane the foundry file runs after the managed-credentials file and should no longer fail at fixture start with "No projects" in the error context. The Ubuntu lane exercises the user1 path, where the row persists after Quit and the "Create new session" button is used as before.

title: Fix pending auto-update installing a stale build
description:
Fixes #8284

### Summary

When Positron finds a pending update and the user delays "Restart to Update," a second update published in the meantime was never picked up: the pending update just stayed pending until restart, at which point it installed the stale build and immediately found a newer one. This PR makes the pending-update path re-check the feed instead of assuming what it staged is still current:

- The overwrite check (`checkForOverwriteUpdates`) now runs on a recurring interval while `Ready`, on explicit "Check for Updates" (also allowed from the `Ready` state, not just `Idle`), and again right before `quitAndInstall` -- so a restart can't install a build the feed has already superseded.
- Comparisons against the feed disable Chromium's HTTP cache (`disableCache: true`), which was letting a stale feed response look authoritative.
- On a metered connection, the overwrite check is deferred (not silently dropped) and re-attempted once the connection is no longer metered.
- Win32's `supportsUpdateOverwrite` is re-enabled (disabled in #16083 as a stopgap, since the overwrite round used to strand a pending update by clearing it without a way back); a new `restorePendingUpdate()` puts the original pending update back whenever the overwrite round doesn't produce a newer one.
- Adds dev-only tooling to exercise the whole flow without waiting for two real builds to ship: a mock update feed server (`npm run mock-update-server`, or the **Mock Update Server** task), a `devUpdateTesting` mode that simulates the download/install states on an unsigned source build, and a **Developer: Stage Pending Update from Feed URL...** command to stage an arbitrary hosted build as pending. See `scripts/mock-update-server/README.md` for the full walkthrough.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- Fix Positron installing a stale update after a newer one was published while a "Restart to Update" was pending (#8284)

### Validation Steps

Signed builds of this branch, for testing the real download/install flow rather than `devUpdateTesting`'s simulation:
- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/35229762744
- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/35232431766

@:update

Unit coverage: `positronQuitAndInstall.vitest.ts` and `positronIsLatestVersion.vitest.ts` exercise the overwrite check, the metered-connection deferral, and `quitAndInstall`'s pre-restart re-check.

Manual, against the mock feed (no signed build needed):

1. Add to a gitignored `product.overrides.json` at the repo root:
   ```json
   { "quality": "dev", "updateUrl": "http://localhost:8902/positron" }
   ```
2. Run the **Mock Update Server** task (or `npm run mock-update-server`), then launch Positron with `./scripts/code.sh`. Within 30s the tooltip reads **Restart to Update**.
3. Publish a newer version while Positron is still running:
   ```bash
   curl localhost:8902/publish/2026.09.0-3/bbbbbbb
   ```
4. Either wait up to 30s or click **Restart to Update** -- it should re-check first, pass through **Downloading Newer Update**, and settle back on **Restart to Update** with the new version instead of installing the stale one.
5. Click **Restart to Update** again; the main log should record it would install the newer version.

On macOS/Windows with a signed build, **Developer: Stage Pending Update from Feed URL...** can stage an older hosted build as pending and then verify the real overwrite/download round completes against the actual channel feed.
