title: Add a Positron command agent skill for Posit Assistant
description:
Ships a `positron-commands` agent skill that teaches Posit Assistant which Positron IDE commands exist, what arguments they take, and when to reach for each one. It is one skill with a short router (`SKILL.md`) that points at a set of reference files, one per area, so the model loads only what it needs.

The skill lives in a new built-in extension, `positron-skills`. Rather than hand-copy each command's argument and return shapes into the docs, the extension bundles skill *templates* and fills in those mechanical facts from the running
build at activation. Each command's facts have one source of truth (its registration), so they cannot drift out of date. The prose around them -- when to use a command and where the raw metadata is misleading -- is still written by hand, because auto-generated descriptions like "Focus on Variables View" say nothing about *when* to use a command, and a required argument can have every property inside it optional. 

To support this, three additions to the Positron extension API:

- `getAgentSkillRoots()` returns the filesystem roots holding the skills that ship with the build.
- `registerAgentSkillRoot()` lets an extension add a root it produced at runtime, so the generated skill is discovered alongside the shipped ones.
- `getAgentAllowedCommands()` gains an `includeDisabled` option, so a command can be documented even when its precondition does not currently hold (for example, a Data Explorer command while no Data Explorer is open).

The extension only activates once `ai.enabled` is on, and it rewrites its output only when its inputs change, so an ordinary launch does no work.

Drift is guarded three ways: a directive naming an unknown command expands to an empty block and logs a warning; `agentSkillDrift.vitest.ts` fails when a command id named in a template no longer resolves in the workbench source; and `templateExpander.test.ts` covers the expansion itself.

Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15343

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Posit Assistant now knows the Positron IDE commands it can call, learning their arguments and intended use from a skill that ships with Positron (https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15343).

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:assistant

1. Build and launch Positron with `ai.enabled` on (the default).
2. Open the assistant and confirm it can name and correctly call Positron commands (for example, focusing a pane or opening a data frame in the Data Explorer), including for panes that are not currently open.
3. Confirm no skill files are written on a second launch when nothing has changed.

Unit coverage:

- `npm run test-extension -- -l positron-skills` (template expansion)
- `npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/api/common/positron/positronSkillRoots.vitest.ts`
- `npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/agentSkillDrift.vitest.ts`

title: Add a header with the Positron badge and a Help button to the welcome page
description:
Addresses #14934

Stacked on https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15564

This PR adds the header to the new welcome page: the Positron badge, the product name and tagline, and a Help button.

A primer on the logo assets, because the choice here is not obvious:

- `positron-header.svg` is the SVG the original welcome page shows. It contains the positron icon + product name + tagline
- `positron-icon.svg` is the positron icon on its own.

I started with the original SVG but found that it was hard to scale so it looked good next to the help button. I decided to recreate the parts that make the SVG. This is what the welcome page originally did. https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/8118 dropped the HTML text, but only because the SVG contained the same words (keeping both would have printed the name and tagline twice). Using the badge removes the duplication and the reason with it. The original welcome page is untouched and still shows the old SVG.

A few smaller points:

- The name comes from `IProductService`, so a dev build says "Welcome to Positron Dev" rather than claiming to be a release.
- The Help button runs `workbench.action.positron.openHelp`, the command the Help view registers for itself, so the welcome page does not have to depend on the `positronHelp` contribution.

Note: the tagline is now a localizable string rather than baked-in artwork, so it will translate where the SVG never could.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80eec8b2-96ec-4189-9d00-0ae3efeb9f84

<!-- Add each release note as a bullet point in the appropriate section below. -->
<!-- Use the format: - Description of the change (#issue-number) -->

- The welcome page shows the Positron badge and name, with a Help button that opens the Help pane. (#14934)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

title: server: support aws license manager
description:
Implements the licensing half of posit-dev/positron-builds#1135
PR that must land at same time to work https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/pull/1190

### Summary

For Positron Server on AWS SageMaker, there is no Posit-issued key to hand out: customers already hold an RStudio license in AWS License Manager, and our licensing client is the supported way to check a seat out of it. Positron makes no licensing decision of its own; it accepts the client's verdict. That path takes precedence over the key sources, so a leftover key in the environment cannot quietly win. 

This adds support for passing in a `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH` to derives a licensed state from what the AWS licensing client reports. **Question: is this the only/assumed entrypoint for the license manager? 👀 👀 **

- **Grace period.** Losing the lease starts a single 10-minute countdown before the server exits. Repeated failure messages (the client retries roughly every 10s) do not rearm it; rearming would keep an unlicensed server alive indefinitely.
- **Failure modes.** A missing binary fails immediately rather than burning the 60s startup timeout respawning it. A binary that exists but cannot execute (wrong arch, not executable) raises `error` and never raises `exit`, so both paths are treated as the client dying, followed by a delayed respawn.
- `remoteExtensionHostAgentServer.ts` hoists the existing `DisposableStore` earlier in `createServer` so the manager can be registered on it. That is what signals the client on shutdown, which is what checks the seat back in.


### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:web @:workbench

Positron-side licensing has no e2e coverage by design, the Platform team will own end-to-end SageMaker validation. The web tag here is a regression check on the *existing* signed-key path: web e2e runs `createServer` with a mandatory connection token and goes through `validateLicenseKey`, which is what the `DisposableStore` hoist and the new early-return branch touch.

**Unit tests**

```bash
npx vitest run src/vs/server/test/node/licenseManager.vitest.ts src/vs/server/test/node/remoteLicenseKey.vitest.ts
```

These cover the stdout frame parsing, the supervisor lifecycle (startup timeout, grace period, respawn, dispose), and the precedence/fail-fast behaviour of `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH`.

**Manual, against real AWS License Manager**

Needs AWS credentials with an accepted RStudio license grant. The client binary is **x86-64 only**. If you're running this on an arm mac in docker (like me 😅), things like R/Python will not start up due to the kernel supervisor mismatch. Since I'm only changing the licensing code, I think this is okay for now, since we can still check if the ui is starting. We can defer more usability testing elsewhere.

1. Check out this branch and build the x64 server:

   ```bash
   npm run gulp vscode-reh-web-linux-x64
   ```

2. Get the license manager tarball (verified against `1.2.6-89`).

3. Build an image around both. Full working example that I've been running locally on Docker, saved as `Dockerfile.aws`:

   ```dockerfile
   FROM ubuntu:22.04

   RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
       ca-certificates libsecret-1-0 libkrb5-3 python3 python-is-python3 curl \
       && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

   RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
   ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH"

   # The x64 server built in step 1.
   COPY --from=reh-server . /opt/positron-server
   WORKDIR /opt/positron-server

   # The license manager client. Keep the sha256 check.
   COPY --from=lm-client licensing-clients-aws-sagemaker-1.2.6-89.tar.gz /tmp/lm.tar.gz
   RUN echo "37edcffb36a81185cd265f5e2f318e2205c8fb002dcd8538f59b7bba012b41d6  /tmp/lm.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c - && \
      mkdir -p /usr/lib/positron-server/bin && \
      tar -xf /tmp/lm.tar.gz -C /usr/lib/positron-server/bin license-manager-aws-sagemaker && \
      chmod 0755 /usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-aws-sagemaker && \
      rm /tmp/lm.tar.gz

   ENV POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH=/usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-aws-sagemaker
   ENV LM_LOG_FILE=/tmp/sagemaker-lm.log
   ENV LM_LOG_LEVEL=debug

   CMD ["/opt/positron-server/node", "/opt/positron-server/out/server-main.js", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]
   ```

   ```bash
   docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -f Dockerfile.aws \
     --build-context reh-server=/path/to/vscode-reh-web-linux-x64 \
     --build-context lm-client=/path/to/tarball/dir \
     -t posit/positron-server-aws --load .
   ```

4. Run it (the client uses the standard AWS SDK credential chain and requires a region):

   ```bash
   docker run --platform linux/amd64 --rm -p 8000:8000 \
     -e AWS_REGION=us-east-1 \
     -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY -e AWS_SESSION_TOKEN \
     posit/positron-server-aws
   ```

**What to check**

- Server stdout shows the handoff and then the acquisition:

  ```
  Acquiring a Positron license through the license manager named by POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH.
  Positron license acquired from the license manager (days left: ..., users: ...).
  ```

- The workbench loads on `http://localhost:8000/?tkn=<token from stdout>`.
- `/tmp/sagemaker-lm.log` shows `Checked out license with consumption token '...'`.
- Point `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH` at a nonexistent path and confirm the server exits immediately rather than hanging for 60s.
- Use AWS credentials with no license granted/accepts, server does not start

title: Only show the academic license banner for academically-licensed deployments
description:
Resolves https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/issues/1141

The academic license banner was shown to every Positron Server web session, including
Server Pro deployments like SageMaker, because nothing distinguished an academic license
from a commercial one.

`validateLicense` tries each embedded public key in turn; the orchestrator key is used
exclusively by the JupyterHub/TLJH academic minting flow, so which key verified the
signature tells us whether the Education License Rider applies. This tracks the matching
key and surfaces it as `academic` on the validation result, then plumbs it to the browser
through a new `IPositronAcademicLicenseService`:

- **Server:** derived from the validated license at startup and carried on
  `IPositronLicenseeInfo`.
- **Browser:** `webClientServer.ts` injects a `_POSITRON_IS_ACADEMIC` global into the served
  HTML (reusing the existing marker slot, so no template change), which `platform.ts` reads.
- **Desktop / CLI:** always false -- these paths never run a license check.

The banner contribution and its show command now return early unless the session is
academic. The same flag is also sent to P3M as `positron-is-academic`, so gallery traffic
can be split by license type.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Positron Server Pro deployments no longer show the academic license banner.

### Validation Steps

@:extensions @:web

The web lane is tagged because this changes the HTML that `webClientServer.ts` serves --
a broken marker injection would surface as a web workbench that fails to load, which the
web smoke tests would catch.

Unit coverage:

```
npx vitest run \
  src/vs/server/test/node/remoteLicenseKey.vitest.ts \
  src/vs/platform/positronLicense/test/common/positronAcademicLicenseService.vitest.ts \
  src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/test/common/positronGalleryTelemetry.vitest.ts \
  src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronLicenseeInfo/test/browser/positronAcademicLicenseBanner.vitest.ts
```

`positronAcademicLicenseBanner.vitest.ts` is the regression test for this issue: it fails
without the license guard on the show command and passes with it.

Manual, needs a licensed server:

1. Start a Positron Server web session with a license validated against the primary key. No academic banner should appear, and`positron.showAcademicLicenseBanner` from the command palette should do nothing.
2. Start a session against an orchestrator-minted license (TLJH/JupyterHub). The banner should appear as before, and dismissing it should still persist across reloads.
3. Desktop: confirm no banner (unchanged -- desktop has no license check).
4. In the Extensions gallery log, confirm P3M requests carry `positron-is-academic=false` for the Server Pro session and `true` for the academic one.

title: Show known security vulnerabilities (CVE scoring) in the Packages pane
description: Fixes #13356 ### Summary Shows known security vulnerabilities (CVE scoring) for installed packages in the Packages pane, sourced from a Posit Package Manager (PPM) repository. **Where the pieces live:** the lookup itself is in the workbench (`packageVulnerabilityLookup.ts`): it probes the resolved repository's `/__api__/status` to confirm it is a PPM instance new enough to serve vulnerability data (2023.12+), queries `/__api__/filter/packages` with installed name+version pairs, and normalizes the OSV records -- aliased PYSEC/GHSA/CVE records are deduplicated into one advisory with the best CVSS v3/v4 score, a CVE-preferred display id, fixed-in versions, and an NVD/osv.dev link. The runtime extensions contribute only what they uniquely know: a `packageRepositoryUrl` hook resolves the index/repository the environment installs from (pip: `PIP_INDEX_URL` then `pip config get global.index-url`; uv: `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` / `UV_INDEX_URL` -- each manager reads only the variables it actually honours; R: the r-versions `Repo:` field, `repos.conf`, and settings, in kernel-launch precedence). The HTTP requests run on the extension host (the renderer's `fetch` is subject to CORS) and are pinned to the resolved host: redirects are followed manually, and an off-host redirect is refused before anything is re-sent. **Which PPM answers:** the advisories are the same OSV data wherever they are served from, so the environment's own index decides *which* PPM answers. An index or repo that probes as a PPM is used as-is (a managed environment gets advisories from the instance its admin configured). The public instance at `packagemanager.posit.co` answers when the environment names no internal host: nothing configured, an index we can't resolve (notably uv taking its index from `uv.toml` / `pyproject.toml` rather than the environment variables read here), or the language's own public default configured explicitly (pypi.org, cran.r-project.org, cloud.r-project.org) -- spelling out the default is the same statement as saying nothing. Any *other* configured index that is not a PPM gets no advisories at all: there is no silent fallback, so an environment installing from an internal repository never has its package inventory sent to a host its administrator didn't choose. A second setting, `packages.vulnerabilities.source`, turns off even the public fallback (`'environment'`) for managed or network-restricted deployments. Privacy: the lookup sends only the installed package inventory (names and versions) to that one instance, and the whole feature is off when `packages.vulnerabilities.enabled` is off. The setting descriptions spell out both destinations. **API:** `getPackageMetadata` is unchanged -- it still takes package names; advisories are version-specific, so the workbench lookup builds its own name + installed-version pairs. Package managers gain the optional `packageRepositoryUrl(token)` hook described above. The workbench-side package model gains a `vulnerabilities` field with three states: `undefined` = no data available, `[]` = repository knows the version and reports no advisories, non-empty = advisories. It is populated by Positron's own lookup, never by the runtime. **UI:** vulnerable packages get a severity-banded shield badge (NVD bands, max CVSS score) in the list, and a new Vulnerable filter (`@vulnerable` token) narrows the list. In the package detail, the advisories live behind a **Security tab** alongside Overview: a real `tablist` (arrow keys wrap, Home/End jump to the ends, selection follows focus, panel is focusable), with an advisory count badge on the tab coloured by the worst advisory so moving the advisories behind a tab doesn't hide the one thing worth noticing at a glance. The tab lists each advisory with severity band + score, linked id, summary, fixed-in, and published date. The tab is offered only when the lookup reported advisory data; `undefined` is neither a warning nor an earned all-clear. **Colour and contrast:** the severity ramp is now a shared palette (`packageVulnerabilities.css`) used by both the list badge and the Security tab, built on `list.errorForeground` / `list.warningForeground` with `editorError.foreground` / `editorWarning.foreground` fallbacks, replacing `charts.red` / `charts.orange`. The charts ramp is tuned for fills in a plot, not small text on a pane: `charts.orange` resolves to the find-match highlight, a 33%-alpha wash that lands at 1.5:1 as a text colour and is undefined outright in the high-contrast themes. The tab count badge tints its background with `color-mix` at 14% so 10px text clears 4.5:1 in all four default themes, and the selected tab's underline is a pseudo-element rather than a border because the high-contrast themes set a border on every `.positron-button` at higher specificity. Everything is gated by a new `packages.vulnerabilities.enabled` setting (default on, reacts without a reload). The package metadata cache schema is bumped to v3 to persist advisories, which instance served them, and when each package's lookup last answered -- so a transient advisory failure is retried on the next refresh instead of counting as fresh until the entry ages out. ### Tests - **Vitest (workbench):** the lookup end to end -- which instance may be queried (configured PPM, non-PPM and authenticated repositories, public defaults treated as unconfigured, the `source` setting, credential-free logging), `/__api__/status` discovery (path walking, path-prefixed PPM, pre-2023.12 rejection, per-URL caching, shared-probe cancellation that doesn't fail other waiters, failed-probe aging), `filter/packages` fetching (version-pinned specs, vulnerable/clean/unknown, PEP 503 name matching, per-binary-build row dedup, chunking, partial results on failure or a spent budget, cancellation), and `normalizeOsvVulnerabilities` (alias merging, unscored RSEC records, CVSS v4 over v3, sort order, groups bridged by a later record, fixed versions across release branches). Plus severity banding, `@vulnerable` query parsing, Security tab rendering (scored and unscored advisories, the "no known vulnerabilities" case, no tab when there's no data, arrow-key tab navigation), and the disk-cache merge of advisories into package metadata including per-source freshness. - **positron-python / positron-r unit:** `resolvePythonIndexUrl` (per-manager env var lists, pip-config lookup) and `resolveRRepositoryUrl` (r-versions `Repo:` field, `repos.conf`, settings precedence); the locators and `uiKind` are injected so tests aren't hostage to the machine's real configuration. ### Screenshots Shows a shield when there is a known vulnerability with this version (no score for R package) R Package details with CVE listing Python package _Note: the detail-view screenshots predate the tab layout -- the advisories they show inline now live behind the Security tab._ ### Release Notes #### New Features - The Packages pane shows known security vulnerabilities (CVE scoring) for installed packages, from the environment's own Posit Package Manager repository when it has one and from Posit's public instance otherwise (#13356) #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:packages-pane No repository configuration is required: with a default pypi.org / CRAN setup, advisories come from Posit's public Package Manager (the same holds when the default is spelled out explicitly, e.g. `PIP_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.org/simple`). To exercise the configured-PPM path instead, point the environment at a PPM instance (2023.12+); Posit Public Package Manager works. **Python** 1. Install a version with known advisories, e.g. `pip install urllib3==1.26.4`. 2. Open the Packages pane: the package shows a shield badge with the highest CVSS score, colour-banded by severity; hover for the advisory tooltip. 3. Open the package's detail: a Security tab appears next to Overview with a count badge coloured by the worst advisory. Select it: each advisory lists severity band + score, a CVE id linking to its NVD/osv.dev page, summary, fixed-in version, and published date. A package the repository knows with no advisories shows "No known vulnerabilities..."; a package/version unknown to the repository offers no Security tab at all. 4. Navigate the tabs with the keyboard: Tab into the strip, then Left/Right arrows (wrapping) and Home/End move between Overview and Security. 5. Use the filter menu's Vulnerable entry (or type `@vulnerable` in the filter box) to narrow to vulnerable packages. 6. Toggle `packages.vulnerabilities.enabled` off: badges, the Security tab, and Vulnerable filter matches disappear without a reload (with the Security tab open, the view falls back to Overview). 7. Configured-PPM path: `pip config set global.index-url https://packages.posit.co/pypi/latest/simple` (or set `PIP_INDEX_URL`), relaunch, and confirm advisories still appear -- now served by that instance rather than the public one. 8. Themes: switch between Dark+, Light+, and a high-contrast theme and confirm the badge, the tab count badge, and the Security tab severity text all stay legible. **R** 1. Install an older release of a package with a published RSEC advisory and refresh the pane. CRAN advisories are typically unscored: expect a badge without a number and "Severity unknown" in the detail. 2. Configured-PPM path: point R's repos at a PPM CRAN repo (e.g. `options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://packages.posit.co/cran/latest"))`, or a `repos.conf`) and confirm advisories still appear. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add Canvas mode: standalone presentation, launch, and restoration
description:
Progress towards #15309.

This PR was previously the top of a stack (#15311 standalone mode, #15438 Canvas mode; earlier iterations #15315/#15317). Per reviewer request the stack has been collapsed into this single PR targeting `main`. The three layers, bottom to top:

### 1. Standalone mode (main process)

A main-process coordinator for presenting one window as the application surface:

- Atomic application-wide acquisition with a declared exit command.
- Safe routing for second-instance, Finder, and Dock file opens.
- Correct focus behavior for argumentless relaunches.
- Minimal native menus while engaged.
- An `engaged elsewhere` startup stamp for other windows.

### 2. Canvas mode (presentation)

- Moves a ready Canvas editor into a locked, chromeless auxiliary window.
- Hides the IDE only after the Canvas window is usable.
- Merges the live Canvas editor back into the IDE on exit.
- Handles concurrent entry, failures, and entry/exit races.
- Restricts the default IDE escape shortcuts while Canvas is active.
- Defines and tests the Positron/Assistant command seam.

Posit Assistant owns Canvas discovery and readiness. Without a Canvas-capable Assistant, Positron exposes no Open Canvas palette command.

### 3. Canvas launch and restoration

- Adds `--canvas` for fresh and forwarded launches.
- Covers startup with an inert curtain until Canvas is ready or recovery is chosen.
- Waits for the workspace trust decision behind the curtain before entering Canvas.
- Adds a hidden, experimental `canvas.openOnStartup` setting for `settings.json`.
- Remembers per-workspace Canvas intent across relaunches.
- Merges a restored Canvas window back into the IDE when Canvas mode is not selected.

### Reviewer Q&A

#### Standalone mode

**Why is this a main-process service?**
Only the main process can coordinate multiple renderers, native menus, and external application opens.

**Does standalone mode replace or destroy the main renderer?**
No. Presentation belongs to the consumer. The coordinator only records ownership and routes application-level behavior.

**What if the holder does not exit?**
External opens wait up to 10 seconds, then proceed so a hung renderer cannot swallow the request.

**Why is engagement not persisted?**
It represents a live renderer. Consumers may persist intent and reacquire after restoration.

**Why are protocol URLs excluded?**
They include non-window flows such as authentication callbacks. The forced-exit policy applies to file and folder opens.

**Does the menu restriction affect other windows?**
Yes. Electron's native menu is application-wide, matching the application-wide definition of standalone mode.

#### Canvas mode

**Why does this live in Positron?**
Positron owns native windows, editor groups, focus, and presentation. Assistant owns Canvas content, identity, and readiness.

**How are commands restricted?**
This is a narrow UX deny list for default shortcuts that reveal IDE surfaces, not a command sandbox. Other commands and custom user keybindings remain available.

**What happens to the main IDE renderer?**
It remains alive and is only hidden. Exit reveals it before moving or focusing editors.

**How is the live conversation preserved?**
Entry moves the existing webview editor. Exit merges its group back into the IDE instead of closing or recreating it.

**How stable is the cross-repo interface?**
The seam is limited to Canvas identity, ensure-ready, enter, exit, and active-state commands. Assistant can change Canvas internals while preserving those behaviors.

#### Launch and restoration

**What decides whether a window starts in Canvas?**
After AI-disabled and engaged-elsewhere vetoes, `--canvas` wins, then an explicitly configured setting, then stored workspace intent. Explicit `false` overrides stored intent.

**What happens without a Canvas-capable Assistant?**
The readiness handshake fails before standalone mode engages. The curtain offers Retry, Open Positron, and Quit; a stale restored panel is not trusted.

**Why not check the Assistant version?**
The behavioral handshake avoids coupling Positron to Assistant release numbers and remains safe if Canvas is renamed or removed.

**Does the startup setting affect ordinary users?**
No. It is hidden from the Settings UI, tagged experimental, and only takes effect when manually added to `settings.json`.

**What happens after an Assistant downgrade?**
Stored intent can be cleared by choosing Open Positron. An explicit `canvas.openOnStartup: true` continues to request Canvas until the user disables it, with the same recoverable curtain on failure.

**Why is a startup curtain necessary?**
Assistant and editor restoration require the workbench to initialize. The curtain prevents an IDE flash and makes the covered workbench inert while entry is pending.

**Why does boot wait for the workspace trust decision?**
The trust startup prompt renders in the main window, which Canvas mode hides, and an undecided workspace holds back trust-gated extensions -- including the authentication providers behind the Canvas model picker, leaving Canvas with an empty model list. The gate (`positronCanvasTrustGate.ts`) mirrors the startup prompt's own gating and joins its coalesced request, so it never prompts when the user's `security.workspace.trust.startupPrompt` preference or an earlier answer suppressed it; Canvas then enters untrusted and the Assistant's restricted-mode surface explains. The curtain's z-index sits below workbench dialogs so the native prompt stays visible over it. Trust deliberately stays native workbench UI rather than crossing the command seam.

**How are restored Canvas windows distinguished from user pop-outs?**
Only locked compact windows containing exclusively Canvas editors are merged back. Manually popped-out panels are left alone.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

- `npm run build-check`
- Canvas, standalone-mode, launch, and auxiliary-window Vitest suites: 72 tests passed
- No TypeScript errors in touched files

title: Allow dataConnections.enabled to be set per workspace
description:
`dataConnections.enabled` was registered with `ConfigurationScope.APPLICATION`. Workspace settings files are parsed with `WORKSPACE_SCOPES`, which does not include `APPLICATION`, so the setting was silently ignored in a workspace `.vscode/settings.json`. The Settings editor also refused to write it on the Workspace tab. This PR changes the scope to `WINDOW`. A repository can now enable the Data Connections panel for anyone who opens it, which is useful for demo and workshop repos, such as the ones we are prepping for posit::conf! 🎉 

The setting is also `restricted` now, so Positron reads it only from a trusted workspace. The panel connects to databases and generates connection code, so an untrusted clone should not be able to turn it on. `restricted` applies only to workspace and folder settings. User settings are not affected, and neither is the e2e harness, which writes the flag into user settings.

Two notes for reviewers:

- Anyone who enabled the flag while running a non-default profile must set it again. With `APPLICATION` scope, Positron read the value only from the default profile settings file. With `WINDOW` scope, it reads the value from the current profile settings file. I think this is fine during our preview time period here.
- In a multi-root workspace, the value must go in the `settings` block of the `.code-workspace` file. Folder-level `.vscode/settings.json` is parsed with `FOLDER_SCOPES`, which does not include `WINDOW`. Again, I think this is a fine change to make during our preview period.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A (the Data Connections panel is still behind a preview flag)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections

The connections suite exercises the flag end to end. It writes `dataConnections.enabled` into user settings, then drives the panel. This confirms the panel still appears after the scope change.

Then check the new workspace behavior by hand:

1. Make a folder that contains `.vscode/settings.json` with `{ "dataConnections.enabled": true }`.
2. Open the folder in Positron and trust it. Run _Developer: Reload Window_.
3. Confirm the Data Connections panel appears in the sidebar.
4. Run _Workspaces: Manage Workspace Trust_, remove trust for the folder, and reload. Confirm the panel does not appear.
5. Remove the workspace setting. Set `dataConnections.enabled` to `true` in user settings, reload, and confirm the panel appears again.

title: Unpin bqplot now that bqplot@0.6.1 is published on npm
description:
Removes the `bqplot==0.12.47` pin from `test/e2e/test-files/requirements.txt`.

The pin went in because `bqplot` Python 0.13.0/0.13.1 set `__frontend_version__`
to `^0.6.1` while the `bqplot` JS package on npm was still at 0.6.0, so the CDN
404'd on `bqplot@^0.6.1/dist/index.js` and the widget failed to render with
`Error: Script error for "bqplot"`.

That skew is resolved. Both upstream conditions from #13482 now pass:

- npm `dist-tags.latest` is `0.6.1`, published 2026-07-15.
- Latest PyPI `bqplot` (0.13.1) declares `__frontend_version__ = '^0.6.1'`, and
  `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bqplot@^0.6.1/dist/index.js` returns
  `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `x-jsd-version: 0.6.1`.

Closes #13482

`test/e2e/tests/plots/plots.test.ts` should render `.svg-figure` without the
broken-image / "Click to show javascript error" placeholder.

**Windows is the lane that exercises this change.** It installs from
`test/e2e/test-files/requirements.txt`, so it resolves `bqplot` fresh from PyPI
and will pick up 0.13.1. macOS resolves the same way but is covered by the

from PyPI, and those are the ones validated here. A green chromium run just
confirms nothing regressed on the older version.

title: Add command to retrieve packages metadata
description:
Part of #15575.

### Summary

Adds `positronPackages.getPackages`, an agent-compatible command that reports the packages installed in the foreground interpreter session: each package's name, installed version, newest available version and outdated state, plus which session the answer describes and a `metadataStatus` field saying how the outdated state was obtained (fresh, cached, unsupported, timed-out, or fetch-failed).

The command never throws. When there is nothing to report it returns `available: false` with a reason the caller can act on: `disabled` (Packages pane turned off), `no-session`, `session-not-ready`, `unsupported` (the runtime has no package manager), or `failed` (with the error message).

Implementation notes:

- Backed by a new `getPackagesSnapshot()` on `PositronPackagesInstance`. Unlike a pane refresh, it reads the installed list live on every call (so it works before the Packages pane has ever been opened, and sees packages installed from the console) and awaits the outdated/latestVersion fetch. Both stages are bounded (5s list / 10s metadata), and a metadata fetch already in flight (e.g. a user's refresh) is joined rather than cancelled.
- A "Show Packages as JSON" Command Palette entry opens the same payload the agent reads in an untitled editor, so it can be inspected in a release build.
- Registered via `CommandsRegistry` with no precondition, matching the other payload commands: Assistant discovers it once, and learns the feature is off from the payload (`reason: 'disabled'`) rather than by the command vanishing mid-session.
- Not gated on `ai.enabled`: it reports the user's own environment and doesn't call a model, matching the other agent-compatible package commands.
- The issue also asks for vulnerability data. Nothing in the runtime protocol carries CVE data today, so no field was added yet; a separate PR will add it once that feature has merged, which is why this PR does not close the issue.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Added a command AI agents can use to read the packages installed in the current session, including versions and whether newer versions are available (#15575)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:packages-pane

The new behavior is covered by vitest tests (the command's payload and every unavailable reason, the palette action, and the snapshot's timeout/join/cancellation paths). To verify manually:

1. Start a Python or R session (the Packages pane does not need to be opened).
2. Run "Show Packages as JSON" from the Command Palette. Verify the JSON lists the installed packages with `version` and, for supported runtimes, `latestVersion`/`outdated`, plus a `metadataStatus` of `fresh` or `cached`.
3. Install a package from the console (e.g. `pip install cowsay`), rerun the command, and verify the new package appears.
4. Set `packages.enabled` to `false`, rerun, and verify the payload is `{ "available": false, "reason": "disabled" }`.

title: Rename the RHEL e2e lane to Rocky
description:
### Summary

The e2e container for this lane has always been Rocky (`positron-rocky8`). We
called it "rhel" back when Rocky looked temporary, and since we've decided to
stay on Rocky the naming is now just inconsistent. This aligns it.

Renamed:

- **Workflow**: `test-e2e-rhel.yml` -> `test-e2e-rocky.yml` (tracked rename), title `Test: E2E (Rocky)`, job id and default display name `e2e-rocky`, `PW_JSON_FILE: test-results/rocky.json`, artifacts `*-rocky-json-results` / `*-rocky-logs`.
- **Call sites**: `test-pull-request.yml` jobs `e2e-rocky-electron` / `e2e-rocky-chromium`, outputs `rocky_electron_tag_found` / `rocky_web_tag_found`, display names `electron (Rocky)` / `chromium (Rocky)` (matching the existing `(Debian)` casing). `test-full-suite.yml` dispatch input `run_e2e_browser_rocky`, job `e2e-chromium-rocky`, and the `slack-notify` needs list.
- **PR tags**: the `rhel-electron` and `rhel-web` tags become `rocky-electron` and `rocky-web`, in `test-tags.ts`, `pr-tags-parse.sh`, and the `positron-pr-helper` tag classifier.
- **Identifiers**: `distro: rocky` and the `distro` input docs in `setup-build-env` / `save-build-caches` / `restore-build-caches`; `OS_SUFFIX="rocky"` in `gen-report-dir`.

No back-compat aliases for the old tags: no open PR used either spelling, and an
old tag now surfaces as an "unrecognized tag" warning on the PR rather than
silently selecting nothing.

Deliberately left alone -- names that come from outside Positron and genuinely
are RHEL: the `/etc/os-release` ID match lists (`rhel|rocky|centos|fedora|almalinux`
in `gen-report-dir`, and the same list in `sandboxHelper.ts`), the Workbench /
PPM / R vocabulary (`rstudio-workbench-rhel-`, feed keys `rhel8`/`rhel9`,
`__linux__/rhel9`, `cdn.posit.co/r/rhel-9`), and prose about the RHEL family.

### Two operational notes

- The `distro` change rotates the npm and builtins cache keys for this lane, so its first run is a cold build.
- The report URL suffix becomes `-rocky`. Historic report URLs are unaffected.
- If any ruleset lists `electron (RHEL)` / `chromium (RHEL)` as a required check, it needs the new name. These are opt-in tag lanes, so probably not, but worth a glance.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:rocky-web

CI is the validation here: this PR body's tag exercises the renamed chromium
lane end to end -- tag parsing, the renamed workflow, the new cache key, and the
report/artifact names. Confirm the job shows up as `chromium (Rocky)` and its
report URL ends in `-rocky`.

Locally verified: all four changed YAML files parse, `scripts/test/pr-tags-lib-test.sh`
passes, `npm run precommit` is clean, and tag validation against the enum accepts
the two new tags while flagging the old `rhel` spelling as unrecognized.

title: Add session, mode, and attribution metadata to execution events
description: Fixes posit-dev/positron-builds#1182 Fixes posit-dev/positron-builds#1183 Extends work done in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/7108 ### Summary Posit Workbench audits console input by subscribing to `positron.runtime.onDidExecuteCode`. It is extending that audit log to record where each line of code came from, and needed three things the public event and API didn't yet expose. This PR adds them: - **`sessionId` and `mode` on `CodeExecutionEvent`.** Both already existed on Positron's internal event and were simply dropped when it was rebuilt for the public API. `sessionId` lets the audit trail say which runtime ran a given line when several consoles are open; `mode` lets a subscriber tell an interactive line apart from the silent setup and teardown scaffolding that assistants run around it. - **A new optional `attributionMetadata` argument on `executeCode`.** Its fields are merged into `attribution.metadata` on the resulting event, so a caller can record who really drove an execution. This is what lets Posit Assistant record that a line came from an external agent (for example Claude Code) rather than just "the Assistant extension." Positron keeps sole control of `attribution.source`, so a caller can never forge a human-typed record by claiming `interactive`, and Positron's own fields (`extensionId`, and `codeLocation` for scripts) are written last so a caller cannot overwrite them. The change also picks up executions from Quarto documents, which weren't being forwarded to the event before, and fixes a case where a console session that echoes its own input during execution would show the input twice. ### Interactive Testing To make interactive testing easier, I've added a `listen` command to the Zed runtime that will start dumping execution events to the Zed console. Run `listen` in Zed, then switch to another console and run some commands. ### Release Notes #### New Features - Extensions can now attribute the origin of code they run through the Positron API ### Validation Steps @:console @:quarto @:notebooks The core behavior is covered by unit and API tests: - `npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/positron/mainThreadLanguageRuntime.vitest.ts` -- event forwarding from the console, notebook, and Quarto sources - `npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/services/positronConsole/test/browser/submitCode.vitest.ts` -- the duplicate-echo fix - `npm run test-extension -- -l vscode-api-tests --grep 'executeCode fires events'` -- the merged `attribution.metadata` and preserved `source` To check by hand: run code in a console, a notebook, and a Quarto document, and confirm each fires `onDidExecuteCode` once with the right `sessionId`, `mode`, and `attribution`. The positron-zed runtime has a listener wired up to make this easy to observe.

title: Add a merge guard for inno_updater.exe branding
description:
Fixes #15330

This PR adds a merge guard so the vendored Windows update helper cannot lose its Positron branding again. `build/win32/inno_updater.exe` is a prebuilt binary, and upstream merges have silently replaced it with the unbranded VS Code build twice before (#7769, #13572). When that happens, users see "Visual Studio Code" in update failure dialogs, and the update log is written as `vscode-inno-updater-*.log`, so users cannot find the log we ask them for.

The changes:

- A new test, `src/inno-updater-branding.vitest.ts`, scans the binary for the branded strings: the log filename, the failure dialog text, and the UTF-16 strings in the version resource. It runs in the unit test job on every PR, so an upstream merge that reverts the binary now fails CI instead of shipping.
- The vendored `build/win32/Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` move to 0.22.0 to match the rebuilt binary I am making.
- Pending: the rebuilt, rebranded `inno_updater.exe` from posit-dev/positron-inno-updater#3. That PR merges upstream microsoft/inno-updater 0.22.0 and adds a CI workflow that builds the exe and checks its branding. The binary lands here after that PR is reviewed and merged.

This PR will stay a draft until the binary lands. The guard test fails against the current unbranded exe by design, so the unit test job on this PR is red until the new binary is vendored.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Restore Positron branding in the Windows update helper: update dialogs say Positron again, and the update log is written as `positron-inno-updater-*.log` (#15330)

### Validation Steps

No e2e suite covers the Windows installer update flow, and dev builds do not run the vendored exe. Validation is:

1. `npx vitest run src/inno-updater-branding.vitest.ts` passes after the new binary is vendored. The test was verified in both directions: it fails against the unbranded exe at HEAD and passes against the last branded exe from git history (`a3c249d6314`).
2. On a Windows release build: make sure that `%TEMP%` contains `positron-inno-updater-<timestamp>.log`.

title: Add the environment health data layer for the welcome page
description:
Addresses #14934

The data layer for the welcome page environment setup card. No UI: this is the contract, the service that runs the checks, and the setting that says which languages get checked. The card that renders it is stacked on top of this branch in #15564.

### What it does

The Python and R extensions each expose a command that reports if the language is setup correctly: `python.getEnvironmentHealth` and `r.getEnvironmentHealth`. Each returns a list of checks, where a check has a status (passed, needs attention, failed, not checked), a sentence describing it (`summary`), and a button that runs a command to fix the step if it didn't pass.

`EnvironmentHealthService` runs both commands and holds the results. `environmentHealth.ts` is core's copy of the shape those commands return. The payload arrives as plain JSON from the extension host and core cannot import the extensions' types so they are re-declared.

### Service Registration

This new service is registered per window. Two welcome pages in a split editor share one set of results, and so does a pop window of the welcome page. Two Positron windows would each have their own `EnvironmentHealthService`, which is what we want: the checks resolve the interpreter for the open workspace, so two windows with different folders open are asking different questions.

Opening the old welcome page does currently create `EnvironmentHealthService`. The same editor pane is used by both the old and new welcome pages, and it asks for the service in its constructor. That alone is enough to cause the service to be instantiated. However, we do prevent the environment health check commands from running in this scenario. The `_started` flag prevents them from running until `recheckForPage` runs, which is what the new welcome page calls. An empty service costs one listener and a couple of empty sets, and the old page goes away once the new one lands, so this is fine.

### Other things worth knowing

A running environment health check cannot be cancelled, because `executeCommand` takes no cancellation token. Kicking off  the environment health check manually (via a button) from the welcome page drops the request if a check is already running. 

We queue up an environment health check to run after a "fix" command is complete. We discard the result of a check that was still running when the "fix" finished, since it was computed before the fix and may report the wrong result for that step.

There is a "busy" state (`isBusy(language)`) in the service that reports whether a check or a fix is running for a specific language. This state will be used by the UI to show a busy indicator when a command is running and to "disable" buttons.

### Setting

`welcomePage.environmentChecks` lists the languages that get checked, defaulting to both. Removing one stops its check running.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:welcome

There is nothing to see until the card lands, so this is best reviewed as code, or alongside #15564.

Most worth a careful read is the run lifecycle: a language hidden mid-check, a fix ending after its language was turned off, a fix's recheck landing during another check, and disposal with a check still out. Also whether the shape guard matches what the two extensions actually send.

To watch it work, turn on `welcomePage.experimental`, run `Developer: Set Log Level...` -> Window -> Trace, and filter the Window output channel for `[environment health check]`.

title: Fall back to the registration id when a provider declares no catalogId
description:
Fixes #15416

Companion https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2085

`isSourceEnabled()` treated a missing `catalogId` as "enabled", a default left over from the dev-only echo/error providers deleted in #11089. That meant any extension registering a provider without opting in escaped catalog enforcement entirely, which is how Posit Assistant's Ollama and LM Studio buttons survived being disabled in the provider catalog. The registration id is now the fallback, so registrations get enforcement by default. Ids the catalog has no entry for stay enabled. That's deliberate: when the catalog can't load at all (see #15333, where the ai-lib packages were missing from the remote server), an empty snapshot would otherwise disable every provider instead of just the ones an admin turned off.

While in here: `$getRegisteredProviders()` returns catalog-filtered sources but wasn't waiting for the catalog to load, so an extension calling `positron.ai.getRegisteredProviders()` during activation saw the empty pre-initialization snapshot. Providers declaring a `catalogId` got dropped, and ones that don't stayed enabled even when the catalog disables that id, which is the exact case this PR set out to fix. It now awaits `whenInitialized`, matching `$getEnabledProviders()` and `$isProviderEnabled()`.

Posit Assistant is declaring `catalogId` on its side too (https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2085).

### Release Notes

#### Bug Fixes

- Don't display disabled local providers in provider modal (#15416)

### Validation Steps

@:assistant

Unit tests:

```bash
npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronAssistant/test/browser/positronAssistantConfigurationService.vitest.ts src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/positron/mainThreadAiFeatures.vitest.ts
```

Manual, following the issue's reproduction:

1. Launch Positron from a shell with a couple of local providers turned off or modify providers.json directly (access via command `Preferences: Open AI Provider Settings (JSON)`):

	```bash
	export POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED='{"providers":{"lmstudio":{"enabled":false},"ollama":{"enabled":false}}}'
	```

2. Command Palette -> `Positron Assistant: Configure Language Model Providers`.
3. Verify neither LM Studio nor Ollama is listed, matching how Anthropic already behaves.
4. Relaunch without the env var and confirm both are offered again.

title: Make the debug-e2e-test skill work on Windows
description:
Two Windows-only bugs in the `debug-e2e-test` skill, both in `resolve-test-key.js`.
Both are invisible in CI because CI runs on Linux, where neither reproduces.

Found while auditing the skill for Windows support (companion to #15589, which
does the same for `drive-positron`).

### 1. The front door did not open: `npx` could not be spawned

`listEntries()` ran `tryRun('npx', ['playwright', 'test', '--list', '--reporter=json'])`.
On Windows `npx` is a `.cmd` shim, and `execFileSync` will not spawn one:

```
npx        FAIL ENOENT   spawnSync npx ENOENT
npx.cmd    FAIL EINVAL   spawnSync npx.cmd EINVAL     <- the CVE-2024-27980 fix
npx +shell OK                                          <- deprecated in Node 24
git        OK  git version 2.47.0.windows.2
gh         OK  gh version 2.78.0
```

`git` and `gh` are `.exe`, so they were fine -- `npx` was the only casualty. But
listing the suite is the first thing test-key resolution does, so nothing worked.

Fixed by invoking Playwright's CLI through `process.execPath` and
`node_modules/playwright/cli.js`: no shell, no `.cmd`, and it guarantees the
checkout's own Playwright rather than whatever `npx` would resolve. `shell: true`
would also have worked, but it is deprecated in Node 24 (DEP0190) and unescaped,
and `tryRun` is shared with `git`/`gh` calls that pass dynamic arguments.

### 2. Backslashes were baked into the test key, silently

The key format is `testName|||specPath`, and `specPath` came from `path.relative`:

```
Console History > Python - ...|||test\e2e\tests\console\console-history.test.ts
```

The dashboard's keys are generated by CI on Linux and macOS with forward slashes,
so a key built on Windows matched nothing. The failure mode was the bad one: the
history query returned **no results rather than an error**, which reads as "this
test has no failure history" instead of "your key is malformed."

Fixed by normalizing where `specPath` enters a key, and reusing that helper for
the normalization `fileMatches` was already doing separately.

### 3. Doc corrections

Both entries run on Windows now, so the Requirements section no longer says
otherwise. The `unzip` dependency belongs to the `e2e-failure-analyzer` scripts
that deep escalation delegates to, not to anything in this skill -- SKILL.md
attributed it to "the CI entry," which read as though these scripts needed it.

### 4. Allowlisting the skill's JS files

Unrelated to the bugs, but it blocks the commit. The skill's 17 `.js` files are
tracked but were never added to `.eslint-allowed-javascript-files` when the skill
landed in #15363. `checkNoNewJavaScriptFiles` audits **every tracked JS file
repo-wide** as soon as any JS file is staged, so this blocked JS commits anywhere
in the repo, not just on this branch -- it just needed someone to stage a `.js` to
surface it. The sibling `e2e-failure-analyzer` scripts are already listed, so this
follows existing precedent rather than setting new policy.

Flagging for CODEOWNERS: this is a governance file. Happy to split it into its own
PR if you would rather review it in isolation.

### QA Notes

No product code changed, so there are no e2e tags on this PR.

Verified on Windows 11 / Git Bash against this checkout:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Skill unit tests | 115/115 pass (4 were failing before) |
| `node node_modules/playwright/cli.js test --list` | exit 0, 229 suites |
| `resolve-test-key.js` by spec path | forward-slash keys, candidate list correct |
| `resolve-test-key.js` by title | `resolved` non-null, forward-slash key |
| `triage-history.js` against the live dashboard | matched **482 runs on main** and returned real failure patterns |

That last row is the end-to-end proof for bug 2: a key built on Windows now
matches data keyed by CI.

The four fixed tests already encoded the correct forward-slash expectation, so
they were the spec -- they were simply red on Windows and green in CI.

title: Add a Disconnect option to the Data Connections context menu
description: Fixes #14623 ### Summary Adds a **Disconnect** option to the actions menu for a data connection in the Data Connections panel, reachable both from the `...` button and by right-clicking the row. Disconnecting closes the connection, closes any Data Explorers that were previewed from it, and collapses the row. Disconnect sits in the bottom group of the menu, alongside Remove. It appears only while the profile has a live connection. Before this, the only ways to close a connection were to collapse the row -- which intentionally defers the close while Data Explorers previewed from it are still open -- or to remove the profile outright, which is the gap the issue describes. ### Implementation notes `disconnect()` now closes the Data Explorers previewed from a connection, not just the connection itself. That teardown previously lived on the profile-removal path only, so a connection closed by any other route left its previews behind -- and their backends die with the connection, so a tab left open would show a grid that errors on the next scroll or filter. `disconnectWhenUnused()` is unchanged and remains the way to give up a connection *without* cutting those off -- that is what collapsing a row does, and it still waits for the last Data Explorer to close before the connection goes. Two ordering details inside `disconnect()` are load-bearing and commented as such: the instance leaves `_instances` before the `closeEditors()` await, so the `onDidCloseEditor` handler cannot re-enter and tear the same handle down twice; and a failure to close an editor is logged rather than propagated, so the handle is still released instead of leaking behind a row that shows a connection nothing can reach. ### Screenshot ### Release Notes #### New Features - Added a Disconnect option to the Data Connections context menu, which closes the connection and any Data Explorers opened from it (#14623) #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:connections @:data-explorer Unit coverage is in `dataConnectionEntryRow.vitest.tsx` (which entries the menu offers, and that only Remove is destructive), `dataConnectionsTreeInstance.vitest.ts` (disconnect closes the connection, collapses the row, and does not route through the deferred-close path), and `positronDataConnectionsService.vitest.ts` (the previews close and are forgotten, and a pending deferred close cannot cause a double teardown). Run them with: ``` npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronDataConnections/test/browser src/vs/workbench/services/positronDataConnections/test/browser ``` Manually, in the Data Connections panel: 1. Create and expand a connection (SQLite is the quickest), then double-click a table to open it in the Data Explorer. 2. Right-click the connection row -- or click its `...` button -- and choose **Disconnect**. 3. Verify the Data Explorer tab closes, the row collapses, and the green connected indicator disappears. 4. Re-expand the row and verify it reconnects and the tree repopulates. 5. Verify **Disconnect** is absent from the menu for a saved connection that is not currently connected, and that **Remove** is still the only red item and still prompts for confirmation. Then confirm collapsing still behaves as before: 6. Expand a connection, open a table in the Data Explorer, then collapse the row. 7. Verify the connected indicator stays lit and the Data Explorer keeps working (scroll it, apply a filter). 8. Close that Data Explorer tab and verify the connection then closes on its own.

title: Quarto virtual notebook: replace only the cells that changed
description:
Related to:

- #14540
- #15415 and particularly https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15415#discussion_r3752702171


Positron core keeps a hidden in-memory notebook for each open Quarto document, with one cell text model per code chunk. Until now, any structural change to a document threw away every cell and rebuilt it. Insert one chunk into a 45 chunk document, and every language server that watches those cells saw 45 closes and 46 opens. Each one then re-indexed what it had just dropped.

This PR makes the sync incremental. The diff matches old cells to new ones from both ends of the document. It compares language and code, and replaces only the changed run. Every other cell keeps its handle, its URI, and its extension host document. An inserted chunk now creates one cell instead of N.

A few things about the approach you might want to know before you read the diff:

- **Cell IDs cannot do this job, although it might look like they can.** `QuartoCodeCell.id` is built as `"{index}-{hash8}-{label}"`, so it changes when the content changes, and when anything above it is inserted. That is exactly the set of edits the match has to survive. A match on the ID marks every cell below an insertion point as removed and added. That is the full rebuild this PR removes.

- **A same-shape check runs before the diff, and it is load-bearing.** `diffCellRuns` has no notion of position. A cell edited in place therefore looks identical to one cell removed and a different one inserted at the same index. Without the guard, one character typed in a chunk disposes that cell's text model and creates a new one. That happens on every keystroke. When the cell count and the language at every index are unchanged, the old in-place path still runs. This guard is the negation of the `structureChanged` check that this file already had.

- **Line endings made this a no-op on Windows.** `getCellCode` always joins lines with LF (`quartoDocumentModel.ts:186`), but a text model's own end-of-line is platform dependent. `DEFAULT_EOL` is CRLF on Windows (`modelService.ts:69`), and the buffer builder returns that default when the content has no line break at all. So a chunk that is a single line when its model is created gets a CRLF model on Windows. When the user adds a second line, `applyEdits` normalizes the new text to the buffer end-of-line, and `getValue()` returns CRLF text against an LF comparison string, permanently. Both comparison sites now read with `EndOfLinePreference.LF`. Without this, `sameCell` never matches such a cell, so every structural edit replaces it, and the feature does nothing on Windows while it looks correct everywhere else. Half of this is pre-existing: the old `_sync` compared the same way, so it already rewrote those cells on every parse. This PR adds a second and more consequential use of the same comparison, which is what turns a small waste into a silent no-op.


### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

Nothing here is user visible yet. The whole feature is still behind `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native`, which defaults to off.

### Validation Steps

@:quarto @:r-markdown

The e2e suites are regression cover only. The setting defaults to off, so none of this code runs in them.

The unit tests check the behavior: 13 new cases, and 298 green across the new feature here.

- `quartoCellDiff.vitest.ts`: 7 cases over the splice arithmetic. These include chunks with identical content, and a cell whose text model is gone.
- `quartoVirtualNotebookService.vitest.ts`: 4 cases that assert handles, URIs, and text models survive an append, a middle insert, a delete, and a language change.
- The same file adds a 75 step seeded fuzz test. It compares the service's cells against the document model's own parsed state.
- The same file adds one regression test for the disposal window described below.
- The pre-existing churn test passes unedited. That is the evidence that the splice behaves the same as the rebuild it replaces! 🤞 

No unit test can show the _improvement_ though. Core reports each structural change at trace level, so you can read it in the Window output channel:

```
[QuartoVirtualNotebook] doc.qmd: spliced at 2, removed 0, inserted 1, kept 45
```

1. Set `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native` to `true`, and `positron.logLevel` to `trace`.
2. Open a Quarto document with many chunks, and start an R session.
3. Filter the Window output channel to `QuartoVirtualNotebook`.
4. Insert a new chunk in the middle, not at the end. An append is the one shape that can pass by accident.
5. Expect `inserted 1`, `removed 0`, and a `kept` count equal to the chunks that were already there. `kept` is the claim this PR makes, stated per edit.
6. Type inside an existing chunk. Expect no line at all. A content-only edit takes the in-place path and never splices.
7. Delete a chunk from the middle. Expect `removed 1, inserted 0`.
8. Make sure that the Outline still lists every chunk's symbols. A mis-spliced cell appears there as a chunk with missing or doubled symbols.

If you want protocol-level evidence, set `positron.r.trace.server` to `messages` and filter the R Language Server channel for `vscode-notebook-cell`. Those URIs come only from this path, so they are distinguishable from the Quarto extension's virtual document traffic. However, this is VERY VERY BUSY and I found it hard to parse.

You might want to revisit the 45 chunk repro from #14512, inserting a chunk mid-document:

```
[QuartoVirtualNotebook] positron-outline-demo.qmd: spliced at 24, removed 0, inserted 1, kept 45
```

Position 24 of 45 is mid-document, so this is not the append case that can pass by accident. Nothing was disposed, one cell was created, and all 45 existing cells kept their handle, their URI, and their extension host document. The same edit before this change disposed 45 cells and created 46.

### Known and deferred

`_spliceCells` composes the final `_cells` from a snapshot taken before `applyEdits` and `createModel`, both of which fire their events inline. A listener woken by either one that re-enters `ensureSynchronized` sees a short `_cells`, repairs it, and then has that repair overwritten. No synchronous path from a model or notebook event into that method exists today: the callers in `quartoEmbeddedLanguageFeatures.ts` are ext-host driven and async. Recorded rather than guarded, because a structural change to this function carries more risk than the latent fault.

title: Use lazy useState initializers for configuration reads
description:
Addresses the Positron side of #15427. The core fix, which caches the policy-overlaid configuration model, is going to land in vscode-server and will reach Positron through an upstream merge.

### Summary

React evaluates an eager `useState` argument on every render and discards the result after mount. Components that read configuration this way repeat the read on every render for nothing. When any policy is active, each configuration read deep-clones the settings tree (#15427), and `VerticalSplitter` renders per visible Data Explorer cell and header, so one frame did hundreds of reads.

This PR:

- Converts the three configuration-reading `useState` initializers in `VerticalSplitter` to lazy initializers. The existing configuration-change subscription still updates the widths, so behavior does not change.
- Applies the same one-line fix to four components found in an audit of where else we might be doing the same thing: the console instance (font info), the console action bar and console tab (resource monitor setting), and the Quarto inline data explorer (maximum height). Each one already subscribes to configuration changes.
- Adds `verticalSplitter.vitest.tsx` with four tests: widths at mount for both variants, width updates when the sash size setting changes, and no configuration reads on re-render.

One note on guardrails here is that I would like lint protection against this pattern, but we do not have it yet. I tried drafting a custom eslint rule and then reverted it, because this repository treats eslint warnings as fatal in CI and precommit, so the rule cannot land before the remaining violations are fixed (an audit found about 28 more sites), and review found autofix edge cases to correct first. I think my preference would be to fix the remaining sites, harden the rule and its autofix, and land the rule at error.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Improve Data Explorer scrolling performance when a policy or an enforced setting is active (#15427)

### Validation Steps

@:data-explorer @:console @:variables @:quarto

1. Run `npx vitest run src/vs/base/browser/ui/positronComponents/splitters/test/verticalSplitter.vitest.tsx` and make sure that all four tests pass.
2. Open a data frame, preferably with many columns (wide). Drag the column boundaries, hover a boundary to show the sash indicator, and collapse and expand the summary panel splitter.
3. With the Data Explorer open, change the `workbench.sash.size` setting. Make sure that the splitter thickness updates without a reload.
4. With a console open, toggle the `console.showResourceMonitor` setting. Make sure that the console action bar and the console tab react immediately.
5. Performance check, only reproducible when a policy is active (for example, stale cached account policy data or enforced settings): scrolling a wide data frame is smooth, and a DevTools performance trace no longer shows dominant `deepClone` time.

title: Make the drive-positron skill work on Windows
description:
The `drive-positron` skill could not launch Positron at all on Windows. Git Bash
ships neither `rsync` nor `pgrep`, and the skill used both. Everything downstream
of the launch (`@playwright/cli` attach, snapshot, eval, press, screenshot) already
worked -- only launching and cleaning up were broken.

Found while verifying an unrelated build change on Windows.

### What changed

**`scripts/launch.sh`**

- Replace the three `rsync` calls with a `copy_tree` helper. `rsync` is still used
  where it exists, so macOS and Linux behavior is unchanged; Windows falls back to
  a streaming `tar` pipe. The tar path skips excluded directories rather than
  copying and then deleting them, which matters because the excluded caches can run
  to gigabytes. Exclude patterns keep rsync semantics, so a leading slash still
  anchors at the transfer root.
- Convert the profile paths to native form for the Electron binary. The app cannot
  read MSYS paths, and MSYS argument translation does not reliably rewrite them
  inside `--flag=value` pairs.

**`scripts/stop.sh`** (new)

`kill $PID` is not sufficient on Windows: the PID `launch.sh` reports belongs to the
MSYS shell that `exec`'d the native binary, so killing it can leave the application
running and holding several gigabytes -- the exact outcome the cleanup section
exists to prevent. This was reproduced, not theorized.

`stop.sh` finds the process tree that owns the CDP port, which works on every
platform, waits for the port to stop answering, and exits non-zero if the instance
survives. It removes the run directory only when the path contains a generated
`positron-dev-launch` component.

**`SKILL.md`**

- Add a platform-support section listing the tools each script needs.
- Point cleanup at `stop.sh` and explain why the bare `kill` is insufficient.
- Replace the `pgrep` liveness check with a CDP probe that works everywhere.
- Give the Windows form of `--folder-uri`, built with `cygpath`.
- Note that the 103-character IPC path limit is macOS and Linux only.

### QA Notes

No product code changed, so there are no e2e tags on this PR.

Verified on Windows 11 / Git Bash against a dev build (Electron 42.6.0,
code-oss-dev 1.130.0), running the documented workflow end to end:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `launch.sh` | slim copy (tar), CDP ready in 2s, JSON emitted |
| `--folder-uri` via `cygpath` | workspace opened (`myworkspace - Positron Dev`) |
| attach + snapshot | 210 element refs |
| `stop.sh` | killed the PID tree, port dead, run directory removed, exit 0 |
| after cleanup | zero `Positron.exe` processes, zero run directories |

The macOS and Linux `rsync` path is unchanged and was not re-tested; a spot check
there before merge would be welcome.

Not fixed here: `monaco-paste.sh` clears the target editor but fails to insert, so
it reports a read-back mismatch. A wrong-element selector, a focus problem, and a
missing `jq` were all ruled out; the likely cause is Monaco's EditContext input path
no longer honoring a synthetic untrusted `ClipboardEvent`, which would make it a
general regression rather than a Windows one. Left out deliberately since it cannot
be attributed from Windows alone.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

title: Quarto virtual notebook: expose cell symbols as a command
description:
Related to:

- #14540
- #15486

With this PR Positron can now answer "which symbols are in this Quarto document's code cells" through a command. The Quarto extension will call this command instead of writing a temporary file for each code cell.

The change has three parts:

- `provideQuartoCellSymbols()` is a new exported function. It returns the symbols grouped by the cell they came from. The cell walk that #15486 put inside `QuartoEmbeddedDocumentSymbolProvider` moved into this function, and the provider is now a flatten over it.
- `_executeQuartoCellSymbolProvider` is a new internal command over that function.
- `positron.executeQuartoCellSymbolProvider` is the extension-facing command. It converts the core types to `vscode` types.

**Why the result is grouped by cell.** The Outline shows one group for each document symbol provider. #15486 added a second provider, so the Outline now shows a flat list of code symbols beside the Quarto extension's nested tree. The fix is for the extension to keep its own tree and ask Positron for the contents, because only the extension knows which heading a chunk sits under. A later PR will remove the provider registration in Positron, and the Outline becomes a single nested tree again.

**Nothing calls the new command yet.** The consumer is a PR in the `quarto-dev/quarto` repository. This PR is additive on purpose, so it can land first and give that work something real to build against.

**The Outline does not change in this PR.** It still shows two groups.

### Notes for reviewers

- **`provideQuartoCellSymbols` awaits `whenReady()` before it reads the cells.** Notebook creation is asynchronous, and `ensureSynchronized` does nothing while creation is in flight, so a request that arrives early used to get no cells. The Outline hid this, because a language server that registers its provider makes the Outline recompute. The command's consumer has no such hook, so it needed the wait. A test covers it, and that test fails when the `await` is removed.
- **One malformed symbol no longer discards the rest.** `types.DocumentSymbol` validates in its constructor and throws on an empty name, or on a `selectionRange` that its `range` does not contain. The core type does not validate, and the symbols come from third-party language servers. The converter now handles each symbol separately, so a bad symbol costs only itself.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:quarto @:outline

This PR changes nothing that a user can see, so those suites are regression guards for the Outline and the Quarto features that share this code.

In terms of what will ship, the manual validation is that everything is the same as what you can see https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15486.

If you want to manually verify the command yourself, temporarily register is as something that, say, the R extension can call and send the output to the Developer Tools console. You can then verify that you see output like:

```
[Extension Host] [CellSymbolProbe] on first activation of /Users/juliasilge/Work/posit/scratch/quarto_basic.qmd
    returned 2 cell(s)
    cell lines 8-16 (0-based; add 1 for editor line numbers), 1 symbol(s)
      smaller kind=12 (Variable) detail="" line=13 sel=13
    cell lines 36-42 (0-based; add 1 for editor line numbers), 2 symbol(s)
      mod kind=12 (Variable) detail="" line=38 sel=38
      my_func kind=11 (Function) detail="function(x)" line=40 sel=40
```

title: Add a Workbench (Rocky Linux 9) option to the full-suite workflow
description:
The `@:workbench-rocky` lane (Workbench e2e against a Rocky Linux 9 container) is
wired into `test-pull-request.yml` but there was no way to start it from
**Test: Full Suite**. This adds it:

- a new `run_e2e_workbench_rocky` input, "E2E Tests / Workbench (Rocky Linux 9)",
  defaulting to `false` like the other secondary OS lanes;
- an `e2e-workbench-rocky` job that reuses the same `build-workbench` artifact as
  the Ubuntu lanes (both OSes consume the one `vscode-reh-web-pwb-linux-x64`
  tarball), with `os: rocky9` and `display_name: "workbench-rocky"`;
- `build-workbench` now also runs when only the Rocky box is checked, and the job
  is added to `slack-notify`'s `needs`.

As in the PR workflow, `grep` is pinned to `@:workbench` rather than the run's
`grep` input: `@:workbench-rocky` selects the lane, never individual tests, so no
test carries that tag. The reusable workflow already restricts the Rocky lane to
the `default` shard, so this adds one job, not four.

### Doubling as a verification run

This PR is tagged `@:workbench-rocky`, which also gives us a signal we want
independently of the workflow change.

Until now the Rocky lane had exactly one known failure: the Python case of
`workbench/environment-modules`, filed as #15509 (positron-python probes a
module-provided interpreter as a bare `python`, which does not exist on EL9, so
the bundled ipykernel is disabled and the session dies on a misleading
"sqlite3 extension is required" error). #14746 is the same probe gap described
from the other end: the pre-launch validation probes never apply the module
activation that Positron computes for the session.

#15501 ("Set up module environment in Positron terminals in addition to
consoles") landed since that lane last ran and touched the module locator and
activation plumbing, so the expectation is that the Python environment-modules
test now passes on Rocky. The Rocky lane on this PR runs the PR's Positron build
inside Workbench, so a green `workbench-rocky (default)` here is direct evidence
that #14746 / #15509 are fixed, and a red one tells us the probe path is still
broken. If it is green, the follow-up is to close those issues and update the
"one expected failure" note in `docker/environments/wb-local/ROCKY-PLAN.md`.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### QA Notes

CI-only change; nothing user-facing. Two things to look at:

1. The `workbench-rocky (default)` job on this PR, per the section above.
2. After merge, **Test: Full Suite** should show the new "E2E Tests / Workbench
   (Rocky Linux 9)" checkbox, and checking it alone should schedule
   `build-workbench` followed by one `workbench-rocky (default)` job.

title: Clear webview view badge when set to undefined
description:
Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15567

This is an internal, non-fork PR to get the change from #15567 ready to go, so that CI can run out as outlined in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/6628.

title: Clear webview view badge when set to undefined
description:
`WebviewViewPane.updateBadge` registers the view activity (the numeric badge on the view container) when a badge is assigned, but never disposes it when the badge is set back to `undefined`. The badge therefore stays visible on the activity bar after the extension has cleared it.

The tree view badge setter in `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/views/treeView.ts` handles this correctly with an `else { this._activity.clear(); }` branch; the webview view pane is simply missing the equivalent.

Discovered while implementing a needs-input badge in Posit Assistant (posit-dev/assistant#2094): extension-side logging confirmed `webviewView.badge = undefined` was assigned, yet the badge remained visible.

## Notes

- The same omission exists upstream in microsoft/vscode's `webviewViewPane.ts`; which I upstreamed at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331019
- Manual verification: assign a badge to a webview view via `webviewView.badge = { value: 1, tooltip: '...' }`, then set `webviewView.badge = undefined` — before this change the badge persists; after, it clears.
